rows.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

rows.anchor: Adopting the receipt as authoritative state would supply limb one of the estate's existence test. A decision framed as constitutive would decide existence by the back door -- which this act forbids. Framed as a boundary specification, it does not.
rows.statement: A distinction between a 'constitutive' decision (which would establish existence as a side effect) and a 'boundary specification' decision (which defines a candidate scope without establishing existence) is drawn, warning that D3 must be framed as the latter to avoid silently satisfying the D2 existence test.

rows.anchor: C -- SPLIT. Fits every decided constraint. It matches OQ-J's 2-of-5 result ... applicability / transport / execution are already owned or already excluded
rows.statement: Recommendation: Option C (SPLIT) for D3 -- C-10 would own only the receipt/attestation lifecycle and state (receipt identity, lifecycle state, invalidation, completeness), explicitly excluding applicability determination, delivery transport, session execution, identity binding, dispute adjudication, execution authority, and compliance/application.

rows.anchor: Selecting HALT or BLOCK for any tier decides the category by consequence. ... the exact back-door structure D3's non-constitutive clause was created to prevent.
rows.statement: Selecting an enforcing response (HALT or BLOCK) for any missing-knowledge condition would convert C-10 into a control-plane capability by consequence (per the canonical analysis's own control-plane test: control-plane if it gates START), the same back-door category-deciding risk D3's non-constitutive clause was designed to prevent.

rows.anchor: D2: C-10 is NOT YET ESTABLISHED. No receipt activity is realized. Therefore ZERO receipts exist. Every session, for every required context version, is in state Missing. ... Tier-1 HALT on Missing is not strict -- it is total.
rows.statement: Decisive practical-arithmetic finding: because D2 established C-10 as NOT YET ESTABLISHED, zero receipts currently exist, so every governed act is currently in the Missing-receipt condition -- meaning any blocking/halting response to Missing would halt the entire estate on the day it is enabled, not selectively.

rows.anchor: F -- Compensating Control ... describes what the estate already does deliberately ... the recorded human START act is a compensating control -- a human authorization substituting for absent machine enforcement.
rows.statement: A 'compensating control' option is elevated from underrated fallback to preferred transition mechanism, on the observation that the estate's own recorded human START act is already, in practice, a compensating control -- a human authorization substituting for absent machine enforcement, evidenced by seq 25 and seq 27 elsewhere in the batch.

rows.anchor: E is not merely too weak -- it is the falsified status quo. ... E is not an untested option. It is the option currently in force, and it produced the defects this work item is adjudicating.
rows.statement: Option E ('session responsible', i.e. evidence recorded but nothing enforced) is argued to be empirically falsified rather than merely weak: it is the estate's actual current behaviour and is cited as the direct cause of the same-day EKS-01 distribution failure, the missing-START off-record-execution pattern, and the false identity-attestation claim.

rows.anchor: A receipt's D1 claim is a time-stamped historical fact, so it never becomes FALSE -- only INSUFFICIENT or UNRELIED-UPON. ... STALE, SUPERSEDED and INVALIDATED do not contradict the receipt; they change what it is sufficient FOR.
rows.statement: A structural finding cutting across all five condition types: since a C-10 receipt's claim is a time-stamped historical fact, it never becomes false; later conditions like STALE, SUPERSEDED, or INVALIDATED change what the receipt remains sufficient for, not whether the original claim held.

rows.anchor: DISPUTED is ORTHOGONAL to the lifecycle, not a state in it. ... a receipt can be SUPERSEDED and DISPUTED simultaneously
rows.statement: DISPUTED is reclassified as an orthogonal flag over the receipt lifecycle rather than a terminal state within a linear chain, since a receipt can simultaneously be SUPERSEDED and DISPUTED -- a defect noted in an earlier candidate lifecycle chain that D3 had deliberately left unfinalized.

lineage_claims.target: D3.5's candidate lifecycle chain (ISSUED -> VALID -> SUPERSEDED -> INVALIDATED -> EXPIRED/DISPUTED)
lineage_claims.quote: Recorded as a defect in D3.5's candidate chain -- which D3 expressly did not finalize.

rows.anchor: M4 must be classified NOT ATTESTED -- never MISSING. ... Calling it MISSING asserts "no receipt", which the evidence does not support. Calling it present asserts a binding the platform cannot make.
rows.statement: Extension of the NOT-ATTESTED-never-PASS discipline to condition classification: a receipt that exists but cannot be bound to its executing session (M4) must be classified NOT ATTESTED, since calling it MISSING or VALID would each assert something the platform cannot establish.
invariants: a failure to establish binding must remain unresolved rather than converted into either 'no receipt' or 'valid receipt'

rows.anchor: ca6039a8 was reclassified as HISTORICAL EVIDENCE + NOT INDEPENDENT/PROVENANCE-CONFLICTED -- not deleted, findings intact, only its ASSURANCE STATUS refused. That is exactly the shape of receipt invalidation ... invalidation is PURPOSE-SCOPED, not global.
rows.statement: The earlier reclassification of the AMD2 verification artifact (ca6039a8) as historical-but-not-independent is offered as a real, worked instance of what 'receipt invalidation' should look like: invalidation is purpose-scoped (it removes assurance standing while leaving the content usable as evidence), not a global deletion.

rows.anchor: Every condition and sub-condition proposes NO ENFORCEMENT RESPONSE YET. Zero enforceable mappings are justified. This is not an evasion
rows.statement: Testing all nine condition rows (M1-M5, STALE, SUPERSEDED, INVALIDATED, DISPUTED) against four required prerequisites (semantically defined, authoritative trigger, identifiable evidence source, currently detectable), no row satisfies all four, so no enforceable mapping is proposed for any condition -- SUPERSEDED comes closest since its authority exists at BC-1, but its mechanism (CAP-03) is unbuilt.

rows.anchor: raising a dispute needs far less evidence than resolving one. If a dispute suspends use, then an unqualified right to raise lets any party suspend any receipt indefinitely ... The effect and the "who may raise" gate must be decided together.
rows.statement: A denial-of-service risk is identified for a proposed DISPUTED effect (suspending a receipt's use for the disputed claim only): since raising a dispute needs far less evidence than resolving one, and no adjudicator exists, adopting the suspending effect alone would let any party indefinitely suspend any receipt -- the effect and the 'who may raise' gate must be decided together.

rows.anchor: M1 is effectively universal ... a WARN on every governed act would be noise, not notification -- degrading the floor's value. INFO + RECORD is the proportionate baseline
rows.statement: A proportionality argument (proposed, not decided) recommends INFO+RECORD rather than WARN as the floor response while zero receipts exist, on the ground that a universal WARN degrades into noise rather than useful notification -- this proposal is later NOT adopted by the D4.3 decision (S0120), which leaves M1 fully OPEN instead.

rows.anchor: C - FUTURE / ARCHITECTURAL ... an adopted invariant that has never been exercised ... MUST NOT establish existence by themselves. ... D1 is Class C -- an adopted semantic never exercised.
rows.statement: A third evidence class ('Class C: future/architectural') is formalised alongside realization and boundary evidence: proposed schemas, planned stores, future enforcement, and an adopted-but-never-exercised invariant must never by themselves establish capability existence -- and this class formally re-classifies D1 (a decided but never-performed receipt semantic) as contributing zero to C-10's establishment, correcting the earlier D2-prep's treatment of D1 as existence evidence.
invariants: adopted-but-unexercised invariants do not establish capability existence

lineage_claims.target: the D2 decision-prep's treatment of D1 as existence evidence
lineage_claims.quote: the D2 prep treated D1 as existence evidence; the register already corrected that at D2 section 3. Class C makes the correction structural rather than case-by-case.

rows.anchor: Do not import C-5's existence test automatically. Do not assume 'adopted invariant + performed capability' is a universal rule.
rows.statement: The two-limb existence test derived from C-5's evidence (adopted invariant + performed capability) is explicitly declared not a universal rule to be imported automatically for other capabilities; C-10 must construct its own establishment test rather than inherit C-5's.

rows.anchor: The revisit trigger has a trigger-ownership problem. D4.3 established monitoring is owned by nobody, so a condition requiring an observer will never fire. It must be SELF-EVIDENCING
rows.statement: A design constraint on any D2-revisit trigger: because monitoring/invalidation ownership is nobody's, a trigger that depends on a dedicated unowned observer will never fire; the trigger must instead be self-evidencing, piggybacked on an already-mandatory read.

rows.anchor: the commission's section 2 list -- GOVERNED / OBSERVED / REPRODUCIBLE / INDEPENDENT -- is not one scheme. It mixes a PROVENANCE value, an EPISTEMIC value and two proposed properties of the OBSERVATION METHOD.
rows.statement: A model-integrity flag is raised: the commission's own evidence-scheme list (GOVERNED, OBSERVED, REPRODUCIBLE, INDEPENDENT) conflates three distinct existing evidence schemes (subject/what-it's-about, epistemic/how-well-known, provenance/whose-artifact) with two newly proposed method-properties; whether REPRODUCIBLE/INDEPENDENT are orthogonal new dimensions, overloaded existing ones, or merely new values must be argued explicitly, per the estate's own model-integrity rule (orthogonal AND necessary AND sufficient).
invariants: a new evidence dimension is admissible only if orthogonal AND necessary AND sufficient

rows.anchor: INDEPENDENT is C-5's subject matter, not an evidence class. ... making INDEPENDENT necessary for C-10 establishment would make C-10 unestablishable for reasons that have nothing to do with C-10 ... REPRODUCIBLE does the work INDEPENDENT was reaching for.
rows.statement: A candidate INDEPENDENT evidence dimension is refused for C-10's establishment model because it is C-5's own subject matter (whose organizational independence is itself NOT_ESTABLISHED and cannot be currently supplied), which would make C-10 unestablishable for reasons unrelated to C-10; REPRODUCIBLE (can anyone re-derive the observation?) is adopted instead as doing the same protective work without importing an unresolved capability's unresolved state.

rows.anchor: an observer who notices the trigger but holds no authority to reopen D2 does not close the loop. ... Detection is never automatic revision: registering the detection does not change D2.
rows.statement: A four-field self-evidencing D2-revisit trigger is defined (observable event, evidence source, observation path, authority path), with the authority path split into a duty (Governance must register the detection) and a reservation (only PO/ARB may decide to revisit D2) -- detecting a trigger is never itself a decision.
invariants: detection is a duty; revision is a reserved decision

rows.anchor: reference != ownership, recording != asserting, correlation != authority. ... external correlation reference -- recorded only, not attested, not owned by C-10
rows.statement: An anti-corruption rule is stated for C-10's ubiquitous language: reference != ownership, recording != asserting, correlation != authority; a new neutral term 'external correlation reference' is introduced to avoid importing BC-1's vocabulary into C-10's receipt.

rows.anchor: The Option C label now denotes two different propositions. ... The labels are not merely colliding -- they are CROSSED. ... a future instruction "adopt Option C" is UNRESOLVABLE on the record. Any selection must therefore be recorded by its PROPOSITION TEXT, not by its letter.
rows.statement: Finding S-1: the label 'Option C' has been used for two incompatible propositions across two PO/ARB acts on the same D1 decision slot, so citing it by letter is unresolvable; the recommended fix is that any selection must be recorded by full proposition text, never by option letter.

rows.anchor: The referent gap is caused by the reference being REQUIRED, not by its being recorded. P3 is the only proposition that makes it OPTIONAL and NON-AUTHORITATIVE -- dissolving the gap while keeping traceability.
rows.statement: The decisive structural insight resolving the D1 referent-gap conflict: the gap exists because the applicability reference was a REQUIRED receipt property, not because it was recorded at all; making the reference OPTIONAL (Proposition 3) dissolves the gap while preserving traceability, without contradicting D3.2's 'MAY record references' rule.

rows.anchor: CORRECTION: the D5 provenance finding is SUPERSEDED BY EVENTS. ... 10fbfb05 delivered KOS-AIP04-C10-D5-ESTABLISHMENT-CRITERIA-PROPOSAL.md, 300 lines ... The finding is not withdrawn -- it was accurate at the time
rows.statement: Self-correction: an earlier register entry stating 'no D5 analysis artifact exists' was true when measured but has since been superseded by the delivery of the D5 Establishment Criteria proposal, and the correction is recorded additively rather than as a retraction of a false statement.

lineage_claims.target: an earlier register statement 'no D5 analysis artifact exists'
lineage_claims.quote: The finding is not withdrawn -- it was accurate at the time and the commission gap it recorded was real. It is superseded

rows.anchor: two residues no selection resolves ... knowledge versions K ... all three new propositions are silent on it ... S is unattestable. INV-ATTR-1 -- no gate reads identity ... E2 must mark the session-execution reference RECORDED, NOT ATTESTED.
rows.statement: Two residues survive any D1 selection unresolved: whether 'knowledge versions K' remains a required receipt property (silently dropped by all three new propositions), and that the session-execution reference S must be marked RECORDED-NOT-ATTESTED per INV-ATTR-1/D4.3's M4 finding, both flagged for E2 (receipt completeness) to settle.

rows.anchor: NOT YET ESTABLISHED ... I recommended YES. The PO/ARB decided NOT YET ESTABLISHED. The decision is right and my recommendation was wrong on the estate's own established test
rows.statement: PO/ARB decides C-10 = NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and Governance's own YES recommendation is retracted as methodologically wrong for treating a decided claim-boundary semantic (D1) as equivalent to a performed capability, when the estate's own two-limb existence test requires both an adopted invariant AND a performed instance -- C-10 satisfies neither.

lineage_claims.target: its own D2 decision-prep recommendation of YES
lineage_claims.quote: The decision is right and my recommendation was wrong on the estate's own established test

rows.anchor: NOT YET ESTABLISHED is not NO. ... This decision does not reject the C-10 capability hypothesis; it records that its operational existence has not yet been demonstrated.
rows.statement: An explicit distinction is stated and repeatedly reinforced: 'NOT YET ESTABLISHED' is not equivalent to 'NO' -- the C-10 capability hypothesis is not rejected, only its current operational demonstration status is fixed.

rows.anchor: DECIDED -- OPTION C / SPLIT. C-10's candidate boundary is the receipt / acknowledgement lifecycle. This decision does NOT establish that C-10 currently exists. candidate capability boundary != capability existence != capability realization
rows.statement: D3 decides C-10's candidate boundary as the receipt/acknowledgement lifecycle (receipt identity, lifecycle state, version/supersession invalidation, completeness), explicitly excluding applicability determination, delivery transport, session execution, identity attestation/binding, dispute adjudication, execution authority, application and compliance -- with a critical non-constitutive clause distinguishing candidate capability boundary, capability existence, and capability realization as three separate things.

rows.anchor: recording session identity != attesting session identity ... recording an applicability reference != attesting correctness of applicability
rows.statement: D3 formalises two non-equivalences carrying the decision: recording session identity is not attesting session identity, and recording an applicability reference is not attesting the correctness of applicability -- the platform cannot attest 'a specified session execution' (INV-ATTR-1/2), so identity binding is placed outside C-10's boundary entirely.

rows.anchor: DECIDED -- RISK / CONTEXT-PROPORTIONATE ENFORCEMENT ... INFO, WARN, BLOCK, HALT + ESCALATE ... A compensating control MUST NOT convert NOT ATTESTED into PROVEN or COMPLIANT.
rows.statement: D4.1 decides the enforcement principle (risk/context-proportionate) and a four-value effect vocabulary (INFO, WARN, BLOCK, HALT+ESCALATE), and demotes 'compensating control' from a candidate fifth effect to an exception mechanism with its own preservation duties, with the critical constraint that a compensating control must never convert NOT ATTESTED into PROVEN or COMPLIANT.
invariants: a compensating control must not convert NOT ATTESTED into PROVEN or COMPLIANT

rows.anchor: D4.1 defines the permitted effect VOCABULARY; D4 defines the currently ENABLED SET. Vocabulary != enabled set. ... INFO / WARN + RECORD is the maximum generally applicable C-10 response. No BLOCK or HALT behaviour is enabled by this decision.
rows.statement: D4 distinguishes the legal effect vocabulary (fixed by D4.1) from the currently enabled effect set: BLOCK and HALT+ESCALATE remain legal effects but are not enabled by any current mapping; the maximum currently enabled response is INFO/WARN + RECORD, and tier semantics (e.g. Tier-1/Tier-2 labels) are explicitly retired from this decision and left to Architecture.

rows.anchor: PARTIALLY DECIDED ... M4 = NOT ATTESTED, never MISSING ... All other mappings OPEN ... criterion 5 is new and load-bearing. ... it independently excludes M5 (BC-1's condition) and M3 (infrastructure)
rows.statement: D4.3 decides only one mapping (M4 = NOT ATTESTED, bidirectionally barred from being read as either MISSING or VALID) and leaves all others OPEN, adding a fifth prerequisite (the response must be within C-10's authorized boundary) to the earlier four-prerequisite test, which formally excludes M5 (BC-1's condition) and M3 (infrastructure) from C-10's mapping authority.

rows.anchor: D2 premature existence claims. D3 ownership overreach. D4 enforcement overreach. D5 criteria PROVENANCE overreach. ... The correction is not a setback. It is exactly the type of governance boundary C-10 was designed to expose.
rows.statement: A through-line is recorded across the C-10 decision sequence: each decision (D2, D3, D4, D5) is characterised as preventing a distinct kind of overreach (premature existence, ownership overreach, enforcement overreach, criteria-provenance overreach), framing the recurring corrections as the governance discipline working as designed rather than as failures.

rows.anchor: SELECTED: A C-10 receipt claims that governed knowledge delivery occurred and acknowledgement was recorded ... a receipt EVIDENCES; it does not PROVE ... this is the estate's recording != asserting discipline written into the language itself ... acknowledgement WAS RECORDED
rows.statement: The final D1 consolidation selects a receipt-claim proposition using 'claims'/'records evidence of' rather than 'proves', and 'acknowledgement was recorded' (a fact about the record) rather than 'acknowledgement occurred' (a fact about the world) -- moving the receipt's authoritative claim entirely onto ground the platform can actually hold, and making 'identity binding was established' an explicit non-claim.

lineage_claims.target: Act A's proposition (a0b61305) and the offered Proposition 3
lineage_claims.quote: its PROPOSITION is SUPERSEDED -- the selected text carries neither 'containing knowledge versions K' nor 'under applicability decision A'. The record is RETAINED AS HISTORICAL, unaltered.

rows.anchor: Option A is unsatisfiable ... the full conjunction includes E10, and E10 requires a history that cannot exist at establishment ... One instance establishes L1, and L1 is not C-10
rows.statement: Argues that requiring the full conjunction of ten establishment criteria (including E10, repeatability across operational history) at the moment of establishment is structurally unsatisfiable, and recommends a three-assurance-level model (Option C) where a single instance establishes only L1, not full C-10 capability existence.

rows.anchor: GOVERNED / OBSERVED / REPRODUCIBLE / INDEPENDENT is not one scheme. It mixes a provenance value, an epistemic value, and two properties of the observation method.
rows.statement: Reconciles an evidence-model list that conflated four different kinds of properties into four orthogonal dimensions (SUBJECT, EPISTEMIC, PROVENANCE, REPRODUCIBILITY), adding REPRODUCIBLE as a needed dimension and explicitly refusing to add INDEPENDENT because it would import C-5's own unresolved, unachievable-in-a-single-operator-estate test.

rows.anchor: the common failure is: approved decision exists but execution context does not contain it. This is a distribution failure, not merely a retrieval failure.
rows.statement: Distinguishes knowledge creation/publication/selection/retrieval/context-assembly/session-bootstrap/runtime-verification/enforcement as separate stages, and names 'published = delivered = applied' as a false equivalence that external agent-context architecture explicitly rejects.

rows.anchor: The four unowned capabilities (corrected state)
rows.statement: Records four capabilities with no bounded-context owner as one control loop (policy/knowledge DEFINED in BC-1 -> C-10 DELIVERS -> C-14 GATES -> C-19 EXPRESSES <- C-5 ATTESTS): C-5 Separation attestation (existence YES, cross-context control-plane assurance capability, NOT a bounded context); C-10 Knowledge distribution (existence NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred); C-14 Policy enforcement (existence CONTESTED, deferred); C-19 Communication composition (existence YES, stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern, NOT a bounded context). Flagged as a proposal finding, not adopted architecture; C-10/C-14 existence remain UNDECIDED.

lexical.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.

formal.anchor: Distinguish, explicitly: ContextPublished, ContextSelected, ContextDelivered, ContextAvailable, ContextAcknowledged, ContextApplied, ContextVerified. Receipt is not proof of application or compliance.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.
rationale_evidence.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

rationale_evidence.anchor: EKS-01: the HANDOFF token's tokenRef acted as the de-facto knowledge channel and taught a lane the superseded path. A lane was taught the old path by its workflow record's tokenRef.
rationale_evidence.statement: Finding F-5/F-5a: BC-7's HANDOFF tokenRef is performing de-facto knowledge distribution it does not own, evidenced by EKS-01 where a lane was taught a superseded path via its own workflow record's tokenRef -- the strongest evidence for a distinct C-10 (Knowledge Distribution) capability rather than 'Communication' in the ordinary sense.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Communication is two capabilities wearing one name. C-10 Knowledge Distribution -- a genuine, evidenced, unowned MECHANISM ... C-19 Communication Composition -- a STEWARDSHIP
rationale_evidence.statement: 'Communication' as commonly discussed is proposed to be two distinct capabilities: C-10 Knowledge Distribution (a genuine unowned mechanism, evidenced by EKS-01) and C-19 Communication Composition (a stewardship, failing the bounded-context test on language and reason-to-change); a single 'Communication Engineer' role would wrongly bind a mechanism gap and a reporting duty into one actor.

rationale_evidence.anchor: that recurrence is itself evidence bearing on C-10 -- governed knowledge arriving outside the governed channel -- and the analysis may note it, but per AMD1 must not assume C-10 owns it.
rationale_evidence.statement: A pattern of substantive external input (a cited review, a 925-line brainstorming document, external research) repeatedly arriving outside the governed channel is recorded as evidence potentially bearing on C-10, but explicitly not assumed to be owned by C-10 without further decision.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted
rationale_evidence.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

rationale_evidence.anchor: C-10 is NOT the whole path. Its smallest coherent boundary is APPLICABILITY + RECEIPT. ... What nothing owns is: (a) deciding WHICH governed knowledge is applicable to THIS assignment, and (b) evidencing that the executing session actually holds the CURRENT version.
rationale_evidence.statement: C-10's smallest coherent capability boundary is proposed to be applicability determination plus receipt (not the whole created->published->selected->retrieved->delivered->acknowledged->applied->verified path), since creation/publication is BC-1's, retrieval/bootstrap is BC-6's, and only applicability-determination and receipt-evidencing are genuinely unowned.

rationale_evidence.anchor: fails on 6 of 10 => a STEWARDSHIP / cross-cutting expression concern ... the only state that could make a Communication context real -- delivery-with-acknowledgement -- is C-10's receipt, not C-19's. building C-10 would REDUCE the case for a Communication context.
rationale_evidence.statement: C-19 fails a ten-part bounded-context test on six of ten criteria (own language, independent lifecycle, independent authority, authoritative state, distinct reason to change, audience/consent/channel concepts) and is classified a stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern; the one property that could give it authoritative state (delivery-with-acknowledgement) actually belongs to C-10, so realizing C-10 reduces rather than increases the case for a Communication bounded context.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Recommended: YES -- C-10 exists as a capability, with realization NONE and its outer boundary OPEN. The load-bearing argument is D1 itself. ... A decision fixing the authoritative claim boundary of C-10's artifact presupposes a subject for that artifact.
rationale_evidence.statement: Governance recommends C-10 existence = YES, arguing that D1's decided receipt-claim boundary presupposes a subject for that claim, supported by a distinct reason to change, a distinct outcome, and two genuinely unowned stages sharing one purpose (applicability + receipt) -- this recommendation is later overturned by the PO/ARB (S0120 D2) as conflating a decided semantic with a performed capability.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Of five activities: one occurs and is owned elsewhere; four do not occur at all. Evidence of C-10 having occurred: none
rationale_evidence.statement: Applying the ten-question existence test to the estate's evidence: of C-10's five constituent activities (applicability, delivery, acknowledgement, claim-scoped receipt, invalidation/reconciliation), only one occurs and it is owned by other contexts (BC-6/BC-7), while four never occur at all and have no owner -- the counter-evidence supporting the later NOT YET ESTABLISHED verdict.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
rationale_evidence.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

rationale_evidence.anchor: C -- SPLIT. Fits every decided constraint. It matches OQ-J's 2-of-5 result ... applicability / transport / execution are already owned or already excluded
rationale_evidence.statement: Recommendation: Option C (SPLIT) for D3 -- C-10 would own only the receipt/attestation lifecycle and state (receipt identity, lifecycle state, invalidation, completeness), explicitly excluding applicability determination, delivery transport, session execution, identity binding, dispute adjudication, execution authority, and compliance/application.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Selecting HALT or BLOCK for any tier decides the category by consequence. ... the exact back-door structure D3's non-constitutive clause was created to prevent.
rationale_evidence.statement: Selecting an enforcing response (HALT or BLOCK) for any missing-knowledge condition would convert C-10 into a control-plane capability by consequence (per the canonical analysis's own control-plane test: control-plane if it gates START), the same back-door category-deciding risk D3's non-constitutive clause was designed to prevent.

rationale_evidence.anchor: D2: C-10 is NOT YET ESTABLISHED. No receipt activity is realized. Therefore ZERO receipts exist. Every session, for every required context version, is in state Missing. ... Tier-1 HALT on Missing is not strict -- it is total.
rationale_evidence.statement: Decisive practical-arithmetic finding: because D2 established C-10 as NOT YET ESTABLISHED, zero receipts currently exist, so every governed act is currently in the Missing-receipt condition -- meaning any blocking/halting response to Missing would halt the entire estate on the day it is enabled, not selectively.

rationale_evidence.anchor: F -- Compensating Control ... describes what the estate already does deliberately ... the recorded human START act is a compensating control -- a human authorization substituting for absent machine enforcement.
rationale_evidence.statement: A 'compensating control' option is elevated from underrated fallback to preferred transition mechanism, on the observation that the estate's own recorded human START act is already, in practice, a compensating control -- a human authorization substituting for absent machine enforcement, evidenced by seq 25 and seq 27 elsewhere in the batch.

rationale_evidence.anchor: E is not merely too weak -- it is the falsified status quo. ... E is not an untested option. It is the option currently in force, and it produced the defects this work item is adjudicating.
rationale_evidence.statement: Option E ('session responsible', i.e. evidence recorded but nothing enforced) is argued to be empirically falsified rather than merely weak: it is the estate's actual current behaviour and is cited as the direct cause of the same-day EKS-01 distribution failure, the missing-START off-record-execution pattern, and the false identity-attestation claim.

sources.note: S0903's Step 25K: the central state-machine/closure formalization proving KnowledgeOS's derived-state model is closed under Update with six invariants and eight passing closure tests; extends B0021's earlier knowledge-state-transition-algebra (S0862/Step 7) with event-log/derived-state separation, model-relativity, and explicit non-universal-property findings.

rows.anchor: Can KnowledgeOS compute K_{t+1} from K_t and new evidence? ... K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_t,\Omega,EC)
rows.statement: States the central question of the step and defines the fundamental transition function K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_t,Omega,EC) where K_t=current state, E_t=new epistemic input, Omega=domain ontology/rules, EC=applicable epistemic contract.

type_signature.domain: KnowledgeState x EpistemicInput x Ontology x EpistemicContract

rows.anchor: K=(Assertions,Evidence,Provenance,Relations,Assessments,Validity,TemporalState,Conflicts,Versions,Contracts,Policies)
rows.statement: Rejects K={facts} in favor of an 11-component tuple K=(Assertions, Evidence, Provenance, Relations, Assessments, Validity, TemporalState, Conflicts, Versions, Contracts, Policies), with Decisions/Actions/Observations optionally included depending on whether event history is treated as part of state or an external log.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeState=DerivedState ... EventLog=HistoricalCause ... an important DDD distinction
rows.statement: Recommends keeping the event log conceptually separate from the derived KnowledgeState: Events_t and K_t=Fold(Events_0..t), giving KnowledgeState=DerivedState vs EventLog=HistoricalCause — 'an important DDD distinction.'

rows.anchor: 10:00 Nexus=3.69, 11:00 Nexus=3.70, 12:00 Nexus=3.70 ... CurrentKnowledge\neq HistoricalKnowledge
rows.statement: Worked example: a three-event history where the current state (3.70) differs from the full history (3.69->3.70), showing both are valuable — CurrentKnowledge ≠ HistoricalKnowledge.

rows.anchor: DeterministicUpdate ... our first major invariant
rows.statement: States the first invariant: for fixed (K_t,E_t,Omega,EC), Update must produce the same K_{t+1} on repeated execution — DeterministicUpdate.

rows.anchor: RawInput\rightarrow LLM\rightarrow CandidateEvidence ... NonDeterministicAcquisition\rightarrow GovernedInput\rightarrow DeterministicStateTransition
rows.statement: Resolves the LLM-nondeterminism concern: an LLM may participate before admission (RawInput->LLM->CandidateEvidence), but once admitted as a structured event E_t the transition is deterministic — 'one of the most important architectural boundaries we have discovered.'

rows.anchor: Update(Update(K,E),E)\equiv Update(K,E) ... idempotence
rows.statement: Defines the second invariant, idempotence: applying the same evidence twice should not create artificial additional knowledge, Update(Update(K,E),E) ≡ Update(K,E), worked with a duplicate-database-record example resolved via EvidenceID(E1)=EvidenceID(E2) duplicate detection.

rows.anchor: Update must never destroy the source lineage ... Provenance(K)\supseteq Provenance(E)
rows.statement: States the third invariant, provenance preservation: after E->A->K, Provenance(K) ⊇ Provenance(E) — 'Update must be provenance-preserving.'

rows.anchor: UnresolvedConflict\rightarrow UnresolvedConflict unless new evidence or governance explicitly resolves it
rows.statement: States the fourth invariant, contradiction preservation: contradictory same-time/context evidence with no resolution rule must remain an unresolved conflict rather than being silently resolved.

rows.anchor: NoImplicitConflictResolution ... must not create A or B as the uniquely accepted truth merely because one looks more likely
rows.statement: States the fifth invariant, no hallucinated resolution: given A⊥B with no authorized resolution rule, Update must not pick a winner because it 'looks more likely' — NoImplicitConflictResolution.

rows.anchor: K_t\subseteq K_{t+1} ... not always true ... naive monotonicity fails
rows.statement: Tests naive monotonicity (K_t⊆K_{t+1}) against a version-change example (3.69->3.70 changes current state) and finds it fails.

rows.anchor: H_t\subseteq H_{t+1} ... History is monotonic; CurrentState need not be
rows.statement: Refines the sixth invariant into event-sourced monotonicity: historical event knowledge H_t is monotonic (events accumulate, history is never erased) even though current derived state is not — 'History is monotonic; CurrentState need not be' — 'a much better formulation.'

lineage_claims.target: this file's own rejected naive monotonicity (25K.12)
lineage_claims.quote: History is monotonic; CurrentState need not be.

rows.anchor: H_{t+1}=H_t\cup\{E_t\} ... K_{t+1}=Derive(H_{t+1},\Omega,EC) ... elegant
rows.statement: Formalizes the two-layer transition: H_{t+1}=H_t ∪ {E_t} (monotonic history growth) then K_{t+1}=Derive(H_{t+1},Omega,EC) (current state recomputation) — 'elegant.'

rows.anchor: Retract(E_1) ... Status(E_1)=Retracted ... K_{current} is recalculated
rows.statement: Defines retraction: a source's later 'the previous record was incorrect' becomes Retract(E1), setting Status(E1)=Retracted (not deleting E1 from history), then recalculating K_current.

rows.anchor: E_2:Correction(E_1,3.69) ... preserve E_1 and record E_2 ... Correction\neq Deletion
rows.statement: Defines correction as distinct from retraction/deletion: E2=Correction(E1,3.69) preserves E1 while recording the correcting event E2; the derived state may change to 3.69 — 'Correction ≠ Deletion.'

rows.anchor: The certificate used to establish the evidence has been revoked ... EvidenceValidity(E)=False ... Assertion separate from EvidenceAssessment
rows.statement: Defines revocation: a source can become invalid (e.g. a revoked certificate) without the proposition itself being false, EvidenceValidity(E)=False while the assertion remains historically recorded — demonstrates Assertion must be kept separate from EvidenceAssessment.

rows.anchor: ValidFrom\le t<ValidUntil ... Expired\neq False
rows.statement: Defines explicit validity intervals; when t>=ValidUntil the knowledge becomes Expired, explicitly distinct from False — 'this distinction is extremely important.'

rows.anchor: True/Supported, False/Refuted, Unknown, Expired, Conflicted ... must not be collapsed into a single Boolean
rows.statement: Lists (at least) five epistemic states that must not be collapsed into a single Boolean: Supported, Refuted, Unknown, Expired, and potentially Conflicted.

rows.anchor: \mathcal E=\{Unknown,Supported,Refuted,Conflicted,Expired,Retracted\} ... I would not yet call this a simple lattice ... Expired does not necessarily mean Refuted
rows.statement: Proposes a six-state epistemic space E={Unknown,Supported,Refuted,Conflicted,Expired,Retracted} but explicitly declines to call it a simple lattice since some states are orthogonal dimensions (Expired does not imply Refuted; Retracted may concern evidence rather than assertion).

rows.anchor: EpistemicState=(SupportStatus,ValidityStatus,ConflictStatus,TemporalStatus) ... much more expressive
rows.statement: Refines the epistemic-state space into a four-dimension tuple EpistemicState=(SupportStatus,ValidityStatus,ConflictStatus,TemporalStatus), worked with two example instantiations (one with ConflictStatus=none, one with ConflictStatus=conflicted) — 'much more expressive.'

rows.anchor: EpistemicStatus ... a strong candidate for a Value Object ... The Knowledge Entity owns the status ... derived from evidence, assessments, temporal rules, conflict relations
rows.statement: Maps EpistemicStatus onto DDD as an immutable Value Object owned by the Knowledge Entity, derived from evidence/assessments/temporal rules/conflict relations.

rows.anchor: Is K closed under Update? ... a closed state model must have a valid representation for every legitimate transition
rows.statement: States the core closure question — does Update(K_t,E_t) always produce K_{t+1} within the same state space K? — and argues closure matters because without it an input could produce a state the model cannot represent, e.g. evidence 'simultaneously valid, invalid, current, historical, contradictory and non-existent.'

rows.anchor: Test 1: new evidence K+E->K'. PASS if K' is valid.
rows.statement: Closure Test 1 (new evidence): K+E -> K' is valid — PASS.

experiment.hypothesis: New evidence produces a valid successor state.
experiment.setup: Apply single new evidence E to K.
experiment.method: apply Update
experiment.result: K' is valid
experiment.interpretation: Baseline closure case.
experiment.limitations: illustrative
experiment.conclusion: PASS.

rows.anchor: Test 2: duplicate evidence K+E+E ... PASS if idempotent
rows.statement: Closure Test 2 (duplicate evidence): K+E+E should equal K+E — PASS if idempotent.

experiment.hypothesis: Duplicate evidence does not compound.
experiment.setup: Apply the same evidence E twice.
experiment.method: apply Update twice with same E
experiment.result: equivalent to applying once
experiment.interpretation: Confirms idempotence invariant.
experiment.limitations: illustrative
experiment.conclusion: PASS.

rows.anchor: Test 3: contradictory evidence E_1\vdash A, E_2\vdash\neg A ... Conflict(A,\neg A). PASS.
rows.statement: Closure Test 3 (contradictory evidence): produces Conflict(A,¬A) — PASS.

experiment.hypothesis: Contradictory evidence yields a preserved conflict state.
experiment.setup: E1 vdash A, E2 vdash not-A.
experiment.method: apply Update with both events
experiment.result: Conflict(A, not-A)
experiment.interpretation: Confirms contradiction-preservation invariant within closure.
experiment.limitations: illustrative
experiment.conclusion: PASS.

rows.anchor: Test 4: later correction E_1\rightarrow E_2(Correction) ... Historical(E_1) and Current(E_2). PASS.
rows.statement: Closure Test 4 (correction): yields Historical(E1) and Current(E2) — PASS.

experiment.hypothesis: A correction event yields distinguishable historical vs current status.
experiment.setup: E1 followed by correcting E2.
experiment.method: apply Update with correction event
experiment.result: Historical(E1), Current(E2)
experiment.interpretation: Confirms correction handling.
experiment.limitations: illustrative
experiment.conclusion: PASS.

rows.anchor: Test 5: evidence retraction Retract(E) ... E remains historically available, but its evidential status changes. PASS.
rows.statement: Closure Test 5 (retraction): E remains historically available with changed evidential status — PASS.

experiment.hypothesis: Retraction changes status without deleting history.
experiment.setup: Retract(E) applied.
experiment.method: apply Update with retraction event
experiment.result: E retained historically, status changed
experiment.interpretation: Confirms retraction handling.
experiment.limitations: illustrative
experiment.conclusion: PASS.

rows.anchor: Test 6: expiration ValidUntil(E)<t ... TemporalStatus=Expired. Not False. PASS.
rows.statement: Closure Test 6 (expiration): produces TemporalStatus=Expired, not False — PASS.

experiment.hypothesis: Expiration is distinguishable from falsity.
experiment.setup: ValidUntil(E) < current time t.
experiment.method: apply Update with expired validity interval
experiment.result: TemporalStatus=Expired
experiment.interpretation: Confirms Expired!=False distinction within closure.
experiment.limitations: illustrative
experiment.conclusion: PASS.

rows.anchor: Test 7: semantic reinterpretation A_1\equiv A_2 ... CandidateRelation\rightarrow Assessment\rightarrow Accepted/Rejected. PASS.
rows.statement: Closure Test 7 (semantic reinterpretation): an LLM-proposed equivalence adds a candidate relation without automatically invalidating existing knowledge, going through Assessment to Accepted/Rejected — PASS.

experiment.hypothesis: A proposed semantic relation must not silently invalidate existing knowledge.
experiment.setup: LLM proposes A1 equiv A2.
experiment.method: add CandidateRelation, route through Assessment
experiment.result: Accepted/Rejected outcome, no automatic invalidation
experiment.interpretation: Confirms integration with semantic-equivalence-refinement-contradiction-merge-algebra's governed-validation pattern.
experiment.limitations: illustrative
experiment.conclusion: PASS.

rows.anchor: Test 8: model version change \Omega_1 replaced by \Omega_2 ... Both can coexist as versioned interpretations. PASS. This is extremely powerful.
rows.statement: Closure Test 8 (model version change): K^(1)=Derive(H,Omega1) and K^(2)=Derive(H,Omega2) can coexist as versioned interpretations while the historical event log stays unchanged — 'extremely powerful' — PASS.

experiment.hypothesis: Changing the domain-ontology model produces a distinct, coexisting derived interpretation without altering history.
experiment.setup: Same history H derived under Omega1 vs Omega2.
experiment.method: apply Derive with two ontology versions
experiment.result: K^(1), K^(2) both valid, coexisting
experiment.interpretation: Confirms model-relativity of derived knowledge.
experiment.limitations: illustrative
experiment.conclusion: PASS.

rows.anchor: K=Derive(H,\Omega,EC) ... does not mean truth is arbitrary. It means our computational representation of knowledge depends on the rules under which evidence is interpreted
rows.statement: Draws the philosophical/mathematical conclusion that knowledge is model-relative (K=Derive(H,Omega,EC)) without implying truth is arbitrary — the computational representation depends on interpretation rules.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeSnapshotID ... EventVersion+OntologyVersion+ContractVersion+AssessmentModelVersion ... K_t=Derive(H_{\le t},\Omega_v,EC_v,M_v) ... a very strong foundation for auditability
rows.statement: Defines KnowledgeSnapshotID as referencing EventVersion+OntologyVersion+ContractVersion+AssessmentModelVersion, giving the reproducibility equation K_t=Derive(H_<=t, Omega_v, EC_v, M_v) — 'a very strong foundation for auditability.'

rows.anchor: M=LLM ... Derive(H,\Omega,EC,LLM) may not be reproducible exactly ... LLM\rightarrow CandidateArtifact\rightarrow Assessment\rightarrow AcceptedEvent
rows.statement: Addresses nondeterministic models: if M=LLM, Derive(...) may not reproduce exactly, so the LLM must not silently participate in the deterministic transition — instead LLM->CandidateArtifact->Assessment->AcceptedEvent, after which the accepted Event becomes deterministic input.

rows.anchor: RAW WORLD INPUT -> {Deterministic Extraction, AI/LLM Interpretation} -> CANDIDATE INPUT -> VALIDATION -> EPISTEMIC EVENT -> EVENT LOG -> DETERMINISTIC STATE DERIVER -> KNOWLEDGE STATE ... one of the cleanest architectures we have produced so far
rows.statement: Presents a full architecture diagram from raw world input through parallel deterministic/AI extraction paths, converging at candidate input, validation, epistemic event, event log, and a deterministic state deriver producing the knowledge state — 'one of the cleanest architectures we have produced so far.'

rows.anchor: T:(K,E,\Omega,EC)\rightarrow K' ... IdentityPreserved, ProvenancePreserved, HistoryPreserved, ConflictPreserved, NoUnauthorizedInference, Idempotence
rows.statement: Defines the state transition operator T:(K,E,Omega,EC)->K' with six named invariants: IdentityPreserved, ProvenancePreserved, HistoryPreserved, ConflictPreserved, NoUnauthorizedInference, Idempotence (where applicable).

rows.anchor: T(T(K,E_1),E_2)\equiv T(K,\{E_1,E_2\}) under appropriate conditions ... another major property to test
rows.statement: Poses whether sequential transition composition equals batch application (T(T(K,E1),E2) ≡ T(K,{E1,E2})) under appropriate conditions, flagged as 'another major property to test,' not yet proven.

rows.anchor: processing order should ideally not matter provided temporal semantics are preserved ... resulting current state should be 3.70
rows.statement: Notes that for two timestamped, non-causally-linked events, processing order ideally should not matter provided temporal semantics are preserved, yielding the correct current state.

rows.anchor: E_2=Retract(E_1) ... should not blindly demand T(T(K,E_1),E_2)=T(T(K,E_2),E_1) ... EventOrdering must be explicit where required
rows.statement: Counterexample to universal commutativity: when E2=Retract(E1), processing order matters (retracting before the retracted event exists requires deferred resolution) — events have causal/dependency relationships, so EventOrdering must be made explicit where required.

rows.anchor: What consistency must be guaranteed atomically? ... I would not make the entire KnowledgeOS graph one aggregate ... EvidenceAggregate, KnowledgeAggregate, GovernanceAggregate, DecisionAggregate
rows.statement: Raises the DDD aggregate-boundary question and rejects treating the entire KnowledgeOS graph as one aggregate (would destroy scalability), proposing instead separate bounded aggregates (EvidenceAggregate: evidence identity; KnowledgeAggregate: assertion/version consistency; GovernanceAggregate: authority decisions; DecisionAggregate: decision lifecycle) with cross-aggregate eventual consistency.

rows.anchor: Mathematical closure does not require a single transactional database ... DistributedSystem while maintaining EpistemicInvariants
rows.statement: Argues closure does not require a single transactional database — a distributed system can maintain the epistemic invariants, keeping the architecture compatible with normal enterprise systems.

rows.anchor: K_t is essentially a structured posterior/information state only where a statistical model is explicitly defined ... KnowledgeState\supset StatisticalState
rows.statement: Rejects equating KnowledgeState with a probability distribution: KnowledgeState ⊃ StatisticalState (statistical interpretation applies only where a model is explicitly defined), since KnowledgeOS can hold deterministic facts, rules, observations, hypotheses, and probability models simultaneously.

rows.anchor: P(H)=0.8 does not mean H=True ... H=True in a deterministic rule system does not necessarily mean P(H)=1 ... epistemic representations must remain typed
rows.statement: Illustrates a category error the KnowledgeState/StatisticalState distinction prevents: probabilistic P(H)=0.8 does not equal H=True, and deterministic H=True does not necessarily equal P(H)=1.

rows.anchor: \mathcal K=\{Fact,Hypothesis,Observation,Assertion,Rule,Constraint,Prediction,Decision,...\} ... this typing prevents category errors
rows.statement: Proposes a typed epistemic-object system K={Fact, Hypothesis, Observation, Assertion, Rule, Constraint, Prediction, Decision, ...}, with worked distinctions (a Prediction can become false without having been invalid when created; a HistoricalFact can remain true after it stops describing the current state; a Rule is not a fact about the world at all) — 'this typing prevents category errors.'

rows.anchor: stop using the word knowledge as if it were a single homogeneous object ... KnowledgeState=typed epistemic objects+relations+assessments+temporal state
rows.statement: States the 25K conceptual correction: stop treating 'knowledge' as one homogeneous object; KnowledgeState = typed epistemic objects + relations + assessments + temporal state.

rows.anchor: | Property | Result | ... Universal monotonicity ❌ Universal commutativity ❌ Universal associativity ❌ ... not failures
rows.statement: Presents a 14-row closure test-result table with 11 properties PASS (checkmark) and three explicitly marked ❌ (Universal monotonicity, commutativity, associativity), explicitly framed as 'not failures' but honest statements that these cannot be universally assumed.

rows.anchor: History monotonic but CurrentKnowledge non-monotonic ... Some updates commute but Causal updates may not ... mathematically much more defensible
rows.statement: Argues the refusal to claim universal monotonicity/commutativity/associativity is itself a success: a weaker architecture claiming 'knowledge is always monotonic' would be wrong; the qualified findings (history monotonic, current knowledge not; some updates commute, causal ones may not) are 'mathematically much more defensible.'

rows.anchor: 25K — PASS ... Given a versioned event history, explicit ontology, epistemic contract and deterministic state-derivation rules, KnowledgeOS can maintain a reproducible evolving KnowledgeState
rows.statement: Step 25K self-verdict: PASS, with the central theorem-like statement that given a versioned event history, explicit ontology, epistemic contract, and deterministic state-derivation rules, KnowledgeOS can maintain a reproducible evolving KnowledgeState, formalized via K_t=Derive(H_<=t,Omega_v,EC_v,M_v) and K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_t,Omega,EC).

rows.anchor: Event History + State Derivation + Epistemic Algebra ... rather than simply Database+LLM ... a major architectural distinction
rows.statement: States that KnowledgeOS can be modeled as Event History + State Derivation + Epistemic Algebra rather than simply Database+LLM — 'a major architectural distinction.'

rows.anchor: W_t\rightarrow O_t\rightarrow E_t\rightarrow A_t\rightarrow K_t\rightarrow Zero_t\rightarrow Lord_t\rightarrow Sarathi_t\rightarrow D_t\rightarrow Authorization_t\rightarrow Action_t\rightarrow W_{t+1} ... a genuine epistemic control loop
rows.statement: Presents the full closed-loop architecture with explicit time indices (W_t->O_t->E_t->A_t->K_t->Zero_t->Lord_t->Sarathi_t->D_t->Authorization_t->Action_t->W_{t+1}), calling it 'a genuine epistemic control loop.'

rows.anchor: Can two independently evolving KnowledgeOS instances eventually be merged and produce the same valid state? ... Node A receives E1,E3; Node B receives E2,E4 ... Step 25L
rows.statement: Closes by posing the distributed-consistency question — whether two independently-evolving KnowledgeOS instances (worked example: Node A receiving E1,E3; Node B receiving E2,E4) can be merged into a deterministically convergent state — transitioning to Step 25L, explicitly noting 'KnowledgeOS is unlikely to be a single-machine system in its final form' (ingesting from Git, databases, documents, humans, agents, APIs, multiple bounded contexts) and connecting to distributed systems theory, CRDT-like convergence, event sourcing, DDD bounded contexts, and statistical independence.

lineage_claims.quote: Step 25L — Distributed Knowledge, Merge, Convergence and Consistency

lexical.anchor: Can KnowledgeOS compute K_{t+1} from K_t and new evidence? ... K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_t,\Omega,EC)

conceptual.anchor: EpistemicStatus ... a strong candidate for a Value Object ... The Knowledge Entity owns the status ... derived from evidence, assessments, temporal rules, conflict relations

formal.anchor: Can KnowledgeOS compute K_{t+1} from K_t and new evidence? ... K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_t,\Omega,EC)

operational.anchor: Test 1: new evidence K+E->K'. PASS if K' is valid.

rationale_evidence.anchor: \mathcal E=\{Unknown,Supported,Refuted,Conflicted,Expired,Retracted\} ... I would not yet call this a simple lattice ... Expired does not necessarily mean Refuted
rationale_evidence.statement: Proposes a six-state epistemic space E={Unknown,Supported,Refuted,Conflicted,Expired,Retracted} but explicitly declines to call it a simple lattice since some states are orthogonal dimensions (Expired does not imply Refuted; Retracted may concern evidence rather than assertion).

rationale_evidence.anchor: Is K closed under Update? ... a closed state model must have a valid representation for every legitimate transition
rationale_evidence.statement: States the core closure question — does Update(K_t,E_t) always produce K_{t+1} within the same state space K? — and argues closure matters because without it an input could produce a state the model cannot represent, e.g. evidence 'simultaneously valid, invalid, current, historical, contradictory and non-existent.'

rationale_evidence.anchor: K=Derive(H,\Omega,EC) ... does not mean truth is arbitrary. It means our computational representation of knowledge depends on the rules under which evidence is interpreted
rationale_evidence.statement: Draws the philosophical/mathematical conclusion that knowledge is model-relative (K=Derive(H,Omega,EC)) without implying truth is arbitrary — the computational representation depends on interpretation rules.

rationale_evidence.anchor: What consistency must be guaranteed atomically? ... I would not make the entire KnowledgeOS graph one aggregate ... EvidenceAggregate, KnowledgeAggregate, GovernanceAggregate, DecisionAggregate
rationale_evidence.statement: Raises the DDD aggregate-boundary question and rejects treating the entire KnowledgeOS graph as one aggregate (would destroy scalability), proposing instead separate bounded aggregates (EvidenceAggregate: evidence identity; KnowledgeAggregate: assertion/version consistency; GovernanceAggregate: authority decisions; DecisionAggregate: decision lifecycle) with cross-aggregate eventual consistency.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Mathematical closure does not require a single transactional database ... DistributedSystem while maintaining EpistemicInvariants
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues closure does not require a single transactional database — a distributed system can maintain the epistemic invariants, keeping the architecture compatible with normal enterprise systems.

rationale_evidence.anchor: P(H)=0.8 does not mean H=True ... H=True in a deterministic rule system does not necessarily mean P(H)=1 ... epistemic representations must remain typed
rationale_evidence.statement: Illustrates a category error the KnowledgeState/StatisticalState distinction prevents: probabilistic P(H)=0.8 does not equal H=True, and deterministic H=True does not necessarily equal P(H)=1.

rationale_evidence.anchor: | Property | Result | ... Universal monotonicity ❌ Universal commutativity ❌ Universal associativity ❌ ... not failures
rationale_evidence.statement: Presents a 14-row closure test-result table with 11 properties PASS (checkmark) and three explicitly marked ❌ (Universal monotonicity, commutativity, associativity), explicitly framed as 'not failures' but honest statements that these cannot be universally assumed.

rationale_evidence.anchor: History monotonic but CurrentKnowledge non-monotonic ... Some updates commute but Causal updates may not ... mathematically much more defensible
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues the refusal to claim universal monotonicity/commutativity/associativity is itself a success: a weaker architecture claiming 'knowledge is always monotonic' would be wrong; the qualified findings (history monotonic, current knowledge not; some updates commute, causal ones may not) are 'mathematically much more defensible.'

aliases: Step 12: Identity, Entity Resolution, and Semantic Equivalence

sources.note: S0866's Step 12: separates Representation/Entity/Proposition; defines KnowledgeEntity, canonical ID(x), entity graph G_X, IdentityAssertion as an evidence-based inference; defines context-relative semantic equivalence and EquivalentProposition!=SameAssertion; names 'semantic hallucination becoming structural identity' as a guarded-against AI failure mode; defines auditable Merge/Split, four separated operations (Extraction/Normalization/IdentityResolution/Validation), an ontology Omega with versioning, non-full-decidability of equivalence, and ID1-ID14 invariants; hands off to Step 13 (sufficiency/completeness/readiness for purpose).

rows.anchor: If identity is wrong, everything downstream can be wrong. ... Nexus / Nexus Repository / Nexus3 / nexus3.dgverlag.de / the artifact repository / the old Nexus server ... Same name\neq Same entity ... Different name\neq Different entity. This becomes a fundamental KnowledgeOS principle.
rows.statement: States the fundamental principle SameName≠SameEntity and DifferentName≠DifferentEntity, illustrated with six differently-named references possibly denoting the same Nexus system, and warns that identity errors propagate downstream through Comparison→Conflict→EvidenceAggregation→Inference→Discrepancy.

rows.anchor: Three things must be separated ... Representation r ... Entity x ... Proposition P(x). Representation\neq Entity\neq Proposition
rows.statement: Separates Representation (textual expression r), Entity (the referent x), and Proposition (a statement P(x) about that entity) as three distinct concepts.

rows.anchor: DDD interpretation ... Identity — which domain object is this? Value — what does it represent? Context — where does this identity have meaning? Aggregate — what consistency boundary governs it? Reference — how do we locate it? ... KnowledgeEntity with a stable identity independent of how it happens
rows.statement: Maps identity to five DDD concepts (Identity/Value/Context/Aggregate/Reference), introducing a KnowledgeEntity domain concept with stable identity independent of naming.

rows.anchor: Canonical identity ... ID(x) ... EntityId: system:nexus:production ... multiple representations can resolve to it ... if sufficient evidence establishes Resolve(r_i)=x.
rows.statement: Defines a canonical entity identifier ID(x) (e.g. system:nexus:production) to which multiple surface representations may resolve given sufficient evidence.

rows.anchor: Resolution is not string matching ... Normalize("Nexus3")=Normalize("nexus3") and conclude identity. That is unsafe. Instead EntityResolution = f(Representation,Context,Evidence,IdentityRules). The output should itself have an epistemic status.
rows.statement: Warns that string-normalization matching is unsafe for entity resolution, defining EntityResolution=f(Representation,Context,Evidence,IdentityRules) with an epistemic status on the output rather than a boolean.

rows.anchor: Entity resolution is an inference ... Nexus3 is running on nexus3.dgverlag.de. We infer Entity("Nexus3")=Entity("nexus3.dgverlag.de"). But this is not necessarily directly observed. ... IdentityAssertion with evidence and provenance.
rows.statement: Connects entity resolution to Step 10's inference machinery: identity claims are themselves inferences, not direct observations, and must be represented as an IdentityAssertion carrying evidence and provenance.

rows.anchor: Identity assertion ... I_A=(r,x,S,Ctx,\Pi,\tau) ... "Nexus3" \equiv system:nexus:production. But KnowledgeOS should know why it believes that.
rows.statement: Defines IdentityAssertion I_A=(representation,entity,Support,Context,Provenance,Validity) so KnowledgeOS always records why an identity claim is believed.

rows.anchor: Identity is contextual ... Nexus means the Nexus product in one context ... the production deployment in another context. Meaning(Nexus,C_1)\neq Meaning(Nexus,C_2). Identity is interpreted within context. We should never create a universal global identity merely from a name.
rows.statement: States identity is interpreted within context (Meaning(Nexus,C1)≠Meaning(Nexus,C2)) — a universal global identity must never be created merely from a name.

rows.anchor:
Product versus instance ... NexusProduct versus NexusInstance_{Production} ... Software
eq Deployment
eq Container
eq Host
eq Service
eq Endpoint. A DDD model must preserve these distinctions.
rows.statement: Distinguishes Product from Instance and six further layered concepts (Software/Deployment/Container/Host/Service/Endpoint) that a DDD model must preserve separately.

rows.anchor: Entity identity can be hierarchical ... x_{product}, x_{deployment}, x_{host} ... DeploymentOf(x_{deployment},x_{product}) RunsOn(x_{deployment},x_{host}) ExposedAt(x_{deployment},endpoint). Thus identity is not just a flat lookup. It is a semantic graph. ... Entity graph G_X=(\mathcal X,\mathcal R_
rows.statement: Defines a hierarchical Entity graph G_X=(X,R_X) with typed relations (DeploymentOf, RunsOn, ExposedAt) linking product/deployment/host/endpoint layers, arguing identity is a semantic graph, not a flat lookup.

rows.anchor: Now semantic equivalence ... Version(Nexus)=3.69 and Nexus is running release 3.69 ... may be semantically equivalent. But Nexus was version 3.69 in 2024 is not equivalent to P_1 if P_1 is intended to describe the current state. ... Define semantic equivalence P_1\equiv_C P_2 ... The context subscri
rows.statement: Defines context-relative semantic equivalence P1≡_C P2, warning that without the context subscript equivalence becomes dangerously absolute, illustrated by a temporally-scoped proposition that is not equivalent to a current-state one.

rows.anchor: Equivalence is not identity ... A_1: Nexus=3.69 from a document. A_2: Nexus=3.69 from an API. They may express the same proposition P(A_1)\equiv P(A_2). But they remain separate assertions because their evidence; provenance; acquisition time; source; epistemic state are different. EquivalentProposit
rows.statement: States EquivalentProposition ≠ SameAssertion: two assertions expressing the same proposition from different sources remain distinct assertion objects because their evidence/provenance/acquisition differ — essential for correct evidence aggregation.

rows.anchor: Duplicate evidence problem ... If B was copied from A, we must not count A+B as two independent pieces of evidence. Therefore semantic equivalence alone is insufficient. We also need EvidenceDependency and SourceIndependence. This connects Step 12 directly to Step 11.
rows.statement: Reaffirms semantic equivalence alone is insufficient for evidence counting; EvidenceDependency and SourceIndependence must also be checked (connecting to Step 11), so copied duplicate documents are not double-counted.

rows.anchor: Four different relationships ... Same x_1=x_2 ... Equivalent P_1\equiv P_2 ... Related P_1\sim P_2 ... Contradictory P_1\bowtie P_2 ... Distinct: No established semantic relationship.
rows.statement: Defines four (five including Distinct) proposition/entity relationship kinds: Same, Equivalent, Related, Contradictory, Distinct.

rows.anchor: Contradiction now becomes much more precise ... Conflict= f(EntityResolution,SemanticComparison,Context,TemporalScope,ConflictRule). This is much stronger than simply comparing strings.
rows.statement: Refines Conflict detection as a function of EntityResolution, SemanticComparison, Context, TemporalScope, and ConflictRule together, rather than simple string comparison.

rows.anchor: Example ... Nexus3.dgverlag.de=3.69 and ProductionNexus=3.70. Before declaring conflict, KnowledgeOS must establish Entity(nexus3.dgverlag.de)=Entity(ProductionNexus)? and Environment(P_1)=Environment(P_2)? and Time(P_1)=Time(P_2)? Only then can it evaluate 3.69\neq3.70. This is precisely why identi
rows.statement: Worked example showing entity/environment/temporal identity must all be established before a version discrepancy can be declared a conflict — identity resolution is upstream of contradiction detection.

rows.anchor: Entity resolution has uncertainty ... We should never force identity resolution into Same/NotSame too early. ResolutionStatus could include Unknown, Candidate, LikelySame, ConfirmedSame, LikelyDifferent, ConfirmedDifferent, Contested. This is another multidimensional epistemic object.
rows.statement: Defines a seven-value ResolutionStatus enum (Unknown/Candidate/LikelySame/ConfirmedSame/LikelyDifferent/ConfirmedDifferent/Contested) instead of a premature boolean Same/NotSame.

rows.anchor: Candidate identity ... an LLM ... proposes Entity("repository server")=Entity("Nexus production"). We record CandidateIdentity. We do not immediately merge them. This prevents one of the most dangerous AI failure modes: semantic hallucination becoming structural identity.
rows.statement: Names and guards against a specific AI failure mode — 'semantic hallucination becoming structural identity' — by recording LLM-proposed identity as CandidateIdentity rather than merging immediately.

rows.anchor: Identity merge is a high-impact operation ... Merging them changes potentially huge parts of the graph. Merge(x_1,x_2) should be governed by an explicit policy. It should not be an ordinary side effect of an LLM extraction. ... Identity merge and provenance ... original identities; evidence; provena
rows.statement: Requires entity Merge(x1,x2) be a policy-governed, auditable operation preserving original identities/evidence/provenance/contexts/timestamps/decision authority/reason — never an ordinary side effect of LLM extraction.

rows.anchor: Identity split ... Later evidence establishes they are distinct. We need Split(x)\rightarrow x_1,x_2 with historical provenance. Split\neq Delete. This is belief revision applied to entity identity.
rows.statement: Defines the reverse Split(x)→x1,x2 operation with historical provenance preserved (Split≠Delete), applying belief-revision principles to entity identity.

rows.anchor: Identity is therefore mutable epistemically ... The real-world entity may be stable. But KnowledgeOS's knowledge of identity can change. Entity_{real} may remain constant while KnowledgeOSIdentity_t changes.
rows.statement: Distinguishes the (presumably stable) real-world entity from KnowledgeOS's own time-varying identity knowledge about it.

rows.anchor: Entity resolution and Ideal State ... Every production system must have: canonical identity, owner, environment, endpoint, lifecycle status ... but not whether it is Production or Staging. Then IdentityGap is a legitimate discrepancy. So identity becomes part of \Delta_E.
rows.statement: Connects identity gaps to the Ideal State: missing identity attributes (e.g. unknown environment) become a legitimate IdentityGap discrepancy, feeding the overall discrepancy Δ_E.

rows.anchor: Semantic normalization ... "Nexus runs 3.69" becomes Version(Entity(Nexus),3.69). ... CanonicalRepresentation. ... But canonicalization is not truth ... does not establish that it is true. It establishes only: This is our semantic representation of what the source says. Normalization\neq Validation.
rows.statement: Defines semantic normalization into a canonical predicate form (e.g. Version(Entity(Nexus),3.69)), explicitly warning Normalization ≠ Validation — canonicalization records what a source says, not whether it is true.

rows.anchor:
Parsing versus interpretation ... Syntactic extraction ... Semantic normalization ... Identity resolution ... Validation ... These are four separate operations. Extraction
eq Normalization
eq IdentityResolution
eq Validation. This should become another KnowledgeOS invariant.
rows.statement: States four operations (Syntactic extraction, Semantic normalization, Identity resolution, Validation) must remain distinct as a KnowledgeOS invariant.

rows.anchor: LLM's role ... Text \rightarrow CandidateSemanticRepresentation ... EntityCandidate: Nexus repository ... RelationCandidate: hosted-on ... EntityCandidate: RHEL server ... But these are Candidate until validated.
rows.statement: Illustrates LLM's role producing candidate entity/relation extractions (e.g. hosted-on relation between Nexus repository and RHEL server), remaining Candidate status until validated.

rows.anchor: Deterministic identity evidence ... DNS: nexus3.dgverlag.de → 10.61.133.85 ... Host inventory: 10.61.133.85 = Nexus host ... This provides a much stronger basis for entity resolution. KnowledgeOS can combine LLM semantic candidates with deterministic infrastructure evidence.
rows.statement: Shows deterministic infrastructure evidence (DNS + host inventory chaining) can combine with LLM semantic candidates to give a much stronger basis for entity resolution.

rows.anchor: Entity resolution as evidence accumulation ... E_1,E_2,\ldots,E_n supporting x_1=x_2 ... Support(x_1=x_2) = Assess(E_1,\ldots,E_n). Identity resolution does not need a completely separate epistemology. It is another domain where our general evidence/assessment machinery operates.
rows.statement: Argues entity-identity claims are supported by evidence via the same general evidence/assessment machinery — identity resolution needs no separate epistemology, a major architectural simplification.

rows.anchor: Semantic equivalence can also be evidence-based ... A domain ontology may define Version(x,v)\equiv InstalledRelease(x,v). Then equivalence is deterministic under the ontology. Alternatively an LLM may propose the equivalence. Then EquivalenceStatus=Candidate. SemanticEquivalence can be rule-based o
rows.statement: Shows semantic equivalence can be established deterministically via ontology rules or proposed by an LLM as Candidate — SemanticEquivalence can be rule-based or AI-proposed.

rows.anchor: Ontology becomes important ... a semantic model \Omega containing concepts, relations, constraints, and equivalence rules. DeploymentOf(x,y), RunsOn(x,y), VersionOf(x,v), HostedAt(x,h). The ontology provides the vocabulary in which propositions become comparable. ... But ontology itself is knowledge
rows.statement: Introduces the semantic model Ω (concepts, relations, constraints, equivalence rules) as the vocabulary for comparable propositions, noting the ontology itself is knowledge requiring OntologyVersion governance, connecting to Steps 7 and 10's versioning requirements.

rows.anchor: Semantic equivalence is generally not fully decidable ... For arbitrary natural language P_1\equiv P_2 is not generally decidable. ... SemanticEquivalence = Determined | Supported | Candidate | Unknown. The system must be able to say: I don't know whether these mean the same thing. That is a feature
rows.statement: States semantic equivalence of arbitrary natural language is not generally decidable, requiring a four-value status (Determined/Supported/Candidate/Unknown); the system honestly saying 'I don't know' is a feature, not a failure.

rows.anchor: A semantic comparison result ... SC=(P_1,P_2,Relation,Context,Basis,Status) ... Relation\in\{Equivalent,Compatible,Contradictory,Related,Independent,Unknown\}. The relation itself should not be confused with its epistemic certainty.
rows.statement: Defines a structured SemanticComparison object SC=(P1,P2,Relation,Context,Basis,Status) with a six-value Relation enum, distinguishing the relation from its epistemic certainty.

rows.anchor: This gives us a semantic comparison algebra ... Compare(P_1,P_2,C,\Omega) \rightarrow SC ... This result can feed ConflictDetection or EvidenceAggregation or DuplicateDetection.
rows.statement: Defines Compare(P1,P2,C,Ω)→SC as feeding directly into ConflictDetection, EvidenceAggregation, and DuplicateDetection.

rows.anchor: Identity and proposition equality ... EntityIdentity\neq AssertionIdentity\neq PropositionEquivalence.
rows.statement: States EntityIdentity ≠ AssertionIdentity ≠ PropositionEquivalence as three distinct equality notions that must not be conflated.

rows.anchor: Why this matters for Evidence ... three documents all state Nexus is version 3.69 ... KnowledgeOS should represent A_1,A_2,A_3 as distinct assertions if they have distinct provenance. Then P(A_1)\equiv P(A_2)\equiv P(A_3). Now dependency analysis determines whether E_1,E_2,E_3 are independent. This
rows.statement: Worked example: three documents making equivalent statements remain distinct assertions with independent provenance, so dependency analysis (not proposition equivalence alone) determines correct evidential support.

rows.anchor: Identity mistakes can create false certainty ... If identity resolution incorrectly merges ProductionNexus=StagingNexus, KnowledgeOS creates a false conflict. If it incorrectly separates them ... it might miss a real conflict. EntityResolution errors propagate into epistemic errors.
rows.statement: Warns entity-resolution errors propagate into epistemic errors in both directions: incorrect merging creates false conflicts, incorrect separation hides real ones.

rows.anchor: Identity errors should therefore be first-class discrepancies ... IdentityStatus=Unknown then Zero should potentially produce d_{identity} rather than pretending the comparison is valid.
rows.statement: Extends Zero to produce a first-class d_identity discrepancy when IdentityStatus is Unknown, rather than proceeding as if identity comparison were valid.

rows.anchor: The complete identity pipeline ... Raw representation → Extraction → Canonical semantic representation → Entity candidate → Identity evidence → Entity resolution → Canonical entity → Proposition normalization → Semantic comparison → Equivalent/Compatible/Contradictory/Related/Independent/Unknown
rows.statement: Assembles the complete identity pipeline from raw representation through extraction, canonical semantic representation, entity candidate, identity evidence, entity resolution, canonical entity, proposition normalization, to semantic comparison outcomes.

rows.anchor: DDD aggregate implications ... I would not make EntityResolution part of the Assertion aggregate. Knowledge / Entity (Identity, Representation, Context) / Assertion (Proposition, EpistemicState, Provenance) / SemanticRelation / Conflict / Evidence. This maintains separation of concerns.
rows.statement: Rejects folding EntityResolution into the Assertion aggregate, proposing separate bounded concepts Entity, Assertion, SemanticRelation, Conflict, Evidence to maintain separation of concerns.

rows.anchor: A very important architectural boundary ... The Entity should not be confused with the real-world object. KnowledgeOS has an epistemic representation \hat{x} of a presumed real entity x. KnowledgeOS Entity\neq Reality. It is the system's governed representation of identity.
rows.statement: States KnowledgeOS Entity ≠ Reality: the system holds an epistemic representation x̂ of a presumed real entity x, never the real-world object itself.

rows.anchor: Mathematical formulation ... Resolve: \mathcal R\times C \rightharpoonup \mathcal X ... Normalize: \mathcal R\times\Omega \rightharpoonup \mathcal P ... Compare: \mathcal P\times\mathcal P\times C\times\Omega \rightarrow \mathcal Q ... But these functions should return epistemic results ... Resoluti
rows.statement: Formalizes Resolve:R×C⇀X, Normalize:R×Ω⇀P, and Compare:P×P×C×Ω→Q as partial/total functions whose outputs are structured epistemic results (ResolutionResult, ComparisonResult) rather than bare values.

rows.anchor:
Step 12 invariants ... ID1 Representation
eq Entity ... ID2 Entity
eq Assertion ... ID3 AssertionIdentity
eq PropositionEquivalence ... ID4 SameName
ot\Rightarrow SameEntity ... ID5 DifferentName
ot\Rightarrow DifferentEntity ... ID6 IdentityResolution is evidence based ... ID7 Canonicalization
