rows.statement: Consolidates fourteen candidate invariants ID1-ID14 covering representation/entity/assertion separation, name-identity non-implication both ways, evidence-based identity resolution, canonicalization vs validation, context-dependent equivalence, representable unknown identity, auditable merge/split, independent provenance for equivalent assertions, non-canonical AI-proposed identity, and revisable identity errors.

rows.anchor: The deeper result ... Reality \rightarrow Representation \rightarrow Proposition ... Representation \rightarrow EntityResolution ... Representation \rightarrow SemanticNormalization \rightarrow Proposition ... Then Proposition \rightarrow EvidenceAssessment \rightarrow Knowledge. This gives us a muc
rows.statement: Distills three semantic layers (Reality→Representation→Proposition) with Representation branching into EntityResolution and SemanticNormalization, feeding a cleaner overall architecture.

rows.anchor: The complete chain so far ... Reality/Source \rightarrow Representation \rightarrow EntityResolution / SemanticNormalization \rightarrow Entity+Proposition \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow Assessment \rightarrow Acceptance \rightarrow KnowledgeState \rightarrow Comparison \rightarrow Conflict/Discre
rows.statement: Assembles the full cumulative pipeline from Reality/Source through Representation, Entity/Proposition, Evidence, Assessment, Acceptance, KnowledgeState, Comparison, Conflict/Discrepancy, CandidateEvidence, Inference, to DerivedKnowledge.

rows.anchor: Step 12 verdict ... STRUCTURALLY RESOLVED ... We cannot guarantee perfect semantic identity resolution for arbitrary natural language. What we can guarantee is Uncertainty about identity is itself representable, traceable, and revisable. We should not promise omniscient semantic understanding.
rows.statement: Declares Step 12 structurally resolved with the explicit limitation that perfect semantic identity resolution for arbitrary natural language cannot be guaranteed — only that identity uncertainty itself is representable, traceable, and revisable.

rows.anchor: Step 13 — The next problem ... how does it determine whether the current Knowledge State is sufficient for a particular purpose? This is different from asking Is the knowledge true? It asks Do we know enough to act? ... Step 13 — Sufficiency, Completeness, and Readiness for Purpose ... Truth, Knowle
rows.statement: Poses Step 13: formalize the difference between Truth, KnowledgeCompleteness, EpistemicSufficiency, and DecisionReadiness — 'is the knowledge true?' versus 'do we know enough to act?'.

Then equivalence is deterministic under the ontology. Alternatively an LLM may propose the equivalence. Then EquivalenceStatus=Candidate. SemanticEquivalence can be rule-based o
rationale_evidence.statement: Shows semantic equivalence can be established deterministically via ontology rules or proposed by an LLM as Candidate — SemanticEquivalence can be rule-based or AI-proposed.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Identity mistakes can create false certainty ... If identity resolution incorrectly merges ProductionNexus=StagingNexus, KnowledgeOS creates a false conflict. If it incorrectly separates them ... it might miss a real conflict. EntityResolution errors propagate into epistemic errors.
rationale_evidence.statement: Warns entity-resolution errors propagate into epistemic errors in both directions: incorrect merging creates false conflicts, incorrect separation hides real ones.

aliases: Zoom-in as fact-finding discovery, not detail-inspection

sources.note: Reframes Zoom-in from 'look at more detail inside a represented node' (the prior KR-ZOOM-01/02 formulation) to 'given a relevant observation, discover previously unrepresented dimensions/causal pathways and investigate them' -- an open-ended dimension-discovery operation feeding a FactFinding->Determination->ZoomOut(Integration) loop, proposed as a new artifact KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-2026-09 with hypotheses ZF1-ZF7. Marked POSSIBLY related to the existing recursive-epistemic-zoom-resolution-relative-atomicity-2026-09 (KR-ZOOM-01, B0065) since it is presented as a deeper reformulation of 'Zoom' in the same lineage, but the object here is discovery-of-new-dimensions rather than resolution-relative-atomicity of an existing coordinate, so the merge is uncertain.

rows.anchor: At every observation you have infinite possible dimensions to be discovered. ... the projection to different observation field by zooming in can be the fact finding process about an event or process
rows.statement: Proposes that at every observation there is a potentially unbounded discoverable dimension space, and that zooming into different observation fields to find causes/situations/sources of an event constitutes the fact-finding process about that event, using a Nexus egress=70GB/day example with potentially relevant dimensions {Network,Backup,Repository,CI/CD,GitLabRunner,Configuration,Users,Traffic,Logs,Storage,Time,Security,Deployment,...}.

rows.anchor: D_t subseteq D* and potentially D* -> open/unbounded discovery space. ... Don't claim literally that the dimensions are mathematically infinite unless the model establishes such a domain. Instead: the discoverable dimension space is open-ended relative to the current representation.
rows.statement: Corrects the informal 'infinite possible dimensions' claim to a precise formulation: the currently represented dimensions D_t are a subset of a potentially discoverable D*, and the discoverable dimension space is open-ended relative to the current representation (D_t -Inquiry-> D_{t+1}), without D_{t+1} necessarily being a superset of D_t since dimensions can also become irrelevant/superseded/out-of-contract.

rows.anchor: ZoomIn(K_t,O,Q) -> FocusedInquirySpace ... The dimensions explored by Zoom-in need not have been present in the original observation.
rows.statement: Reformulates Zoom-in from the earlier K_t->Subgraph(K_t) (found inadequate) to ZoomIn(K_t,O,Q)->FocusedInquirySpace, where focus is not deletion of the rest of K_t and the explored dimensions need not have been present in the original observation -- a discovery operation rather than a within-representation detail operation.

lineage_claims.quote: The naive interpretation was K_t -> Subgraph(K_t) which we already found inadequate.

rows.anchor: Graph Traversal != Epistemic Investigation ... KnowledgeGraph = representational substrate ... ZoomIn = inquiry-directed exploration over that substrate and its discoverable extensions.
rows.statement: Separates Graph Traversal (a Knowledge Graph can represent an edge like GitLabRunner-causes->Egress) from Epistemic Investigation (KnowledgeOS asks why the edge should exist, requiring Evidence, Provenance, Time, AlternativeHypotheses, Assessment, Determination), giving KnowledgeGraph=representational substrate while ZoomIn=inquiry-directed exploration over that substrate and its discoverable extensions.

rows.anchor: ZoomOut(F_t,K_t) = Integrate(Finding,F_t,K_t) rather than simply FocusedState -> OriginalState. ... this is exactly why our previous Zoom-out experiments struggled: we were trying to classify Zoom-out before clearly separating restoration from integration.
rows.statement: Reframes Zoom-out from mere restoration (FocusedState->OriginalState) to Integration: ZoomOut(F_t,K_t)=Integrate(Finding,F_t,K_t), diagnosing that prior Zoom-out experiments struggled because they attempted to classify Zoom-out before separating restoration from integration.

lineage_claims.quote: this is exactly why our previous Zoom-out experiments struggled

rows.anchor: ZoomIn = search for potentially relevant structure ... Zero = test eliminability of represented structure. ... ZoomIn discovers and Zero tests.
rows.statement: Proposes Zoom-in and Zero as complementary operations relative to the same (Q,C,Pi,S): Zoom-in searches for potentially relevant structure (discovers), Zero tests eliminability of represented structure (tests); a candidate pipeline ZoomIn->ExpandedRepresentation->ZeroLens->RelevantSubspace->FactFinding is proposed but explicitly not assumed to be a fixed order, tagged [PROP] not axiom.

rows.anchor: projection to different observation field ... I would be careful. ... Unless we have pi^2=pi or an appropriate semantic projection definition, don't call every Zoom-in a projection. Use inquiry-relative view transformation ... or focus transformation.
rows.statement: Warns against calling every Zoom-in operation a mathematical 'projection' unless an established idempotent projection structure (pi^2=pi) or semantic-projection definition is demonstrated; recommends 'inquiry-relative view transformation' or 'focus transformation' as neutral terminology, consistent with the Zero Algebra lesson to discover the algebra rather than impose it.

rows.anchor: ZoomIn: Where should I investigate? EpistemicAgency: What should I do next? FactFinding: What does the evidence establish? ZoomOut: How does the finding change the broader state?
rows.statement: Separates four distinct research questions into a coherent architecture: ZoomIn (where should I investigate), Epistemic Agency (what should I do next), Fact Finding (what does the evidence establish), Zoom-out (how does the finding change the broader state), combined into Observation->Relevance->ZoomIn->DimensionDiscovery->FactFinding->Determination->ZoomOut->Integration->K_{t+1} with a feedback loop from DimensionDiscovery back to NewObservation->NewZoomIn.

rows.anchor: KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-2026-09 ... ZF1 -- Context preservation ... ZF2 -- Dimension expansion ... ZF3 -- Cross-boundary discovery ... ZF4 -- Determination dependence ... ZF5 -- Investigation != determination ... ZF6 -- Zoom-out integration ... ZF7 -- Resource/agency interaction
rows.statement: Specifies KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-2026-09 with seven candidate hypotheses: ZF1 ZoomIn(K_t,Q) does not imply Delete(K_t); ZF2 D_t subseteq D_{t+1} can occur through investigation; ZF3 a relevant dimension need not be contained in the initial observation's representation; ZF4 newly discovered dimensions can change Determine(Q); ZF5 ZoomIn != Determine; ZF6 a finding discovered during Zoom-in can modify the broader state; ZF7 the next investigated dimension depends on K,Q,Delta,Resources,Context,Contract,Risk.

experiment.hypothesis: ZF1-ZF7 as stated
experiment.setup: A Nexus-egress benchmark: initial state knows OS/RAM/Storage/Repositories/Network/Backup/CI-CD but does not explicitly expose GitLab Runner as the cause of 70GB/day egress; compare Restricted Zoom (only children of Egress) vs Inquiry Zoom (any plausibly explanatory dimension)
experiment.method: Measure D_discovered, Evidence_acquired, Hypotheses_generated, Determine_before vs Determine_after under the two zoom variants
experiment.limitations: Not yet executed; explicitly avoids repeating the flawed KR-ZOOM-OUT estimand design
experiment.conclusion: Recorded as [PROP][OPEN]; next step is to test whether Zoom-in is irreducible or a composition of Inquiry Formation + Dimension Discovery + Candidate Generation + Resource Selection + Traversal/Investigation

rows.anchor: Backup -> large transfer, GitLab Runner -> large transfer, Replication -> large transfer ... the system must not say I found GitLab Runner, therefore GitLab Runner is the cause. ... No Determination Without Alternative Space.
rows.statement: Uses a multi-cause Nexus-egress failure case (Backup, GitLab Runner, and Replication all plausibly producing large transfer) to argue against single-hypothesis-collapse ('I found X, therefore X is the cause'), requiring the full hypothesis set H_Q to undergo Evidence Assessment before Determination, stated as the principle 'No Determination Without Alternative Space.'

rows.anchor: O_t -> ZoomIn(K_t,O_t,Q) -> D_t subseteq D_{t+1} -> Acquire -> Assess -> Determine -> ZoomOut(Finding,K_t) -> K_{t+1} ... Terminology Correction: View Transformation vs. Projection
rows.statement: Formalizes a four-level Decoupled Dimensional Expansion & Integration Pipeline (1. Observation Entry O_t={d_0}; 2. Dimensional Discovery ZoomIn(K_t,O_t,Q)->D_t subseteq D_{t+1}; 3. Fact-Finding Acquire->Assess->Determine; 4. Integration ZoomOut(Finding,K_t)->K_{t+1}), and replaces the term 'projection' with 'Inquiry-Directed View Transformation' to avoid assuming idempotence (pi^2=pi) prior to empirical discovery.

lineage_claims.quote: Your analysis establishes a crucial architectural boundary ... This refinement directly addresses the failure modes observed in earlier Zoom experiments

rows.anchor: K_t <=_O Focus(K_t,Q) where <=_O means that the focused view does not make previously available contract-relevant observations unavailable. ... ZF1 -- Context Preservation: Zoom-In changes inquiry focus without itself removing or invalidating surrounding Knowledge State.
rows.statement: Corrects ZF1's undefined comparison ZoomIn(K_t,Q)!=Delete(K_t) to K_t<=_O Focus(K_t,Q), where <=_O means the focused view does not make previously available contract-relevant observations unavailable, avoiding accidentally turning Zoom-In into an undefined representation-theoretic operation.

rows.anchor: Discovery of a dimension != acceptance of that dimension into Knowledge State. ... exactly analogous to your existing Candidate != Determined != Knowledge. ... ZF2 -- Dimensional Expansion: Inquiry-directed investigation can introduce candidate explanatory dimensions not represented in the initial active representation.
rows.statement: Corrects ZF2's D_t subset D_{t+1} (which conflates dimension discovery with state evolution) by introducing D_t^cand as candidate dimensional space distinct from D_t^rep (accepted into Knowledge State), giving D_t^rep subseteq D_{t+1}^cand and a later integration D_{t+1}^cand -> D_{t+1}^rep, analogous to the existing Candidate != Determined != Knowledge chain.

rows.anchor: d* not-in Rep_active(O_t,K_t) AND d* in Discover(I_t) ... ZF3 currently risks becoming tautological ... GitLab Runner may already exist somewhere in the Knowledge Graph but not be connected to the egress observation. That is not dimensional discovery.
rows.statement: Corrects ZF3's under-specified d* not-in Rep(O_t) (risking tautology) by distinguishing not-observable-in-O_t, not-represented-in-K_t, and genuinely-discovered-during-investigation, requiring d* not-in Rep_active(O_t,K_t) AND d* in Discover(investigation trace I_t), noting a dimension already present elsewhere in the graph but unconnected to the observation does not count as dimensional discovery.

rows.anchor: Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) != Determine(K'_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) with K'_t = Expand(K_t,d*). ... Otherwise a change in determination could simply result from changing standards, evidence, inquiry, or reasoning regime.
rows.statement: Corrects ZF4 (Determine(Q|D_t)!=Determine(Q|D')) to hold the full determination signature Q,C,EC,S,R fixed and intervene only on the discovered dimensional representation, giving Determine(K_t,...)!=Determine(K'_t,...) with K'_t=Expand(K_t,d*), so the change is attributable to dimensional expansion alone rather than confounded with standards/evidence/inquiry/reasoning-regime changes.

rows.anchor: A Zoom-In that discovers ... has succeeded even if Fact-Finding concludes: Cause remains underdetermined. So: DiscoverySuccess not-implies Determination should probably become a candidate invariant.
rows.statement: Retains and operationally sharpens ZF5 (ZoomIn:(K_t,O_t,Q)->D^cand versus FactFinding:(D^cand,E,H_Q,M,S)->Standing->Determination), proposing the candidate invariant DiscoverySuccess does not imply Determination: Zoom-In can succeed in surfacing candidates even when Fact-Finding concludes the cause remains underdetermined.

rows.anchor: ZoomOut should not be defined as ZoomOut(ZoomIn(K_t))=K_t. That would recreate the old restoration model. Instead: ZoomOut(F,K_t) = Integrate(K_t,F) -> K_{t+1} ... ZoomOut = integration of finding rather than: ZoomOut = inverse(ZoomIn).
rows.statement: Explicitly forbids defining Zoom-Out as the inverse of Zoom-In (ZoomOut(ZoomIn(K_t))=K_t would recreate the old restoration model); Zoom-Out is Integrate(K_t,F)->K_{t+1} where F may contain newly discovered dimensions, assessed evidence, determined relationships, rejected hypotheses, unresolved alternatives, provenance, and temporal information, so K_{t+1}!=K_t may occur even though Zoom-In itself deleted nothing.

rows.anchor: d* in ArgMax_{d in D^cand} E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d) as a candidate agency policy, not a kernel law. ... ZoomIn != Agency. Agency selects the next investigation; Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus.
rows.statement: Corrects ZF7's dimension-selection formula (which assumed Adeq is measurable, candidate dimensions are comparably valued, costs are scalarizable, and an argmax exists) to an explicitly candidate agency policy d* in ArgMax_{d}E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d), not a kernel law, reaffirming ZoomIn != Agency (Agency selects the next investigation, Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus).
missing: validated measurability of Adeq and comparability of candidate dimensions

assumptions.statement: Adeq is measurable, candidate dimensions have comparable expected value, costs are scalarizable, argmax exists
assumptions.anchor: But it assumes: Adeq is measurable, candidate dimensions have comparable expected value, costs are scalarizable, an argmax exists.

rows.anchor: ZF8 -- Representation Boundary Non-Closure ... An initial observation representation must not be assumed to contain all relevant explanatory dimensions. ... ZF3 asks: Can the relevant dimension cross the initial boundary? ZF8 asks: Is the initial dimensional representation itself epistemically non-closed?
rows.statement: Adds ZF8 (Representation Boundary Non-Closure): the initial observation representation must not be assumed to contain all relevant explanatory dimensions, distinguished from ZF3 (can a relevant dimension cross the boundary) by asking instead whether the initial representation is itself epistemically non-closed.

rows.anchor: Zoom-In != Zero != Fact-Finding ... Determination ... Zoom-Out ... Epistemic Agency ... This is much more promising than trying to make Zoom-In or Zoom-Out kernel primitives.
rows.statement: States a six-way functional separation as the architectural conclusion: Zoom-In (expand/search the inquiry space) != Zero Lens (determine what can be eliminated while preserving contract) != Fact-Finding (establish what evidence supports) != Determination (establish what can be decided under the epistemic regime) != Zoom-Out (integrate finding into broader state) != Epistemic Agency (select what to investigate/do next); recommends testing ZF2+ZF3+ZF5 first as the foundational experiment before the rest of the architecture is tested.

rows.anchor: NewDimension -> Reinterpretation(ExistingRepresentation). So dimensional expansion is not merely adding nodes. It can change the meaning of existing nodes and relations.
rows.statement: Extends ZF2-style dimensional expansion (D^cand_{t+1} superseteq D^cand_t) with the stronger claim that a newly introduced dimension can reinterpret existing representation, NewDimension -> Reinterpretation(ExistingRepresentation), so dimensional expansion is not merely adding nodes but can change the meaning of existing nodes and relations.

rows.anchor: Do not modify KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01. Run the locked experiment first for ZF2, ZF3, ZF5. Then ... create: KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-02 ... Can inquiry-directed fact-finding detect and repair an inadequate or misframed inquiry, rather than merely search for additional facts under the original question?
rows.statement: Recommends not modifying the already-locked KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01 (run it first for ZF2/ZF3/ZF5), and instead creating a follow-on artifact KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-02 asking whether inquiry-directed fact-finding can detect and repair an inadequate or misframed inquiry rather than merely search for additional facts under the original question, extending 'Dimension Discovery' to 'Inquiry Discovery' and 'Fact Finding' to 'Fact Finding Completion = Evidence Sufficiency + Inquiry Adequacy + Determination Boundary'.

rows.anchor: Arm A (Structural Control) Restricted Graph Expansion ... Arm B (Inquiry Zoom-In) Inquiry-Directed Expansion ... 2x2 ZF5 OUTCOME MATRIX ... Case B: Discovery Witness [CRITICAL]
rows.statement: Locks KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01-2026-09 as a two-arm experimental protocol (Arm A: restricted graph expansion within the active representation; Arm B: inquiry-directed ZoomIn(K_t,O_t,Q0) producing a candidate dimension set), over N>=100 simulated system anomalies centered on the Nexus 70GB/day egress profile, with a 2x2 outcome matrix crossing {dimension discovered, no new dimension} x {determined, not determined}, where Case B (dimension discovered but not determined) is the mandatory critical witness for ZF5.

lineage_claims.quote: The formulation is locked ... Below is the concrete, execution-ready Experimental Protocol Artifact KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01-2026-09

experiment.hypothesis: ZF2 (candidate dimensions genuinely new), ZF3 (cross-boundary discovery), ZF5 (discovery is independent of determination), with ZF1 as a hard preservation control
experiment.setup: N>=100 simulated system anomalies; two arms (restricted vs inquiry-directed traversal); pre-registered outcome classification into Cases A-D
experiment.inputs: Simulated Nexus-egress-style anomaly scenarios with incomplete/noisy evidence logs for Case-B guarantee
experiment.method: Five-step pipeline: baseline snapshot, execute both arms, ZF1 preservation check, fact-finding execution, outcome classification
experiment.limitations: Population conditioned on initial underdetermination; cannot establish Zoom-In is universally necessary, a kernel primitive, or that Zoom-Out is its inverse
experiment.conclusion: READY FOR FREEZE pending the ZF2 metric fix and ZF5 criterion split

rows.anchor: ZF2 metric has a type problem ... A positive difference in cardinality does not establish that new dimensions were discovered. ... Delta D_new = |D^cand_{t+1} \ D^represented_t| ... ZF2 witness iff Delta D_new > 0.
rows.statement: Corrects the ZF2 metric Delta N=|D^cand_{t+1}|-|D^represented_t| (a type problem, since the candidate set could re-contain already-known dimensions and a positive cardinality difference would not prove new discovery) to the set-difference Delta D_new=|D^cand_{t+1} \ D^represented_t|, with the witness condition ZF2 iff Delta D_new>0, aligning it with ZF3's definition; Delta N may be retained only as a descriptive metric.

rows.anchor: CaseB>0 and P(Determine|Discovery)>P(Determine|No). These are actually two different claims. ... ZF5 is supported if a non-zero number of valid Case-B witnesses occurs under the preregistered conditions. Then report the conditional determination rates separately as descriptive/secondary evidence.
rows.statement: Splits the ZF5 success criterion into two logically distinct claims that had been conflated: the required logical-separation witness (Case B count>0, establishing Discovery does not imply Determination) versus a merely comparative, non-necessary association claim (P(Determine|Discovery)>P(Determine|No)) which could fail even when ZF5 holds; recommends treating only the Case-B-count criterion as the ZF5 pass/fail condition, reporting the comparative rate as separate descriptive evidence.

rows.anchor: your population is conditioned on initial underdetermination ... The experiment studies inquiry-directed discovery from initially underdetermined observations. It therefore cannot establish that Zoom-In is necessary for all observations.
rows.statement: Flags that requiring Determine(K_t^pre,Q0)=UNDERDETERMINED at Step 1 conditions the experimental population on initial underdetermination, which must be stated explicitly as scope: the experiment studies inquiry-directed discovery from initially underdetermined observations and cannot establish Zoom-In's necessity for all observations.

rows.anchor: Class Reachability != Estimand Nondegeneracy != Estimand Adequacy ... add an explicit estimand non-degeneracy gate before execution ... use the already accepted O-F* rule rather than inventing a new methodology.
rows.statement: Requires applying the existing O-F* estimand-nondegeneracy gate to every declared variable quantity (Delta D_new, ZF3 witness indicator, Case-B indicator, determination outcome, preservation outcome) before execution, restating Class Reachability != Estimand Nondegeneracy != Estimand Adequacy and explicitly reusing the already-accepted O-F* rule rather than inventing a new methodology.
invariants: Class Reachability != Estimand Nondegeneracy != Estimand Adequacy

lineage_claims.quote: add an explicit estimand non-degeneracy gate before execution ... use the already accepted O-F* rule

rows.anchor: Candidate discovered != Candidate supported != Candidate determined. That is exactly the separation your KnowledgeOS theory has been building toward.
rows.statement: Restates the three-way separation Candidate discovered != Candidate supported != Candidate determined as the epistemic backbone the Case-B benchmark cleanly exercises (70GB/day egress -> Zoom-In discovers GitLab Runner/Backup/Replication/CI-CD -> Fact-Finding finds insufficient evidence -> UNDERDETERMINED).
invariants: Candidate discovered != Candidate supported != Candidate determined

rows.anchor: What the experiment cannot yet establish: that Zoom-In is a kernel primitive; that Zoom-In is universally necessary; that Zoom-Out is its inverse; that dimensional expansion improves knowledge; that discovery causes determination; that Zoom-In is generally optimal; that the dimensional space D* is literally infinite.
rows.statement: Enumerates the explicit epistemic scope boundary of the frozen KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01-2026-09 protocol: it cannot establish Zoom-In as a kernel primitive, as universally necessary, that Zoom-Out is its inverse, that dimensional expansion improves knowledge, that discovery causes determination, that Zoom-In is generally optimal, or that D* is literally infinite -- explicitly no Theory v1.3, no kernel modification, no operator canonization from this experiment.

rows.anchor: ZoomIn approx Issue Refinement -- not as an identity, but as a research hypothesis. ... questioning actions ... do not themselves give information immediately; they raise/manage issues ... almost exactly our ZF5: ZoomIn != FactFinding
rows.statement: Proposes ZoomIn approx Issue Refinement as a research hypothesis (not identity), and reports that the thesis's characterization of questioning actions as knowledge-seeking actions that do not themselves supply information gives an external theoretical analogue for the already-adopted ZF5 (ZoomIn != FactFinding) and DiscoverySuccess does not imply Determination.

rows.anchor: context of discovery ... context of the final product ... Value(E | Discovery) != Value(E | FinalState). ... A clue that is enormously valuable while searching can become redundant after determination.
rows.statement: Extracts Kusch's context-of-discovery vs context-of-final-product distinction, proposing that evidence value can depend on the stage of inquiry, Value(E|Discovery) != Value(E|FinalState), so KnowledgeOS should not treat evidence as having a timeless scalar value -- directly relevant to Fact-Finding and Zoom-In.

rows.anchor: Model Adequacy != Model Factivity ... InformationLoss not-implies UnderstandingLoss. But also UnderstandingGain not-implies KnowledgeGain. This is potentially very important for Zoom-Out and Representation Reduction.
rows.statement: Extracts Elgin's idealization argument into Model Adequacy != Model Factivity, giving InformationLoss does not imply UnderstandingLoss and (conversely) UnderstandingGain does not imply KnowledgeGain, flagged as important for Zoom-Out and Representation Reduction since a simplified model can omit reality yet increase understanding.

rows.anchor: we will use EA-2 (Outcome vs. Process) and EA-3 (Luck vs. Control) as qualitative evaluation filters to verify whether successful state determinations were achieved through controlled candidate expansion or ungrounded traversal heuristics.
rows.statement: States an immediate operational directive: the registration of KR-EPISTEMIC-ACHIEVEMENT-LENS-09 leaves Theory v1.2 and the active KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01 protocol untouched, and EA-2/EA-3 will be used only as post-execution qualitative evaluation filters (controlled candidate expansion vs ungrounded traversal heuristics) rather than modifying the frozen experimental design.

rows.anchor: Cross-Boundary Role Discovery ... versus New Dimension Discovery. Those are not the same experiment. ... Type 1 -- New entity/dimension ... Type 2 -- Existing entity, new epistemic role ... Type 3 -- New relation ... the fact finding may actually discover relational structure, not a new dimension.
rows.statement: Refines ZF2/ZF3's binary discovery test into three distinct possible outcomes for the KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01 experiment: Type 1 new entity/dimension (d not-in K_t -> d in D^cand); Type 2 existing entity gaining a new epistemic role (Role_t(d|Q)=Peripheral -> Role_{t+1}(d|Q)=Focus); Type 3 new relation activated between already-known entities (Relation(d1,d2) newly instantiated), illustrated by GitLabRunner->DockerPull->Repository->Network->70GB/day being a relational discovery rather than a new-dimension discovery.

rows.anchor: the immediate priority remains the already-authorized KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01: determine whether the original ZF2/ZF3/ZF5 experiment actually detects dimension discovery, relational discovery, or merely traversal behavior. That distinction should be an adjudication issue for the existing experiment, not a reason to alter its frozen protocol.
rows.statement: Concludes that the Sher-derived Type-1/2/3 discovery typology should be used as a post-execution adjudication lens for the already-frozen KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01 protocol (distinguishing dimension discovery, relational discovery, or mere traversal behavior in the results) rather than as grounds to alter the frozen experimental design; registers KR-EPISTEMIC-FRICTION-LENS-2026-09 (FR-A Epistemic Freedom, FR-B Epistemic Friction, FR-C Dynamic Epistemic Roles, FR-D Structured Holism) in the master governance ledger alongside the other external lenses.

rows.anchor: soft announcements that cut epistemic links while keeping the whole model available for further reference ... contrasted with eliminative announcements. ... Focus != Delete ... Inquiry transformation != Knowledge destruction.
rows.statement: Extracts the thesis's 'soft announcement' operator (cuts epistemic links while keeping the whole model available, contrasted with eliminative announcements) as an established formal precedent closely resembling the corpus's own ZF1 (Focus != Delete, Inquiry transformation != Knowledge destruction), explicitly not treated as proof of ZF1 within KnowledgeOS.

rows.anchor: I_t = <Q_t, approx_t, D_t^cand, S_t^source, A_t> ... Factivity Separation: I_t carries no truth assertions ... Non-Destructive Focus: Focus(I_t,w) not-implies w not-in K_t ... State Evolution Autonomy: Delta I_t != empty not-implies Delta K_t != empty (Question Raised not-implies Knowledge Acquired).
rows.statement: Formalizes the candidate Inquiry State schema I_t=(Q_t,approx_t,D_t^cand,S_t^source,A_t) (active question DAG with per-question id/target/status/priority; issue-partitioning relation approx_t over states; candidate dimension set; source-dependency map; inquiry agenda/history) with three explicit separation rules: Factivity Separation (I_t carries no truth assertions), Non-Destructive Focus (focusing does not remove states from K_t), and State Evolution Autonomy (Delta I_t!=empty does not imply Delta K_t!=empty), giving ZF5 a clean formal witness Delta I_t!=empty AND Delta K_t=empty.
invariants: Focus does not imply removal from K_t
Delta I_t != empty does not imply Delta K_t != empty

rows.anchor: Questioning != Answering != Resolution which translates very naturally into: ZoomIn != FactFinding != Determination. This is one of the strongest external correspondences we have found so far. But it remains [EXT] -> [PROP], not [PROVED].
rows.statement: States that Minica's Questioning != Answering != Resolution translates naturally into ZoomIn != FactFinding != Determination, describing it as the strongest external correspondence found so far for ZF5, explicitly kept at [EXT]->[PROP], not [PROVED]; separately notes Issue Refinement != Information Elimination reinforces the triad ZoomIn != Zero != FactFinding.

rows.anchor: A. Inquiry expansion J_t -> J_{t+1} 'What should we investigate?' B. Candidate expansion H_t -> H_{t+1} 'What explanations become candidates?' C. Knowledge expansion K_t -> K_{t+1} 'What has actually become epistemically established?' These are not the same.
rows.statement: Refines the ZF2/ZF3 'dimension discovery' test into three distinct expansion events: A. Inquiry expansion (J_t->J_{t+1}, what should we investigate), B. Candidate expansion (H_t->H_{t+1}, what explanations become candidates), C. Knowledge expansion (K_t->K_{t+1}, what is actually epistemically established), explicitly stated as not the same and described as the most important architectural insight the book gives for the current Zoom-In work.

rows.anchor: Knowledge Representation != Inquiry Operation. ... The underlying knowledge structure doesn't necessarily change merely because a new epistemic operation is applied. ... That aligns strongly with your Zoom-In discovery idea.
rows.statement: Compares GoF's Visitor pattern (representing an operation over elements of an object structure without changing the element classes) to the hypothesis Knowledge Representation != Inquiry Operation, illustrated by multiple investigations (root-cause, compliance, cost, security) applying to the same knowledge structure {Network,Backup,Repository,CI/CD,Security} without necessarily changing it, reinforcing the corpus's own Zoom-In-as-discovery-without-mutating-K_t architecture.

rows.anchor: ZoomIn != Memento. ... Memento asks: Can we preserve a previous state and restore it later? Your Zoom-In asks: Can we focus inquiry without destroying the surrounding epistemic state? These are not the same problem. ... This actually reinforces your earlier conclusion: ZoomOut != inverse(ZoomIn).
rows.statement: Compares GoF's Memento (preserve and later restore a previous state without exposing internal representation) to Zoom-In's preservation requirement K_t^pre <=_O K_t^focus, concluding ZoomIn != Memento since restoration and non-destructive focus are different problems, and reports this comparison as independent architectural support (via a different external lens) for the already-established ZoomOut != inverse(ZoomIn) finding.

rows.anchor: a cross-boundary traversal ... Egress -> Network -> CI/CD -> Runner -> Caching -> Repository -> Replication. ... GoF gives us a mature design vocabulary for investigating whether such traversal is: structural traversal, visitor-like operation, strategy selection, chain-of-responsibility, or something genuinely new.
rows.statement: Uses GoF's Composite pattern (part-whole hierarchies, often paired with Iterator/Visitor) and a nested Nexus knowledge structure (System/Network/CI-CD/Repository with sub-nodes) to illustrate that ZoomIn's ZF3 cross-boundary traversal (a candidate dimension crossing from Egress through Network, CI/CD, Runner, Caching, Repository, Replication) is not simply 'walk deeper in the tree' but a cross-boundary traversal, and that GoF's vocabulary can help determine whether such traversal is structural traversal, visitor-like, strategy selection, chain-of-responsibility, or genuinely new.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition
rows.statement: Central hypothesis: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition, not merely the smallest unit that stores knowledge. Kernel = (State, Transition Capability): the state is what the kernel currently holds, the transition capability determines what can legitimately happen to that state. Gita lens (analytical, not DDD names): Mind -> evolving epistemic state, Buddhi -> discriminative capability, Karma -> action/transition, Phala -> resulting state/outcome.
dependencies: K_t knowledge state at time t

rows.anchor: K = (K_t,\Omega_K)
rows.statement: Candidate kernel K=(K_t,Omega_K) with 11 candidate operations, each carrying a load-bearing distinction: (1) Observe(O_t) with O_t != K_t (observation is not automatically knowledge, preserving W->O->E and Qualify); (2) Discriminate(K_t,O_t)->{d_1..d_n} = the Buddhi operation, meaning 'distinguish', not yet 'decide truth'; (3) Qualify(x,E,C,t,Pi), the G1 unresolved operation, whose result may be {admit,reject,defer,qualify} rather than binary {true,false}; (4) Incorporate: K_{t+1}=Incorporate(K_t,p), a state transformation not simple insertion; (5) Reject(K_t,p) with Reject != Prove False (a proposition can be rejected as insufficiently qualified without being established false); (6) Contradict: recognizing p _|_ q via the corpus's Relation primitive; (7) Revise(K_t,p,E) for evidence-conflicting knowledge, with explicit warning not to import AGM revision theory merely because it exists, per Step 287; (8) Supersede: p_1 supersedes p_2 while preserving lineage; (9) Recall(K_t,h)/Remember distinguishing currently-known from historically-known, with K_t != H_K (history of states/transitions); (10) Withdraw(p): K_t -> K_{t+1} with withdraw != delete history (the historical fact of having held it may remain, important for auditability); (11) Act/Transform(a), external to the epistemic state per Command != Transformation != Result and Step 285's finding that Action, Event, Policy were external to the verification projection.
dependencies: Step 287 warning against importing AGM revision theory

lineage_claims.target: Step 287 AGM warning; Step 285 externality finding

rows.anchor: \delta:(K_t,O_t,C_t)\rightarrow K_{t+1} ... only when the transition satisfies the kernel's invariants
rows.statement: The kernel should not be an unrestricted machine: reject delta:KxO->K as an unrestricted transition function; instead delta:(K_t,O_t,C_t)->K_{t+1} only when the transition satisfies the kernel's invariants. Kernel operation = candidate transition + discrimination + qualification + state transition, subject to constraints. Motivated by the 'mind can become its own enemy' observation made mathematically useful.
invariants: I(K_t,omega,K_{t+1}) = true required for any transition

assumptions.statement: Accept/Reject/Revise/Supersede can be composed from Discriminate+Qualify+Transition

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel: the smallest bounded epistemic mechanism that maintains a time-indexed knowledge state and can discriminate and perform legitimate transitions of that state under the applicable constraints.
rows.statement: Provisional formal kernel definition: K = (K_t, Omega_K, I) where K_t = current knowledge state, Omega_K = permitted kernel operations, I = kernel invariants; K_t --omega in Omega_K--> K_{t+1} only if I(K_t,omega,K_{t+1})=true. Gita gives only the philosophical lens Mind~Kernel, Buddhi~discriminative capability; the mathematical/DDD investigation determines the actual kernel. Key research hypothesis: Kernel != Knowledge Store, but potentially Kernel = Epistemic State + Discrimination + Legitimate State Transition.

rows.anchor: Step 291 — KnowledgeOS Kernel and Operation Algebra
rows.statement: Proposes next research step 'Step 291 -- KnowledgeOS Kernel and Operation Algebra' with 12 questions: minimal kernel definition; whether K_t is the kernel state or the kernel holds additional state; minimal Omega_K; which operations are genuinely epistemic vs belong outside (Governance, Authority, Action, Replay); whether Discriminate is primitive or composite; what Qualify consumes/produces; whether every legitimate K_t->K_{t+1} transition can be classified; determinism of the transition; which invariants must never be violated; whether the operation algebra can be proven minimal; which parts are independently derivable vs merely Gita-correspondences.

rows.anchor: B(K_t,x)\rightarrow d ... d \in \{\text{supported},\text{refuted},\text{contradictory},\text{unknown},\text{unqualified},\text{inadmissible}\}
rows.statement: Mathematical correction to 'the kernel should always be busy determining right and wrong': right/wrong should not initially be binary. Buddhi should implement a discrimination function B(K_t,x) -> d with d in {supported, refuted, contradictory, unknown, unqualified, inadmissible}, not a Boolean truth oracle. Hence Buddhi = epistemic discrimination, not Buddhi = truth; the kernel does not create truth, it evaluates what can legitimately be concluded from its current state and evidence.

lineage_claims.target: 'kernel always busy determining right and wrong' statement
lineage_claims.quote: I would make one mathematical correction.

rows.anchor: \mathcal B: (K_t,O_t,E_t,C_t) \rightarrow D_t
rows.statement: Proposes B:(K_t,O_t,E_t,C_t)->D_t (discrimination/decision result), enumerating what B must do: distinguish, compare, validate, detect contradiction, assess evidence, qualify, reject, accept, defer, update the knowledge state, preserve provenance, determine what remains unknown. Central hypothesis: KnowledgeOS Kernel ~philosophically~ Mind; Buddhi ~philosophically~ Kernel's discrimination capability; K_t = changing Knowledge State; K (calligraphic) = Knowledge Space. Four-level picture: Knowledge Space K -> Knowledge State K_t -> KnowledgeOS Kernel -> Buddhi -> epistemic operations -> K_{t+1}. Explicitly marked as hypothesis pending testing against actual Gita passages and the existing KnowledgeOS corpus, not yet canonical.
missing: formal semantics of each of the 12 sub-functions

rows.anchor: \mathcal K \overset{\Omega}{\longrightarrow} O_t \overset{\mathcal B}{\longrightarrow} D_t \overset{\delta}{\longrightarrow} K_{t+1}
rows.statement: The central kernel question evolves from 'what operations does the Kernel perform?' to 'what can a bounded KnowledgeOS Kernel legitimately know, observe, discriminate, and conclude about a knowledge space larger than its current state?'. Final research-model pipeline: K (Knowledge Space) --Omega (observation/projection)--> O_t (observation) --B (Buddhi/discrimination)--> D_t (discrimination result) --delta (state transition)--> K_{t+1} (new Knowledge State). Explicitly not yet canonical architecture; identifies convergence of existing open questions about Observation, Proposition, State, Event, Buddhi, Qualify, delta, and the five-axis Sigma.

rows.anchor: Can the existing KnowledgeOS eight primitives and the five-axis \Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) express the proposed Mind–Buddhi–Kernel behavior without introducing a new primitive?
rows.statement: Proposes pausing philosophical interpretation after Chapter 12 to test mathematically: can the existing eight primitives and five-axis Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) express the proposed Mind-Buddhi-Kernel behavior without a new primitive? Specifically test whether Buddhi = an operation over existing primitives, Mind = a state/orientation over existing primitives, and Kernel = (K_t, operations, invariants, transition rules) -- framed as the first real mathematical/DDD test of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel = Mind' interpretation.

rows.anchor: E_d(K_t)=K_{t+1} ... R_d(K_t)=K_{t+1} ... C(K_t,o)=K_{t+1} ... X(K_t)\rightarrow \text{conflict-qualified state} ... Z(K_t)\rightarrow G_t
rows.statement: Six candidate (not canonical) operators: E (Expansion) discovers a new relevant dimension d not-in D_t, now in D_{t+1}; R_d (Refinement) improves an existing dimension, v_t(d) prec_d v_{t+1}(d); C (Correction) changes an existing value because new evidence shows the previous state was wrong -- explicitly Purification != monotonic accumulation, since a purified state may contain less due to removed erroneous knowledge; X (Contradiction resolution) given p and not-p, the kernel must not arbitrarily select one, producing a conflict-qualified state until Buddhi/evidence/qualification can discriminate; Q (Qualification), the unresolved G1 operator, determining sufficient justification for the intended epistemic purpose, reframed via the recent Cavell-derived reconsideration so purification can mean correctly recognizing a gap cannot currently be resolved rather than resolving it; Z (Zero detection) detects epistemic absence, Z(K_t)->G_t (recognized gaps), with G_t transformable via E,R,C,Q into G_{t+1} -- the system becomes more purified partly by knowing more accurately what it does not know.

rows.anchor: \{\operatorname{Discriminate},\ \operatorname{Qualify},\ \operatorname{Transition}\}\ \cong\ \{\equiv,\ G1,\ \delta\}
rows.statement: The philosophically-proposed minimal kernel algebra Omega_K={Discriminate,Qualify,Transition} (from S2219, the kernel-definition-from-evidence-maths-DDD file) maps exactly onto the formal lane's independently-established blockers: Discriminate = the equality/distinguishability relation equiv (the unique minimal cycle cut per Steps 289/291, unique over both graph universes); Qualify = the corpus's own Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence, i.e. G1, named/typed/no body, irreducible; Transition = K_t --delta--> K_{t+1}, i.e. delta, commit case unspecifiable, executed as K1 is K0. This is a genuine independent arrival (derived from 'what must a kernel be able to do', not from the dependency graph, 261.23, or the G1 register) but a NEGATIVE convergence: it solves none of the three, and is a restatement of the blocker set, not a kernel. Registered as new gap G-90 (derived, raises confidence, closes nothing). Sharp consequence stated: any minimal kernel algebra containing Qualify inherits G1 -- since Qualify is the one irreducible gap, a genuinely minimal kernel cannot be closed without closing G1.

lineage_claims.target: S2219's Omega_K={Discriminate,Qualify,Transition} proposal and the formal blocker set {equiv,G1,delta}
lineage_claims.quote: EXACTLY the three blockers the formal lane reached by a different route.

rows.anchor: A correctly shaped triple whose three components are EXACTLY the three open items. It states the problem well. It populates nothing.
rows.statement: Tests the proposed kernel shape K=(K_t,Omega_K,I) slot by slot against the formal lane: K_t (the state) is OPEN (per Step 285; 258.35 says it may not be a tuple at all); Omega_K (permitted operations) is OPEN (N-4 mandatory membership open, 0 of 22 operations has a body/identity/ratification per 291); I (invariants) has 0 of 7 established (per REFINED-STEP-287-INVARIANTS), and I is downstream of equiv in 261.30's chain. Conclusion: a correctly-shaped triple whose three components are exactly the three open items -- a well-posed problem statement, not progress toward closure; must not be mistaken for populating the kernel (per 291's 'shape -> content requires a derivation, and none exists').

rows.anchor: 1. Perceive / receive ... 5. Orient
rows.statement: Proposes the KnowledgeOS kernel may need five fundamentally different classes of work: (1) Perceive/receive O_t; (2) Represent O_t->K_t; (3) Discriminate B_t(K_t,O_t)->d_t; (4) Transform delta(K_t,d_t)->K_{t+1}; (5) Orient rho_t(K_t,Omega). The fifth (Orient) is said to become much more visible once Chapter 11 (the horizon Omega) is added to the model.

rows.anchor: \Omega = \{ Observe,\; Discriminate,\; Relate,\; Validate,\; Qualify,\; Transform,\; Reject,\; Accept,\; Revise \}
rows.statement: Candidate (non-canonical) operator family from Chapters 10-15 combined: Omega={Observe, Discriminate, Relate, Validate, Qualify, Transform, Reject, Accept, Revise}, with Buddhi approx delta as the mechanism selecting/executing several of these, e.g. delta(Observation,Context)->Decision and delta(K_t,E_t)->K_{t+1}, connecting to the unresolved Qualify problem from Steps 285-287.

rows.anchor: \mathcal K \neq K_t \neq \mathcal M
rows.statement: Formal first principle: K (Knowledge Space, potentially unbounded) != K_t (Knowledge State at time t, what the system currently represents) != M (KnowledgeOS Kernel, the smallest persistent computational unit that evaluates and transforms knowledge states). The Gita's language helps interpret M as Mind, but the software kernel is not literally the philosophical mind. Defines M = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition, i.e. capable of K_t->K_{t+1} under some evidence/observation/proposition/event/operation.

rows.anchor: Z:\boxed{K_t\rightarrow G_t} ... \delta: \boxed{(K_t,G_t,E_t,C_t)\rightarrow D_t} ... \tau: \boxed{(K_t,D_t)\rightarrow K_{t+1}}
rows.statement: Full typed operator pipeline: Z:K_t->G_t (gap/boundary discovery, internal inspection); delta:(K_t,G_t,E_t,C_t)->D_t (discrimination/Buddhi, taking gaps, evidence, and context); tau:(K_t,D_t)->K_{t+1} (transition/transformation). Composition tau o delta o Z is type-correct given matching interfaces; for external input f_x(K_t)=tau(K_t,delta(x,E,C)); for internally discovered gaps f_Z(K_t)=tau(K_t,delta(Z(K_t))). The kernel therefore performs two fundamentally different activities: external epistemic input (x->delta) and internal epistemic inspection (K_t--Z-->G_t).

rows.anchor: Level 0 — Primitive kernel mechanisms ... Level 1 — epistemic operations ... Level 2 — higher-order processes
rows.statement: Proposes a three-level operator hierarchy to address the concern that not all candidate operators should be primitive: Level 0 primitives {delta,Z,tau} (smallest candidates); Level 1 epistemic operations built from primitives (Observe, Compare, Validate, Qualify, Revise, Accept, Reject), e.g. Accept(x)=tau(K_t,delta(x,E,C)=accepted), Reject(x)=tau(K_t,delta(x,E,C)=rejected); Level 2 higher-order processes as compositions (Purification, Learning, Investigation, Knowledge evolution), P = O_1 o O_2 o ... o O_n, assessed as important for DDD (avoiding conflating primitive operations with their compositions).

rows.anchor: \mathcal M=(Q,\mathbb O,\delta,\tau,\mathbb I)
rows.statement: Proposes formalizing the kernel as a state machine M=(Q,O,delta,tau,I) where Q=kernel control states (renamed from S to avoid collision with Sigma's S axis), O=kernel operations, delta=discrimination function, tau=transition function, I=invariants. Also proposes the kernel invariant M != K_t must hold (otherwise K_t->K_{t+1} would mean the kernel becomes a different object every time); formalized as Identity(M_t)=Identity(M_{t+1}) while K_t != K_{t+1} is permitted -- 'persistent kernel identity + mutable epistemic state' proposed as a fundamental candidate architectural invariant, worth testing against the corpus.

rows.anchor: Qualify: X\rightarrow \{Qualified,\;Unqualified,\;Terminated\} ... Kernel determines the admissible epistemic status of a state transition.
rows.statement: Refines Qualify (still classified G1) via the Cavell insight (justification may legitimately terminate rather than being infinitely extended) into Qualify:X->{Qualified, Unqualified, Terminated}, rather than assuming qualification is always a total true/false decision -- candidate only. Reframes the kernel's deeper job away from 'determine truth' toward 'Kernel determines the admissible epistemic status of a state transition', assessed as much closer to what the corpus actually supports; enumerates the kernel's operative questions (what do we have, what evidence supports it, what is missing, what conflicts, what relationship exists, what can legitimately be concluded, where must qualification stop, what state transition is admissible).

rows.anchor: Knowledge quantity \neq Knowledge quality ... Purification \neq accumulation
rows.statement: Refines purification: P:Sigma_t->Sigma_{t+1} must not assume P(Sigma_t)>Sigma_t (per Step 287's finding that axes lack fully declared orders); instead a desired property Q(Sigma_{t+1})>=Q(Sigma_t) is wanted where Q is a future epistemic-quality functional that does not yet exist (an important research gap). Illustrates via example that K_1={1000 unsupported claims} could contain more information than K_2={100 well-supported claims} yet K_2 may be epistemically superior -- so Knowledge quantity != Knowledge quality, and Purification != accumulation; the kernel should maximize epistemic adequacy, not raw knowledge.
missing: formal definition of the epistemic-quality functional Q

rows.anchor: \mathcal K_{\text{kernel}} = (K_t,\;B_t,\;Z_t,\;Q_t,\;\delta_t)
rows.statement: Proposes candidate kernel tuple K_kernel=(K_t,B_t,Z_t,Q_t,delta_t) [current knowledge state, Buddhi discrimination/transformation capability, Zero explicit epistemic boundary/gap detection, qualification state/justification boundary, state transition], with O_t --Qualify--> K_t externally and K_t --B_t--> K_{t+1} -- explicitly not yet canonical, the strongest candidate architecture emerging from the philosophical analysis so far. Reframes the research question from 'what is the KnowledgeOS kernel' to 'what must a kernel be capable of doing to prevent knowledge from becoming distorted while transforming state over time', proposing Kernel = State + Discrimination + Qualification + Boundary Detection + State Transformation, and a next step of deriving a minimal algebra of kernel operations (observe, discriminate, qualify, accept, reject, retain, revise, discover-gap, transform) tested against the eight primitives and five-axis Sigma.

rows.anchor: K_{t+1} = \delta \left( Q \left( B \left( M(O_t,K_t) \right) \right), K_t \right)
rows.statement: Consolidated candidate kernel tuple K=(K_t,M,B,Q,Z,delta) with status column (K_t established corpus concept; M Manas-like representation, philosophical hypothesis; B Buddhi/discrimination, strong hypothesis; Q qualification, existing unresolved architecture gap; Z explicit epistemic boundary/gap, strong Zero correspondence; delta state transition, existing formal direction, commit case still incomplete), yielding one central candidate kernel equation K_{t+1} = delta(Q(B(M(O_t,K_t))), K_t) -- explicitly candidate only, but assessed as testable.
missing: formal definitions of M, B, Q individually

rows.anchor: O_S=\{Observe,Compare,Discriminate,Corroborate,Qualify,Resolve,Validate\} ... O_R=\{Search,Acquire,Transform,Investigate,Generate,Execute\} ... O_T=\{DetectBlock,ExposeUnknown,Suspend,Flag,Invalidate,RequestEvidence\}
rows.statement: Proposes mode-dependent admissible operator sets O_{M_t} subset O = full operator set: O_S (Sattva, clarification/discrimination mode) = {Observe,Compare,Discriminate,Corroborate,Qualify,Resolve,Validate}; O_R (Rajas, activity/acquisition mode) = {Search,Acquire,Transform,Investigate,Generate,Execute}; O_T (Tamas, obscuration mode) = diagnostic operators {DetectBlock,ExposeUnknown,Suspend,Flag,Invalidate,RequestEvidence}, not productive operators. Warns Rajas is not inherently bad (a system with zero Rajas would never investigate anything); the problem is uncontrolled Rajas (activity does not imply knowledge) -- 'more operations do not necessarily produce more knowledge'.

rows.anchor: \mathbb K=(\Sigma,M,B,D,O,\delta) ... Formal Kernel Definition & Operator Algebra
rows.statement: Proposes the candidate formal kernel K=(Sigma,M,B,D,O,delta) [epistemic state, operational mode, Buddhi/discrimination function, determination, admissible operations, transition function] with M in {S,R,T} and delta:(Sigma,M,O)->(Sigma',M'). Explicitly recommends stopping the addition of Gita terminology and proposes the concluding research step 'Formal Kernel Definition and Operator Algebra' with 9 questions: what is the minimum kernel state; which operations belong inside the kernel; what Buddhi formally does; how Sattva/Rajas/Tamas modify operator semantics; how Zero participates in transitions; how knowledge changes with time; which operations are internal vs external; where Governance enters without becoming part of the kernel; whether this structure can be independently derived without the Gita. Notes the source material itself cautions against selective reinterpretation, recommending every KnowledgeOS mapping be separately labelled as correspondence, hypothesis, derivation, or canonical result.

rows.anchor: \operatorname{Stop}(K_t) ... No further qualification is presently justified.
rows.statement: Discovers a missing operator through simulation: when Buddhi cannot determine sufficiency, the kernel needs Escalate or SeekQualification -- the kernel must know when NOT to decide. Proposes Stop(K_t) as a legitimate kernel operation: a disciplined kernel can say 'no further qualification is presently justified', which is an epistemic decision, not a failure -- contrasted with a bad kernel's uncertainty->more computation->more computation loop. Gives Qualify(x) codomain {Qualified,Rejected,Suspended,Escalated,bot}, with bot meaning the kernel has reached a legitimate epistemic terminus, connecting to the Cavell insight.

rows.anchor: input \rightarrow precondition \rightarrow Buddhi decision \rightarrow state transformation \rightarrow postcondition \rightarrow Zero effect \rightarrow provenance
rows.statement: Proposes the concluding research step 'Define the Kernel Algebra': stop adding Gita chapters and take the simulated kernel through a formal operator analysis of {Observe,Attend,Discriminate,Qualify,Compare,Transform,Purify,Act,Expose,Stabilize,Stop,Escalate}, determining for every operator a 7-step profile: input -> precondition -> Buddhi decision -> state transformation -> postcondition -> Zero effect -> provenance, then testing composition, idempotence, commutativity, associativity, reversibility, monotonicity, mode-dependence and purification effects -- framed as turning the philosophical interpretation into an actual mathematical research programme.

Constructs a five-operator formal algebra: Omega:W->O (observe), Q:O->E (qualify), J:ExK->K' (know/transform), B:K'xC->D (discriminate), A:D->W' (act), with explicit composition K_{t+1}=J(Q(Omega(W_t)),K_t), D_t=B(K_{t+1},C_t), W_{t+1}=A(D_t,W_t). Proposes working kernel definition Kernel=(K_t,Omega,Q,J,B,A,Delta,Sigma,Pi) with central transition K_t --Omega,Q--> E_t --J--> K'_t --B--> D_t --A--> W_{t+1} --Omega--> K_{t+1}, explicitly non-canonical pending formal validation. Frames Chapter 4's strongest contribution as a theory of what the kernel DOES with knowledge (Knowledge->discrimination->decision->action->new state), not another primitive.

rows.anchor: freeze a KERNEL-CANDIDATE-v1 consisting of only \{K_t,\;Zero,\;Sa\d{m}śaya,\;Jñāna,\;Buddhi,\;Decision,\;Action\}
rows.statement: Recommends, before simulating the whole Gita-KnowledgeOS system, freezing a minimal KERNEL-CANDIDATE-v1 = {K_t, Zero, Samsaya, Jnana, Buddhi, Decision, Action} and mathematically testing operators J, B, A, Omega, Q for closure, typing, identity, composition, reversibility, monotonicity, and information loss -- explicit caution that the source's religious claims must not be converted into technical claims by analogy alone; the strongest candidates are those independently derivable from KnowledgeOS per Step 286. Chapter 4 generates and corroborates hypotheses; it does not ratify the kernel.

rows.anchor: \mathbb K_t = ( M_t, B_t, K_t, \Sigma_t, G_t, D_t, \Gamma_t )
rows.statement: Proposes a 12-operator candidate catalogue (Receive, Attend, Compare, Discern_B, Accept, Reject, Hold, Transform, Act, Observe-consequence, Reconcile, Purify) and a candidate kernel state (fraktur K)_t=(M_t,B_t,K_t,Sigma_t,G_t,D_t,Gamma_t) [Manas/working state, Buddhi/discrimination state, knowledge state, epistemic dimensions, detected gaps, detected distortions, operational mode/guna]. Gives transition algebra (fraktur K)_t --Omega--> O_t --M--> M_{t+1} --B--> B_{t+1} --Q--> Q_t --A--> a_t --delta--> K_{t+1}, noting Qualify's natural position between Buddhi and Action ('Perceive->Think->Discriminate->Qualify->Act') but explicitly leaving whether Qualify deserves this exact formal role OPEN, consistent with Steps 285-287.

rows.anchor: \operatorname{Gate}(c,p)
rows.statement: From 2.58's tortoise analogy (senses withdrawn and redeployed for particular purposes): proposes a channel-gating operator Gate(c,p) where c=channel, p=purpose/context, mapping to {OPEN,CLOSED,QUARANTINE,SUPPRESS}, e.g. Observation channel->OPEN, External distraction->CLOSED, Untrusted source->QUARANTINE, Irrelevant signal->SUPPRESS -- assessed as much more concrete than simply saying 'sense control'.

rows.anchor: \mathcal{K}_{ernel} = (K_t,\ M_t,\ B_t,\ \delta,\ G_t,\ Z_t)
rows.statement: Concludes with candidate kernel K_ernel=(K_t,M_t,B_t,delta,G_t,Z_t) [knowledge state, mode/regime, Buddhi, transition, input/action gating, Zero detection] and fundamental cycle (K_t,M_t) --Observe--> O_t --Buddhi--> D_t --Gate--> A_t --delta--> K_{t+1} --Zero--> GAP_{t+1}. Explicitly designates this a 'Gita-derived research hypothesis', not canonical, pending testing against the eight primitives, Sigma, delta, Zero, Qualify, identity/equality, and the existing corpus. Proposes as the next intellectually important step deriving the smallest possible algebra of kernel operators (Buddhi, Gate, Discriminate, Qualify, Purify, Zero, Update, Mode-transition) across Chapters 2-18, explicitly checking which are genuinely derivable from KnowledgeOS vs purely Gita-inspired.

rows.anchor: What is the smallest algebra of operations required for this kernel to reproduce the epistemic dynamics identified across Chapters 2–18?
rows.statement: Proposes stopping independent chapter analysis and instead deriving the smallest algebra of operations O_K={o_1,...,o_n} required to reproduce the epistemic dynamics identified across Chapters 2-18, testing each operator against 10 questions: input state, output state, preconditions, invariants, whether it changes K, whether it changes Sigma, whether it consumes evidence, whether it produces an Observation/Event/Action, whether Buddhi is required, whether the operator is mode-dependent. Explicitly framed as achievable without letting the Gita dictate the architecture: the Gita supplies the hypothesis, mathematics/DDD/the existing corpus determine whether the operator belongs.

rows.anchor: 1.\ Observe ... 2.\ Represent ... 3.\ Discriminate\;(\text{Buddhi}) ... 4.\ Revise ... 5.\ Decide/prepare\ for\ action
rows.statement: Closing statement of the whole hpa Gita-kernel thread: candidate kernel (fraktur M)_t=(O_t,K_t,C_t,P_t,B_t,G_t,D_t) with transition (fraktur M)_t --Omega--> O_{t+1} --Interpret--> K'_{t+1} --Buddhi--> E_{t+1} --Decision--> D_{t+1}. States the formal research result: a system may possess substantial observations and internally coherent propositions while remaining unable to produce an appropriate decision because its interpretive model and discriminative capacity are compromised -- explicitly independent of accepting the Gita's theology. Concludes with five fundamental kernel responsibilities: Observe, Represent, Discriminate (Buddhi), Revise, Decide/prepare-for-action, with Zero exposing unresolved boundaries and the Krishna/Sarathi lens representing guidance/reorientation rather than a knowledge container -- explicitly NOT yet promoted to canonical operations; final proposed next step is deriving the minimal operator algebra from these five responsibilities and testing whether all of Chapters 1-18 can be represented without ad-hoc operators.

rows.anchor: Every other Gītā chapter addressed what the kernel should DO. Ch 1 is the only one that addresses how it FAILS. ... REFINED-STEP-287-INVARIANTS has 7 candidate invariants, 0 ESTABLISHED ... 291 §03 found 0 of 22 operations with failure semantics.
rows.statement: Ch1 is identified as the only Gita chapter addressing failure/uncertainty semantics -- one of the kernel proposal's own declared-open slots (primitive operators, types, pre/postconditions, composition rules, identity elements, invariants, failure/uncertainty semantics, minimality). sources.note: The candidate canonicalization mechanism by which different surface expressions normalize to one stored semantic structure; the subject of a dedicated mathematical measurement-framework research thread (H_I, C_conv, D_sep, T_preserve, FCR, FDR, A_abstain) in this batch, explicitly classified mechanism-level, never kernel.

rows.anchor: Semantic Normal Form (SNF): different surface expressions normalize to one stored semantic structure; expressions become views
rows.statement: The first formal naming of SNF in the admitted corpus, illustrated by two paraphrase sentences both normalizing to one EVENT/ACTOR/OBJECT/JUSTIFICATION/CONDITION structure; explicitly classified 'New Candidate Mechanism (Not Kernel)'.

rows.anchor: Semantic Invariance Layer: Expression Layer -> Semantic Parser -> Meaning Graph -> Knowledge Identity
rows.statement: A proposed mechanism pipeline realizing SNF, cited as feeding Logical Architecture, never the kernel.

rows.anchor: Expression Order != Meaning Structure
rows.statement: The order-invariance facet of the Vani (Expression != Meaning) principle: meaning must be reconstructed from invariant relationships, not from the accidental arrangement of expressions.

rows.anchor: two different sentences can become the same knowledge object; two similar sentences can become different knowledge objects
rows.statement: States the semantic-identity discrimination rule contrasting KnowledgeOS's target behavior with an LLM's similar-expression-implies-similar-meaning risk.

rows.anchor: rigorous SNF metric definitions: a semantic metric-space distance d (non-negativity, identity, symmetry, triangle inequality), a Bayesian posterior P(theta_i|E,C) over semantic interpretations, normalized semantic entropy H_sem, convergence C_snf, non-collapse NC_snf, transformation stability T_snf,
rows.statement: A senior-mathematician-style formalization of an originally underspecified SNF measurement proposal (undefined D, undefined p_i, undefined C_snf/NC_snf/T_snf), giving each metric explicit mathematical properties and a proposed experimental protocol (1,000 controlled cases) with target thresholds.

rows.anchor: structural similarity != semantic equivalence: a Jaccard-style graph-edit distance over SNF graphs measures 'SNF Structural Distance', not yet 'Semantic Distance' -- APPROVE(Architect,Design) vs AUTHORIZE(Architect,Design) may be semantically equivalent but structurally different, while adding one C
rows.statement: A critical mathematical correction rejecting the premature identification of a graph-edit metric with 'semantic distance', renaming the former precisely.

rows.anchor: three distinct uncertainties must not be conflated: model/interpretation uncertainty ('which interpretation should I choose'), representational uncertainty ('does my representation capture the meaning'), and epistemic uncertainty ('is this justified') -- the semantic compiler should expose the first
rows.statement: Refines the Bayesian semantic-entropy proposal by noting that low entropy over a compiler's own candidate-interpretation space does not mean the expression is objectively unambiguous -- it only means the model's own candidate set has low uncertainty.

rows.anchor: false convergence (semantic collision) is more dangerous than false divergence: if two equivalent sentences produce different SNFs, that is inefficiency; if two different propositions produce the same SNF, that is knowledge corruption.
rows.statement: A stated safety asymmetry motivating the introduction of a hard non-collapse safety gate (rather than a weighted composite score that could average away a catastrophic collapse) and a proposed 'Semantic Collision Rate' metric.

rows.anchor: do NOT use a weighted harmonic-mean composite SNF score; instead impose a hard safety constraint (non-collapse below threshold => FAIL, independent of the other metrics) plus descriptive metrics for the surviving system.
rows.statement: Rejects the mathematically-elegant but architecturally-dangerous idea of averaging convergence/non-collapse/transformation/entropy into one quality score, on the grounds that a catastrophic non-collapse failure must never be diluted by good scores elsewhere.

rows.anchor: 100-case synthetic pilot result: semantic collision rate 25% (5 of 20 deliberately distinct-meaning pairs collapsed to the same synthetic SNF); 0/20 distinct-meaning pairs passed the non-collapse threshold.
rows.statement: A deliberately-seeded synthetic pilot demonstrating that the measurement framework mechanically detects injected semantic collisions; explicitly caveated as testing the measurement mathematics only, not whether SNF actually preserves semantics (which requires a real semantic distance, not a synthetic structural one).

experiment.hypothesis: the proposed multi-metric measurement framework mechanically detects seeded semantic collisions
experiment.setup: 100 synthetic cases (20 true equivalences, 20 deliberate semantic collisions, 15 word-order transformations, 15 context changes, 10 ambiguities, 10 contradictions, 10 unknown/unrepresentable) with a synthetic structural distance function
experiment.assumptions: synthetic SNF representations and distances stand in for a real semantic distance
experiment.method: computed C_snf/NC_snf/CR/T_snf/H_sem on the synthetic corpus
experiment.result: semantic collision rate 25% (5/20 deliberately-collapsed pairs detected); 0/20 non-collapse threshold passes
experiment.interpretation: a composite quality score would hide this failure (e.g. C=0.99,T=0.98,H=0.05 but NC=0 looks excellent yet is a collision) -- non-collapse must be a hard gate
experiment.limitations: the SNF representations and distances are synthetic, not derived from a real semantic parser
experiment.conclusion: the measurement framework works mechanically; whether SNF actually preserves semantics remains untested and requires a gold-relation/confusion-matrix experiment (proposed as v0.3) rather than immediately scaling to 1,000 real cases

rows.anchor: gold-relation / confusion-matrix design (v0.3): compare SNF's EQUIVALENT/DISTINCT/UNKNOWN judgment against an independently-labelled gold relation, producing three failure classes -- false divergence, semantic collision, and false certainty (UNKNOWN converted into confident interpretation).
