sources.note: Gita-Chapter-4-derived (Krishna remembers past births, Arjuna does not) three-layer memory formalization distinguishing current state S_t, historical lineage H, and accessible/authorized memory K(H); yields Provenance-vs-Lineage distinction and the claim that Ephemeral Agent Memory != Authoritative Knowledge Memory, used to validate the prior decision that .claude/ and .codex/ are not authoritative KnowledgeOS memory.

rows.anchor: In Chapter 4, Krishna tells Arjuna that both have had many births, but Krishna remembers them while Arjuna does not. ... It introduces a distinction between: Continuity and: Accessible memory. Those are not the same thing.
rows.statement: Uses Krishna's remembered-vs-Arjuna's-unremembered past births as an example motivating a distinction between Continuity (that a lineage of states exists) and Accessible memory (what a given state can currently retrieve of that lineage) -- these are argued to not be the same thing.

rows.anchor: Layer 1 -- Current state: S_t. Layer 2 -- Historical lineage: H={S_0,S_1,...,S_t}. Layer 3 -- Authorized historical knowledge: K(H). These are different. Therefore: State != History != Accessible Memory.
rows.statement: Formalizes a three-layer memory model: Layer 1 current state S_t; Layer 2 historical lineage H = {S_0,...,S_t} (what actually happened); Layer 3 authorized/accessible historical knowledge K(H) (what some actor/system is permitted or capable of knowing about H). States the invariant State != History != Accessible Memory, i.e. 'History exists' does not imply 'Current agent knows history'.
missing: formal definition of K as a function, access-control semantics

rows.anchor: Agent_{t+1} != Agent_t in terms of accessible memory. But KnowledgeOS can preserve: History(Agent) outside the ephemeral agent state.
rows.statement: Applies the three-layer memory model to an AI agent session example: a later session's agent (Agent t+1) need not remember an earlier session's agent (Agent t) state, but KnowledgeOS can preserve History(Agent) outside the ephemeral per-session agent memory, so the agent does not have to carry its entire history itself.

rows.anchor: Ephemeral Agent Memory != Authoritative Knowledge Memory. This strongly validates the architecture decision we previously made that: .claude/ and .codex/ should not become the authoritative KnowledgeOS memory. The agent harness may contain operational memory. KnowledgeOS contains governed historical knowledge.
rows.statement: States the principle Ephemeral Agent Memory != Authoritative Knowledge Memory and explicitly claims this validates a prior architecture decision that agent-harness directories (.claude/, .codex/) must not become the authoritative KnowledgeOS memory -- the agent harness holds operational memory, while KnowledgeOS holds governed historical knowledge.
invariants: Ephemeral Agent Memory != Authoritative Knowledge Memory

lineage_claims.target: prior architecture decision that .claude/ and .codex/ are not authoritative KnowledgeOS memory
lineage_claims.quote: This strongly validates the architecture decision we previously made that: .claude/ and .codex/ should not become the authoritative KnowledgeOS memory.

rows.anchor: We need to distinguish: Actor identity, State, Memory, Role, Authority, Experience, Knowledge. ... ActorIdentity = A ... State(A,t1) != State(A,t2). And: Memory(A,t2) may not contain: Memory(A,t1). Yet: History(A) can still exist.
rows.statement: Argues identity should not be shallowly answered with 'the user ID'; instead distinguishes seven separate notions -- Actor identity, State, Memory, Role, Authority, Experience, Knowledge -- and formalizes that a stable ActorIdentity A can have State(A,t1) != State(A,t2), Memory(A,t2) not necessarily containing Memory(A,t1), while History(A) still exists as a distinct object.
missing: formal relations among the seven notions

rows.anchor: D1 [with] actor, context, evidence, method, timestamp, provenance. Otherwise the determination becomes: 'Something the AI once said.' That is not governed knowledge. Instead it becomes: Historical epistemic artifact.
rows.statement: Argues that a determination D1 must retain its actor, context, evidence, method, timestamp and provenance even after the originating session disappears, because without this it degrades from governed knowledge into a mere unattributed 'historical epistemic artifact' ('something the AI once said'); this is offered as the reason provenance must be external to transient agent state.

rows.anchor: I would not model Krishna simply as "the administrator who has all memory." A better abstraction is: Witness + Teacher + Source of continuity. ... A trusted epistemic authority that can establish continuity across states that individually lack complete historical memory.
rows.statement: Rejects modeling Krishna as 'an administrator who has all memory' (an omniscient-database analogy) and instead re-characterizes his architectural role as Witness + Teacher + Source of continuity -- a trusted epistemic authority able to establish continuity across states that individually lack complete historical memory.

rows.anchor: Provenance asks: Where did this knowledge come from? Provenance(x). Lineage asks: What states/instances are connected through continuity? Lineage(x). They overlap but are not identical. So: Provenance != Lineage.
rows.statement: Distinguishes Provenance(x) (where knowledge came from) from Lineage(x) (what states/instances are connected through continuity): the two overlap but are argued to not be identical, proposed as an addition to the architecture vocabulary. A governed 'Historical Continuity' mechanism is proposed to maintain Lineage(x) even when Memory(x,t) is incomplete.
missing: formal relation/mapping between Provenance and Lineage

rows.anchor: Principle IV-B -- Continuity exceeds accessible memory: Historical continuity must not depend on the current actor's accessible memory. Therefore: CurrentMemory subseteq HistoricalKnowledge may be true. But: CurrentMemory = HistoricalKnowledge must not be assumed.
rows.statement: Names and records 'Principle IV-B -- Continuity exceeds accessible memory': historical continuity must not depend on the current actor's accessible memory; CurrentMemory subseteq HistoricalKnowledge may hold, but CurrentMemory = HistoricalKnowledge must never be assumed.

rows.anchor: The actor must know the limits of its own knowledge. This is perhaps the most important principle for AI. An agent should be able to say: I know this. I do not know this. I previously knew this but cannot currently reconstruct it. ... That is epistemically mature architecture.
rows.statement: States a third principle, considered possibly the most important for AI: 'the actor must know the limits of its own knowledge', illustrated by a required repertoire of self-report statements (I know this / I do not know this / I previously knew this but cannot currently reconstruct it / the system has historical evidence for this / the evidence is insufficient for action / the action is prohibited / the action requires authority), termed 'epistemically mature architecture'.
missing: formal encoding of the self-report repertoire

rows.anchor: HISTORICAL LINEAGE -> KNOWLEDGE -> INQUIRY -> EVIDENCE -> DETERMINATION -> WISDOM -> (SHOULD DO / SHOULD NOT DO) -> DECISION -> (ACT/DEFER/REFRAIN) -> EXECUTION -> OBSERVATION -> NEW KNOWLEDGE/UPDATE, and above all of it: PROVENANCE + LINEAGE
rows.statement: Revises the KnowledgeOS pipeline diagram (previously Knowledge->Inquiry->Evidence->Determination->Decision->Action) into a richer chain: HISTORICAL LINEAGE -> KNOWLEDGE -> INQUIRY -> EVIDENCE -> DETERMINATION -> WISDOM -> {SHOULD DO, SHOULD NOT DO} -> DECISION -> {ACT, DEFER, REFRAIN} -> EXECUTION -> OBSERVATION -> NEW KNOWLEDGE/UPDATE, with PROVENANCE + LINEAGE positioned as an overarching background layer.

lineage_claims.quote: Previously we had: Knowledge -> Inquiry -> Evidence -> Determination -> Decision -> Action. After Chapter 4, I would revise it to: ...

rows.anchor: I would actually say Chapter 4 strengthens our architecture rather than forcing us to redesign it. Especially these existing decisions: knowledge separated from agents; evidence separated from claims; determination separated from decision; decision separated from execution; provenance preserved; context snapshots; immutable historical determinations; supersession rather than overwriting; AI agents treated as actors; governance as a separate concern.
rows.statement: Explicitly claims Chapter 4's material strengthens/validates (rather than forces redesign of) ten prior architecture decisions: knowledge separated from agents; evidence separated from claims; determination separated from decision; decision separated from execution; provenance preserved; context snapshots; immutable historical determinations; supersession rather than overwriting; AI agents treated as actors; governance as a separate concern.

lineage_claims.quote: I would actually say Chapter 4 strengthens our architecture rather than forcing us to redesign it.

rows.anchor: 3C. Missing concepts ... Look for concepts that the reasoning requires but which were never explicitly modeled. Examples discovered during later reasoning may include: wisdom, action guidance, historical continuity, epistemic restraint. Do not automatically accept these. Evaluate them against the complete corpus.
rows.statement: Explicitly names wisdom, action guidance, historical continuity, and epistemic restraint as candidate 'missing concepts' example categories to evaluate for Phase 3C -- directly referencing (and thereby corroborating the significance of) the Chapter-4-derived wisdom-action-guidance-function and historical-continuity-vs-accessible-memory material found elsewhere in this same batch (S1067), while cautioning these candidates must not be automatically accepted.

lineage_claims.quote: Examples discovered during later reasoning may include: wisdom, action guidance, historical continuity, epistemic restraint.

rows.anchor: 8. DO NOT CONFUSE MEMORY WITH KNOWLEDGE ... Apply the same discipline to this synthesis project. The current Claude context is NOT the authoritative memory of the project. The corpus is the historical source. The synthesis artifacts become the structured working model.
rows.statement: Applies the same memory-vs-knowledge discipline the corpus develops about KnowledgeOS reflexively to the synthesis process itself: the synthesizing agent's own (Claude) context is explicitly declared NOT the authoritative memory of the project -- the brainstorming corpus is the historical source and the synthesis artifacts (files under docs/knowledgeos/reviews/synthesis/) become the structured working model. This mirrors the Ephemeral-Agent-Memory != Authoritative-Knowledge-Memory principle found in S1067.
invariants: Ephemeral Agent Memory != Authoritative Knowledge Memory

lineage_claims.quote: The current Claude context is NOT the authoritative memory of the project. The corpus is the historical source.

rows.anchor: Gītā text ↓ Philosophical principle ↓ Abstract structural pattern ↓ KnowledgeOS question ↓ Mathematical / architectural test ↓ Possible hypothesis ... Never: Gītā character → KnowledgeOS object ... and never: philosophical idea → equation → architecture
rows.statement: The Bhagavad Gita research track is classified as external research, not an architecture source. Correct method: Gita text -> philosophical principle -> abstract structural pattern -> KnowledgeOS question -> mathematical/architectural test -> possible hypothesis; forbidden shortcuts are 'Gita character -> KnowledgeOS object' and 'philosophical idea -> equation -> architecture'. Current research covers Chapters 1-4, with candidate hypotheses including Continuity != Memory != Observation and Knowledge != Wisdom != Action ('Wisdom is active discernment concerning what should be done and what should not be done'), explicitly framed as research hypotheses only. DeepSeek's Gita document is separately classified EXTERNAL RESEARCH / NON-AUTHORITATIVE / CONCEPTUAL LENSES / HYPOTHESES, and its unsupported quantitative equations are not accepted as KnowledgeOS derivations.

assumptions.statement: Gita-derived structural patterns may map onto KnowledgeOS questions only after independent mathematical/architectural testing

rows.anchor: Source ≠ History ≠ AccessibleMemory. ... For an object x, we want Lineage(x)={x0,x1,…,xt}. But an actor at time t may have only Memory_t(x) ⊂ Lineage(x). KnowledgeOS should preserve enough information to reconstruct the relevant lineage independently of the actor's current memory.
rows.statement: Applies the Gita-Chapter-4-derived principle Source != History != AccessibleMemory as three new audit questions (What is the authoritative source? What happened during transmission -- Lineage? What does the current actor actually remember -- AccessibleMemory?). Formalizes Lineage(x)={x_0,...,x_t} versus an actor's Memory_t(x) which is only a subset of Lineage(x) at time t, and states KnowledgeOS should preserve enough information to reconstruct relevant lineage independently of an actor's current memory -- termed a major architecture capability (historical continuity audit).
missing: mechanism for lineage reconstruction not specified

lineage_claims.quote: This is where the Chapter 4 review becomes practically useful.

rows.anchor: We must never confuse: Archive with: Lineage. An archive answers: 'Do we still have the old information?' Lineage answers: 'How did the current state arise from the previous state?' KnowledgeOS requires the second. ... TransactionTime from ValidTime.
rows.statement: Distinguishes Archive ('do we still have the old information?') from Lineage ('how did the current state arise from the previous state?'), arguing KnowledgeOS requires the latter; historical continuity evidence (session logs, change logs, repository history, saved conversations) is judged PARTIAL because these are not yet a unified historical model. Also distinguishes TransactionTime from ValidTime as an explicit audit requirement, since createdAt/updatedAt fields are not automatically sufficient to reconstruct semantic validity at a point in time (State(x,t)).

rows.anchor: H_t be the total relevant historical lineage at time t. ... M_t be what an agent currently remembers. Then generally: M_t ⊆ H_t. A new agent/session may have M_{t+1}∩M_t that is much smaller than the complete historical lineage. Yet the system can preserve H_t. ... Continuity must belong to the governed system, not depend solely on the memory of the current actor.
rows.statement: Formalizes the Chapter-4 continuity insight: H_t = total relevant historical lineage at time t, M_t = what an agent currently remembers, with M_t subseteq H_t generally holding; a new agent/session's overlap with the prior agent's memory (M_{t+1} intersect M_t) may be much smaller than the full lineage H_t, yet the system can still preserve H_t independently. Yields the principle 'continuity must belong to the governed system, not depend solely on the memory of the current actor' -- described as highly relevant to AI engineering.
invariants: continuity belongs to the system, not the actor's memory

lineage_claims.target: the Gita Chapter 4 insight raised earlier in the step series
lineage_claims.quote: Now we can express the insight you raised earlier mathematically.

rows.anchor: The system preserves the lineage necessary to reconstruct relevant prior states. ... GlobalHistoricalContext may be available to the system of record while LocalActorContext is intentionally incomplete. Therefore: SystemContext ⊇ ActorContext can be a design principle. ... Projection(H,C) → Context_C. The agent receives a context projection appropriate to its task. ... Context supplied to an actor must be distinguishable from complete historical state. Otherwise the actor may incorrectly assume: 'What I was given is everything that exists.'
rows.statement: Reframes the Gita continuity insight architecturally: not 'the system remembers everything' but 'the system preserves the lineage necessary to reconstruct relevant prior states'; models GlobalHistoricalContext (system of record) vs intentionally incomplete LocalActorContext under the design principle SystemContext ⊇ ActorContext, formalized as a context-projection function Projection(H,C) -> Context_C giving an agent only a task-relevant slice of history. Adds a new invariant: context supplied to an actor must be distinguishable from complete historical state, else the actor may wrongly assume it was given everything that exists. Argues a complete-memory-for-every-agent design would be expensive, hard to govern, potentially unsafe, and hard to invalidate/reason about, so Agent -> RelevantContext is preferred over Agent -> Everything.
invariants: context supplied to an actor must be distinguishable from complete historical state

lineage_claims.quote: We should also translate that insight carefully rather than literally.

rows.anchor: State(t) ⊉ History(0..t) in general. ... K.current is not equivalent to: KnowledgeHistory. ... AgentMemory ≠ SystemHistory. The system's authoritative lineage must live outside ephemeral agent context. ... Memory ≠ Knowledge ≠ Evidence ≠ History.
rows.statement: States the general formal principle State(t) does not superset History(0..t): the current aggregate state (e.g. K.v7) need not contain its full reasoning history (K.v1->...->K.v7), so K.current != KnowledgeHistory; an agent's session sees only CurrentState, not PreviousReasoning, so AgentMemory != SystemHistory and the authoritative lineage must live outside ephemeral agent context -- reinforcing the chained non-identity Memory != Knowledge != Evidence != History.

lineage_claims.target: the Gita Chapter 4 'only Krishna knows' insight
lineage_claims.quote: We should be careful not to literalize the theological metaphor into software architecture. But as an architectural analogy, it is powerful.

rows.anchor: we must not turn the metaphor into an empirical architectural claim ... CurrentActorState ≠ CompleteSystemHistory. ... History ≠ Truth. History is evidence about the past. ... Record ≠ History ≠ Truth. ... Record --interpretation--> HistoricalAccount --reasoning--> KnowledgeClaim. Each transformation introduces assumptions. ... 'This is what the recorded evidence indicates.' rather than: 'This is what happened.' ... A current state must not be assumed to contain sufficient information to explain its own origin.
rows.statement: Explicitly labels the Atma/Krishna 'who knows the past' framing as a modeling metaphor, not an empirical architectural claim, extracting only CurrentActorState != CompleteSystemHistory with an external lineage system playing the continuity role; then separately warns against equating StoredHistory with Truth, since history itself can contain errors/omissions/conflicting accounts/corrupted records (History != Truth -- history is evidence about the past, not the past itself), chaining Record != History != Truth via Record --interpretation--> HistoricalAccount --reasoning--> KnowledgeClaim (each step introducing assumptions). Concludes the system should say 'this is what the recorded evidence indicates' rather than the stronger, often unjustified 'this is what happened,' and restates: a current state must not be assumed to contain sufficient information to explain its own origin -- more precise than 'keep an audit log.'

lineage_claims.quote: we must not turn the metaphor into an empirical architectural claim

rows.anchor: Memory ≠ Knowledge. Memory can support knowledge reconstruction. It does not automatically constitute it. ... We could retain millions of events and still be unable to answer: Why was this decision reasonable at the time? We therefore need semantic links: Evidence → Determination → Decision.
rows.statement: Sharpens Memory != Knowledge with a concrete contrast: a raw log entry ('Architecture approved at 14:32') is memory; 'the architecture was approved because evidence X supported determination Y under rule Z' is structured knowledge/provenance; millions of retained events without semantic links (Evidence->Determination->Decision) still cannot answer why a decision was reasonable at the time -- raw historical data is not historical understanding.

lexical.anchor: In Chapter 4, Krishna tells Arjuna that both have had many births, but Krishna remembers them while Arjuna does not. ... It introduces a distinction between: Continuity and: Accessible memory. Those are not the same thing.

conceptual.anchor: I would not model Krishna simply as "the administrator who has all memory." A better abstraction is: Witness + Teacher + Source of continuity. ... A trusted epistemic authority that can establish continuity across states that individually lack complete historical memory.

formal.anchor: Layer 1 -- Current state: S_t. Layer 2 -- Historical lineage: H={S_0,S_1,...,S_t}. Layer 3 -- Authorized historical knowledge: K(H). These are different. Therefore: State != History != Accessible Memory.

governance.anchor: Ephemeral Agent Memory != Authoritative Knowledge Memory. This strongly validates the architecture decision we previously made that: .claude/ and .codex/ should not become the authoritative KnowledgeOS memory. The agent harness may contain operational memory. KnowledgeOS contains governed historical knowledge.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Agent_{t+1} != Agent_t in terms of accessible memory. But KnowledgeOS can preserve: History(Agent) outside the ephemeral agent state.
rationale_evidence.statement: Applies the three-layer memory model to an AI agent session example: a later session's agent (Agent t+1) need not remember an earlier session's agent (Agent t) state, but KnowledgeOS can preserve History(Agent) outside the ephemeral per-session agent memory, so the agent does not have to carry its entire history itself.

rationale_evidence.anchor: D1 [with] actor, context, evidence, method, timestamp, provenance. Otherwise the determination becomes: 'Something the AI once said.' That is not governed knowledge. Instead it becomes: Historical epistemic artifact.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues that a determination D1 must retain its actor, context, evidence, method, timestamp and provenance even after the originating session disappears, because without this it degrades from governed knowledge into a mere unattributed 'historical epistemic artifact' ('something the AI once said'); this is offered as the reason provenance must be external to transient agent state.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Gītā text ↓ Philosophical principle ↓ Abstract structural pattern ↓ KnowledgeOS question ↓ Mathematical / architectural test ↓ Possible hypothesis ... Never: Gītā character → KnowledgeOS object ... and never: philosophical idea → equation → architecture
rationale_evidence.statement: The Bhagavad Gita research track is classified as external research, not an architecture source. Correct method: Gita text -> philosophical principle -> abstract structural pattern -> KnowledgeOS question -> mathematical/architectural test -> possible hypothesis; forbidden shortcuts are 'Gita character -> KnowledgeOS object' and 'philosophical idea -> equation -> architecture'. Current research covers Chapters 1-4, with candidate hypotheses including Continuity != Memory != Observation and Knowledge != Wisdom != Action ('Wisdom is active discernment concerning what should be done and what should not be done'), explicitly framed as research hypotheses only. DeepSeek's Gita document is separately classified EXTERNAL RESEARCH / NON-AUTHORITATIVE / CONCEPTUAL LENSES / HYPOTHESES, and its unsupported quantitative equations are not accepted as KnowledgeOS derivations.

assumption_register.statement: Gita-derived structural patterns may map onto KnowledgeOS questions only after independent mathematical/architectural testing

sources.note: Step 220 'Concept Genealogy: Find the Origins of the Architecture' (phase_measure_theory): establishes what the Steps 1-182 audit is trying to recover (Origin->Evolution->Formalization->Implementation->Verification), a five-question genealogy per concept (first problem/first idea/first formalization/first architecture/first verification, explicitly FirstMention!=FirstInsight!=FirstFormalization!=FirstArchitecture!=FirstVerification), semantic-vs-terminological origin, a Concept Genealogy Ledger schema, an invariant genealogy I0(implicit)->I1(recognized)->I2(explicit)->I3(implemented)->I4(verified), a 7-field temporal tuple G(C_i)=(t_o,t_r,t_n,t_f,t_a,t_m,t_v) reframed as a directed acyclic knowledge graph rather than a linear chain to allow convergent/divergent discovery paths, Convergence(I) as independent-path count (explicitly not a probability), concept collision (SameTerm+DifferentMeaning) as a boundary-discovery mechanism, semantic typing Concept=(Name,Context,Meaning,Constraints), a per-chapter Gita-genealogy integration (chapters 1-4 mapped to candidate technical analogues via P1/P2/P3), an explicit safeguard that the Gita is not a source of software requirements, a mathematical-formula genealogy schema, Architecture_empirical vs Architecture_theoretical, and 'Architectural Residuals' (Intended-Implemented gaps) as a model-revision audit loop. Ends with the Step 221 agenda (eight candidate concept 'families' A-H) embedded in its tail.

rows.anchor:
$$FirstMention
eq FirstInsight
eq FirstFormalization
eq FirstArchitecture
eq FirstVerification.$$ This distinction is essential.
rows.statement: Step 220 establishes that a concept's five genealogical milestones (first mention, first insight, first formalization, first architectural adoption, first verification) may occur at entirely different points in the 182-step history and must not be conflated.

rows.anchor: Therefore we distinguish: $$Origin_{semantic}$$ from: $$Origin_{terminological}.$$
rows.statement: Step 220 distinguishes semantic origin (where the underlying idea first implicitly appears) from terminological origin (where the name for it is first introduced), noting a term's first appearance does not establish where the concept itself originated.

rows.anchor: | Concept ID | ... | First verification | Where is it tested/evidenced? | Later reinterpretation | Did our understanding change? | Gītā relation | ... | Current status | F/D/P/U | This becomes the **Concept Genealogy Ledger**.
rows.statement: Step 220 defines the Concept Genealogy Ledger schema: for every candidate major concept, record concept ID, first semantic appearance, first explicit formulation, first terminology, first formalization, first architecture, first implementation, first verification, later reinterpretation, Gita relation (chapters 1-4 and P1/P2/P3), and current F/D/P/U status.

rows.anchor: $$Implemented(I)$$ does not imply: $$Verified(I).$$ This should become a permanent KnowledgeOS rule.
rows.statement: Step 220 explicitly proposes Implemented(I) does not imply Verified(I) as a permanent KnowledgeOS rule, building on the implementation-vs-verification distinction.

rows.anchor: $$I_0\rightarrow I_1\rightarrow I_2\rightarrow I_3\rightarrow I_4$$ where: I_0 = implicit intuition; I_1 = recognized principle; I_2 = explicit invariant; I_3 = implemented constraint; I_4 = verified invariant. Not every invariant reaches I_4. That itself becomes an important result.
rows.statement: Step 220 defines a five-stage invariant genealogy (I0 implicit intuition, I1 recognized principle, I2 explicit invariant, I3 implemented constraint, I4 verified invariant), explicitly noting that not every invariant reaches I4 and that this fact is itself an important result.

rows.anchor: $$G(C_i)=(t_o,t_r,t_n,t_f,t_a,t_m,t_v)$$ ... The genealogy is therefore an ordered temporal structure. ... Therefore the concept genealogy is better represented as a **directed acyclic knowledge graph** than a simple chain.
rows.statement: Step 220 defines a 7-field temporal-milestone tuple G(C_i) per concept (observation, recognition, naming, formalization, architectural adoption, implementation, verification), then generalizes it from a linear ordered chain to a directed acyclic knowledge graph to accommodate concepts developing along independent, later-converging paths.

rows.anchor: All converge on: $$I.$$ Then: $$Convergence(I)=3.$$ This gives us a powerful indicator of conceptual robustness. Again, it is not a probability. It is evidence of **independent conceptual convergence**.
rows.statement: Step 220 defines Convergence(I) as the count of independent discovery paths (e.g. Experiment, DDD, Governance) converging on the same principle I, explicitly stating it is not a probability but evidence of independent conceptual convergence -- reprising the same Convergence concept later used uncomputed in Step 215.

rows.anchor: Later we discover: $$I_1\neq I_2.$$ This is not necessarily a problem. It may reveal a previously hidden bounded context.
rows.statement: Step 220 frames divergent interpretation (the same observation producing two different, later-discovered-incompatible principles I1 and I2) not necessarily as an error but as potentially revealing a previously hidden bounded context.

rows.anchor: If two teams use: "Evidence" but mean different things, then: $$Evidence_{ContextA}\neq Evidence_{ContextB}.$$ The correct response is not necessarily to force one universal definition. ... Therefore concept divergence can be a **boundary-discovery mechanism**.
rows.statement: Step 220 argues that when the same term (e.g. Evidence) carries different meanings across contexts, the correct DDD response is not necessarily to force one universal definition but to recognize distinct bounded contexts -- concept divergence is framed as a boundary-discovery mechanism.

rows.anchor: We should explicitly search for: $$SameTerm + DifferentMeaning.$$ This is a **concept collision**.
rows.statement: Step 220 defines 'concept collision' as SameTerm+DifferentMeaning and proposes a systematic collision-audit table (Term, Context A, Context B, Same meaning?, DDD consequence) to be applied across the corpus, applicable directly to this batch's own findings of symbol drift (E, I, A, S, G, K across Steps 208-219).

rows.anchor: We can therefore treat every important domain concept as semantically typed: $$Concept=(Name,Context,Meaning,Constraints).$$ Two concepts with the same name are not equivalent unless: $$Meaning_A=Meaning_B$$ under the relevant context.
rows.statement: Step 220 proposes treating every domain concept as semantically typed via a 4-tuple Concept=(Name,Context,Meaning,Constraints), establishing that two concepts sharing a name are not equivalent unless their Meaning is equal under the relevant context -- framed as both a DDD principle and a mathematical abstraction.

rows.anchor: **The Gītā does not serve as a source of software requirements.** Rather: $$Gita\rightarrow Question/Reflection$$ while: $$EngineeringEvidence\rightarrow Architecture.$$ ... the direction of proof remains: $$Evidence\rightarrow Architecture.$$
rows.statement: Step 220 states an explicit philosophical safeguard for the methodology: the Gita does not serve as a source of software requirements; Gita reflections and architectural insights may converge conceptually, but the direction of proof always remains Evidence->Architecture, never Gita->Architecture.

rows.anchor: If we force the Gītā into the architecture, sophisticated readers will notice. ... then the reader can see the correspondence themselves. That is much more intellectually defensible.
rows.statement: Step 220 argues the book is intellectually stronger if it presents the engineering problem, technical reasoning, mathematical formulation, and DDD interpretation first, letting philosophical resonance with the Gita emerge for the reader to notice themselves, rather than forcing the correspondence.

rows.anchor: $$X\sim F_\theta$$ ... Otherwise: $$X\sim F_\theta$$ is merely notation.
rows.statement: Step 220 extends the genealogy discipline to mathematical formulas and distributions: for any X~F_theta used in the architecture, the file requires identifying what X represents, what population/process it models, what assumptions are made, and whether the model has been empirically validated -- otherwise the notation is merely decorative.

rows.anchor: $$\boxed{ArchitecturalResiduals}$$ meaning: Differences between the architecture we believe exists and the behavior/evidence actually observed. ... These residuals are not merely defects. They are **knowledge**.
rows.statement: Step 220 introduces 'Architectural Residuals' (Observation-Prediction analogue applied to architecture: IntendedCapability-ImplementedCapability, DeclaredInvariant-ObservedBehavior), explicitly reframing gaps between believed and observed architecture as knowledge rather than mere defects, feeding a Model->Prediction->Observation->Residual->ModelRevision audit loop.

rows.anchor: A stronger conceptual description may be: **A system for maintaining an evidence-linked, temporally aware, governable model of engineering knowledge and its transformations.** Again, this is a candidate synthesis pending the historical audit.
rows.statement: Step 220 proposes a candidate high-level characterization of KnowledgeOS itself -- 'a system for maintaining an evidence-linked, temporally aware, governable model of engineering knowledge and its transformations' -- explicitly marked as candidate synthesis pending the historical audit, not an established definition.

rows.anchor: ### Family A — Identity and State ... ### Family H — Temporal Continuity ... Then we can determine whether these families converge on a deeper architecture: $$\boxed{Semantic\ Integrity+Evidence+Lineage+Governance}$$
rows.statement: The file's tail embeds the Step 221 agenda: organize candidate principles into eight genealogical families (A Identity/State, B Knowledge/Epistemology, C Authority/Action, D Semantic Boundaries, E Assurance, F AI Transformation, G Governance, H Temporal Continuity) and determine whether they converge on a deeper architecture of Semantic Integrity + Evidence + Lineage + Governance, or reveal a different structure.

rows.anchor: the agenda titles drift from the executed titles. Step 218 announced "Step 219 — Begin the Actual Evidence Audit"; the file is "Evidence Audit: Establish the Ground Truth". ... **Minor, but it means agenda titles cannot be used to identify steps.**
rows.statement: The verifier notes that forward-agenda titles embedded in a predecessor step's tail systematically drift from the eventually-executed file's actual title (Step 218's announced 'Step 219 -- Begin the Actual Evidence Audit' became 'Evidence Audit: Establish the Ground Truth'; Step 219's announced 'Step 220 -- Evidence Audit Pass 1: Find the Origins' became 'Concept Genealogy: Find the Origins of the Architecture'), meaning agenda titles cannot reliably be used to identify steps.

rows.anchor: **Authoritative range, as of 2026-08-30 09:18: Steps 001–220.** All present. **Step 217 has no file of its own**
rows.statement: The verifier sets the authoritative corpus step-count range as of 2026-08-30 09:18 at Steps 001-220, all present, with the sole exception that Step 217 has no file of its own (existing only embedded within Step 216); Step 221 is forward-referenced but does not yet exist at this point.

rows.anchor: ### The citation-density mirage `[SUPERVISOR-VERIFIED]` ... **Inspection refutes it. All nine are hypothetical placeholders inside one illustrative diagram** ... **Genuine prior-step citations in Step 220: ZERO.**
rows.statement: Supervisor-verified finding: a raw grep of Step 220 returns nine apparent prior-step citations (Steps 4,12,17,34,61,88,117,143,169) that would break the corpus's near-zero citation baseline, but inspection reveals all nine are hypothetical placeholders inside one explicitly-labeled illustrative diagram ('Suppose the historical material eventually shows...'); genuine prior-step citations in Step 220 are zero, and the baseline holds unbroken.

rows.anchor: But the corpus labels its own placeholder honestly, and that is the correct behaviour — the failure mode this would have been (fabricated genealogy presented as history) is precisely what step-129 did with `Checked: 1,248 objects`. **Step 220 does not do it.** Credit recorded.
rows.statement: The verifier credits Step 220 for honestly labeling its illustrative genealogy diagram as illustrative rather than passing it off as historical fact -- explicitly contrasted with the earlier step-129 fabricated-result pattern, which Step 220 avoids.

sources.note: Reconstruction of Omega in post-267 corpus steps 269-291: four live senses, one Level-3 identity match (Omega-A same as the earlier 031 Omega-2, mis-attributed), a local (not global) reading of C-06 TRUE CONTRADICTION, and a second apparatus-loss mechanism (rediscovery mislabeled as gap closure) distinct from G-12s continuity-without-apparatus mechanism.

rows.anchor: §1 · Population ... 44 of the 55 are step_286 — one step number ... ONE evidential lineage, not 44 confirmations. ... The two 'intervals' are not sequential — they overlap by ~44 hours ... Step numbers imply sequence; the chronology shows parallel lanes.
rows.statement: Censuses Omega in steps 269-291: 168 files, 55 containing Omega, 293 total occurrences, of which 44 cluster in a single step (s286) written within one continuous 08-31/09-01 Gita-thread session -- explicitly weighted as ONE independent evidential lineage rather than 44 separate confirmations. Discovers the '269-291' and '231-267' windows are NOT sequential: the last Omega occurrence in the 231-267 window (s266, 2026-08-30 19:54:50) comes AFTER the first Omega occurrence in the 269-291 window (s286, 2026-08-28 23:52:31) -- the later-numbered window begins 1 day 20 hours before the earlier-numbered window ends, proving step numbers do not imply chronological sequence and the two ranges represent parallel, not sequential, lanes.

rows.anchor: §2, §6 · The Ω objects in this interval, with their definitional sources (Ω-A Sañjaya/observation, Ω-B epistemic horizon, Ω-C Ω_K kernel operations, Ω-D integration/element domain) ... Ω-D contains a type error inside one file
rows.statement: Defines four live post-267 Omega senses with verbatim sources: Omega-A 'Sanjaya/observation' (08-31, boxed Omega:W->O, described as 'recovered', citing D285-6); Omega-B 'epistemic horizon' (09-01, boxed Omega=epistemic horizon, explicitly rejecting both Omega=God and Omega=K as 'unjustified architectural identities'); Omega-C 'Omega_K kernel operations' (09-01, boxed K=(K_t,Omega_K) later K=(K_t,Omega_K,I), Omega_K='legitimate/permitted kernel operations'); Omega-D 'integration/element domain' (08-28, appearing as both a measure space and a set of knowledge states). Finds an internal type error within Omega-D's own single source document: one line integrates K_t OVER Omega (making K_t a function on Omega) while another quantifies 'for all K in Omega' (making K an element of Omega) -- K cannot be both; recorded, not repaired.

rows.anchor: §5 · Three-level identity test ... does the horizon document mention Sañjaya? 0 times. does the Sañjaya document mention horizon? 0 times. ... Only ONE pair reaches Level 3: Ω-A × Ω-2. And it reaches it on a byte-identical signature with identical glosses — while citing the wrong source.
rows.statement: Runs a three-level (lexical/mathematical/semantic) identity test across all Omega-sense pairs: finds Omega-A and Omega-2 (from 031) reach full Level-3 SAME-OBJECT status with a byte-identical W->O signature and identical W/O glosses, but Omega-A mis-attributes its provenance to D285-6 rather than 031; Omega-B and Omega-4/7 are DISTINCT-EXPLICIT since the corpus explicitly rejects Omega=K; Omega-B and Omega-A are IDENTITY UNWITNESSED (neither document mentions the other, despite both being definitionally developed); Omega-C and Omega-5 (the s236 operation-set reading) are RELATED with no citation; Omega-C and O_core (s277) are RELATED-IDENTITY-UNWITNESSED; Omega-D's internal type error makes it UNDECIDABLE. Notes the two most-developed Omega senses in this interval (the horizon document and the Sanjaya document) never mention each other at all.

rows.anchor: §7 · C-06 — a local ruling against COMBINING, not a global verdict on Ω ... C-06 adjudicates that two HOMONYMS must not be combined. It does NOT rule that Ω is contradictory. ... the corpus independently reaches the same separation five days later ... CORROBORATIVE, and by §9 this counts as two lineages, not two documents.
rows.statement: Re-examines the corpus's own C-06 'TRUE CONTRADICTION' ruling (Omega=Knowledge Space vs Omega:W->O) verbatim, identifying it addresses specifically Omega-7 vs Omega-2, contradicting the 031 non-identifiability result, is a mathematical+semantic (set vs function) type incompatibility, concerns objects G-22 already classed DISTINCT, and crucially is BOUNDED/conditional ('combining them WOULD make...') rather than a global verdict. Concludes C-06 rules only that two homonyms must not be COMBINED, not that Omega itself is contradictory. Notes the corpus independently reaches the identical separation five days later via Omega-B's explicit rejection of Omega=K, in a different lane, with no citation between the two -- classified as two independent (CORROBORATIVE) lineages rather than a single duplicated finding.

rows.anchor: §12 · Continuity with apparatus loss — the Ω instance, and it is sharper than 026's ... A gap was opened for an object the corpus had DEFINED THREE DAYS EARLIER — and then closed by 'recovering' it. ... apparatus never left the corpus — only the working set — and its re-discovery was recorded as a gap closure.
rows.statement: Traces a precise sequence: 031 defines Omega:W->O boxed (08-28 10:22) -> a 155-file silence -> Omega returns (08-29) -> step_251 cites it unattributed (08-30) -> a NEW GAP is explicitly opened ('Gap 1: (W,Omega) referent layer', 08-31 19:03) -> the same gap is closed hours later by 'recovering' the Sanjaya layer (08-31 19:52, G3->G5) -> a claim that 'the earlier claim that the verification lane lacked an entire observation/referent layer is no longer valid' (08-31 19:40) -> Omega-A's document frames this as resolving 'a structural omission discovered in D285-6' (08-31 20:11). Concludes a gap was opened for an object the corpus had already defined three days earlier, then closed by 'recovering' it -- the corpus does not record this as a loss, it records it as a discovery. Contrasts this with G-12's 026 mechanism ('continuity declared, apparatus not carried'): here, the apparatus never left the corpus at all, only the ACTIVE WORKING SET did, and its re-discovery was mislabeled a gap closure -- two distinct mechanisms in one family, recorded as evidence not generalized into a law.

rows.anchor: The corpus draws the right distinction itself ... 'Observation' being recovered closes the discovery gap, but the executable semantics of Ω and Qualify are not thereby solved. Discovery gap ≠ semantic gap — stated by the corpus, and correct.
rows.statement: Notes approvingly that the corpus itself already draws the correct distinction: recovering Omega's observation-layer definition closes only a DISCOVERY gap, not the underlying SEMANTIC gap (executable semantics of Omega and Qualify remain unsolved) -- endorsed here as a stated-and-correct corpus self-observation, not a finding original to this investigation.

rows.anchor: §8 · Distributed completeness ... Ω-A COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES ... Ω-B GENUINE CORPUS GAP (bounded: Ω-B only) ... Ω-C IDENTITY UNRESOLVED ... Ω-D UNDECIDABLE
rows.statement: Tests distributed completeness per sense: Omega-A is COMPLETE THROUGH MULTIPLE SOURCES (031 supplies the non-identifiability result Omega-A itself omits); Omega-B is a GENUINE CORPUS GAP, explicitly bounded to Omega-B only -- searched across all 55 Omega files plus the whole non-firewalled corpus, no type/domain/codomain is ever given for the 'horizon' concept; Omega-C is IDENTITY UNRESOLVED (operations named but the set never enumerated; s277's O_core enumerates a candidate set with unwitnessed identity); Omega-D is UNDECIDABLE due to its internal type inconsistency.

rows.anchor: §10 · Mathematical audit (Ω-A PROVEN function W→O, Ω-B UNKNOWN never typed, Ω-C PROVEN as a set/UNKNOWN membership, Ω-D contradictory within one file) ... No TYPE-CONSTRAINED value was promoted to PROVEN. §11 · DDD audit ... Four bounded-context candidates, one glyph, zero context mappings.
rows.statement: Mathematical audit: Omega-A is PROVEN as function W->O; Omega-B is UNKNOWN, never typed at all; Omega-C is PROVEN as a finite set but its membership is UNKNOWN; Omega-D is contradictory within one file (measure space and element set simultaneously). Notes no type-constrained value in this audit was ever promoted to PROVEN status. DDD audit assigns each Omega sense to a distinct bounded context (Omega-A observation/referent layer -- map reality to observation; Omega-B epistemic framing/Gita lens -- situate a finite state against a horizon, explicitly Omega!=K and Omega!=God per the corpus; Omega-C kernel -- delimit permitted operations; Omega-D Gita-derived mathematics -- integration domain/state set), concluding four bounded-context candidates share one glyph with zero context mappings between them.

rationale_evidence.statement: Six negative constraints (C1-C6), assessed as the Gita's genuine kernel-relevant yield: C1 Knower != Knowledge != Knowledge Space (Ch5 sec15, Ch6 sec20) -- kills three identity mappings (Atma, Paramatma, Krishna) at once; C2 the kernel is a mind-like functional analogy, not an identity (Ch6) -- forbids 'the kernel is the mind'; C3 Moksha != infinite knowledge (Ch6) -- kills the completeness reading; C4 knowledge REVEALS rather than CREATES, so obscured != false != absent (Ch5 sec7) -- equated with MNAR, naming gaps A6/G-60; C5 action decomposes into act/subject/instrument/context/result (Ch5, H-290-1) -- orthogonal to, not a contribution to, the O blocker; C6 Guna needs a scale before it may be opened (Ch7) -- protects the theta gap. Concludes: the Gita's strongest contribution to the kernel is a set of refusals, not a set of objects.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The Gītā is rich in DISTINCTIONS and empty of CARRIERS. A kernel is made of carriers.
rationale_evidence.statement: Systematic explanation for why so little Gita material reaches the kernel: a kernel needs a membership rule, decision procedures, types/signatures, and carriers, whereas the Gita supplies narrative/normative guidance, directions of practice, roles (knower/guide/field/observer), and distinctions -- not carriers. This predicts the observed pattern: both T4 hits are separations (N notin K; W--Omega-->O), the six real contributions are refusals, and every attempt to promote a Gita term to an object (K_atma, K_supreme, Theta_total, Sigma=3 gunas) has been refuted on type-checking.

sources.note: Step 124's distinction between self-verification ('does the system conform?') and self-governance ('what should the system do when it does not conform?'), with the boundary Detection != Authority governing agent autonomy limits.

rows.anchor: Self-verification answers 'Does the system conform?' Self-governance answers 'What should the system do when it does not conform?'
rows.statement: Opens Step 124 by drawing a new distinction: self-verification (conformance detection) must not be collapsed with self-governance (deciding what to do about non-conformance); previews the transition SelfVerification -> Finding -> Governance -> AuthorizedDecision -> Remediation while preserving the boundary Detection ≠ Authority, framed as determining how autonomous KnowledgeOS/AI agents may be versus where human/organizational authority must remain explicit.

rows.anchor: SelfVerification ≠ SelfGovernance
rows.statement: Formalizes the two functions: Self-verification answers 'is the current state conformant?' (Expected->Observed->Verification->Verdict); Self-governance answers 'what authorized response should follow the verdict?' (Finding->Governance->Decision->Action); diagrams the complete separation with the critical boundary Finding =/=> Action automatically.

rows.anchor: whether the deviation is intentional; whether an exception exists; ... who has authority to approve remediation.
rows.statement: Argues the Finding->Action boundary is necessary because a checker finding a violation cannot on its own know whether the deviation is intentional, covered by an exception, safe to change now, in conflict with other in-flight changes, or who holds approval authority — hence Detection ≠ Authorization.

rows.anchor: Remediate / AcceptRisk / Exception / Investigate / FalsePositive / ChangeReferenceArchitecture.
rows.statement: Defines finding-disposition options (Remediate, AcceptRisk, Exception, Investigate, FalsePositive, ChangeReferenceArchitecture) so a finding does not immediately dictate remediation; worked example — a runtime/architecture difference might mean the architecture document is obsolete, so the correct action is UpdateArchitecture rather than ChangeRuntime, hence governance must interpret the finding.

rows.anchor: Architecture=A, Runtime=B. Which is wrong? We cannot infer automatically.
rows.statement: States the 'bidirectional truth problem': given Architecture=A and Runtime=B, four possibilities exist (runtime is drift and architecture is correct; architecture is historical/outdated and runtime is correct; B is an approved exception; both are incomplete) — Difference ≠ Error, requiring Difference -> Assessment -> Disposition rather than automatic inference, and often human/domain authority.

rows.anchor: 'Rollback runtime to A' ... 'Architecture/runtime discrepancy requires classification.'
rows.statement: Worked experiment: an agent proposing 'rollback runtime to A' on detecting Architecture=A vs Runtime=B is potentially premature; the correct response is to flag the discrepancy for classification, verdict PASS; generalizes to UnresolvedDifference ≠ Violation until rule/authority context establishes meaning — the agent must preserve ambiguity rather than resolve it unilaterally.

rows.anchor: FindingClassification = f(Rule, Observation, Authority, Exception, TemporalValidity).
rows.statement: Defines FindingClassification as a function of Rule, Observation, Authority, Exception, TemporalValidity yielding Violation/Exception/ExpectedChange/Unknown; emphasizes UNKNOWN as a valid, indeed preferable, result ('insufficient evidence to determine whether the observed state is non-conformant') over a hallucinated conclusion.

rows.anchor: Decision = (Subject, Choice, Rationale, Authority, EffectiveDate, Scope, Evidence)
rows.statement: Defines the DecisionRequest package (finding, evidence, impact, options, affected systems, recommended action) an agent may prepare without making the decision, agent roles limited to EvidenceCollector/Analyzer/Verifier/RecommendationGenerator (never Authority), and a governed Decision record schema (Subject, Choice, Rationale, Authority, EffectiveDate, Scope, Evidence); worked experiment — agent recommends 'remediate immediately,' decision maker instead grants a 30-day exception, and the authoritative decision (Exception) must not be overwritten by the agent's recommendation, which remains merely a Recommendation.

rows.anchor: D-17: Remediate immediately; D-21: Exception until September, D-21 supersedes D-17
rows.statement: Defines decision supersession (D1 -> D2 means D1=Superseded and agents must use D2 for current governance), worked with D-17/D-21 where D-21 explicitly supersedes D-17 and current authority is D-21, verdict PASS.

rows.anchor: AllowedActions = {ChangeDeployment, UpdateConfiguration}.
rows.statement: Defines remediation-delegation scoping — a decision authorizing 'engineering team shall remediate' does not automatically authorize every action; the allowed action set must be explicit (e.g. {ChangeDeployment, UpdateConfiguration}); worked experiment — a decision authorizing configuration change, with an agent attempting a database migration instead, is OutsideDelegationScope, verdict DENY.

rows.anchor: ActionRisk = Impact × Irreversibility × Scope.
rows.statement: Defines ActionRisk = Impact x Irreversibility x Scope as a conceptual dimension requiring stronger authorization for higher-risk actions; worked experiment contrasting changing markdown documentation vs. a production database schema (the latter requiring substantially stronger governance), verdict PASS.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS → Evidence → Agent Analysis → Recommendation → Governance Decision → Delegation → Agent Execution → Verification
rows.statement: Defines the preferred default workflow for material engineering changes (separation of recommendation and execution): KnowledgeOS -> Evidence -> Agent Analysis -> Recommendation -> Governance Decision -> Delegation -> Agent Execution -> Verification; for low-risk actions the workflow can collapse to Recommendation -> Pre-authorizedAction under an explicit StandingDelegation (an authority defines 'agents may perform action X under conditions Y,' formalized as Condition(Y) ∧ Action(X) -> Allowed), e.g. auto-refreshing a search index; worked experiment — policy allows agents to auto-update non-authoritative metadata (last_seen: ALLOW) but not an architecture decision (DENY).

rows.anchor: Policy + Actor + Action + Resource + Context → Decision.
rows.statement: Frames this as a policy engine — a classic authorization problem (Policy+Actor+Action+Resource+Context->Decision) but connected to KnowledgeOS's semantic governance; the decision may depend on ResourceType, Environment, Risk, DecisionStatus, Delegation, Exception; worked experiment — the same action ('deploy version 2') is ALLOW in staging but REQUIRES APPROVAL in production, i.e. contextual authorization.

rows.anchor: Self-governance = Self-observation + Self-verification + Governed response, not Self-governance = Unlimited autonomy.
rows.statement: States self-governance does not mean self-authority: Self-governance = Self-observation + Self-verification + Governed response, explicitly not Unlimited autonomy; the system can automatically observe, verify, create findings, collect evidence, and prepare recommendations, but authority remains explicitly modeled, giving Automation ⊆ Governance (not Governance ⊆ Automation); diagrams the mature self-governance loop KnowledgeOS State -> Self-Observe -> Self-Verify -> Finding -> Classification -> Governance -> Authorization -> Action -> Verification -> back to KnowledgeOS.

rows.anchor: KOS = (Knowledge, Authority, Observation, Verification, Decision, Action, Evidence).
rows.statement: Formalizes KnowledgeOS as a controlled system, a 7-tuple KOS=(Knowledge, Authority, Observation, Verification, Decision, Action, Evidence) with transitions Knowledge->ExpectedState, ExpectedState<->ObservedState, Difference->Finding, Finding->Governance, Governance->Decision, Decision->AuthorizedAction, Action->Verification, Verification->KnowledgeUpdate.

rows.anchor: No agent may convert its own observation, inference, or recommendation into authoritative organizational knowledge without the required validation and authority.
rows.statement: States the architecture's central AI-governance invariant (boxed) and its enforcement-layer corollary: 'governance must be enforced below the LLM instruction layer' — a prompt instruction like 'don't change architecture decisions' is weak, whereas an architectural enforcement of Agent -/-> AuthoritativeDecision without an authorization path is strong.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS owns authority/knowledge/evidence/governance/lifecycle/traceability; Claude/Codex harness owns agent operating behavior/tool invocation/local workflow/session management/pointers; Agent owns reasoning/analysis/recommendation/delegated execution; Deterministic assurance layer owns machine-verifiable checks/reproducibility/objective evidence.
rows.statement: Assigns a four-way ownership division (KnowledgeOS / Claude-Codex harness / Agent / Deterministic assurance layer) each owning distinct responsibilities, diagrammed as a layered architecture: Governance (Authority/Policy) -> KnowledgeOS (Knowledge/Evidence) -> {AI Agent Layer (Claude/Codex), Assurance Layer (Deterministic)} -> Engineering -> Runtime -> back to Evidence; framed as more precise than 'AI agents connected to a knowledge base.'

rows.anchor: SelfVerification ≠ SelfGovernance; Capability ≠ Authority; Observe→Verify→Find→Govern→Authorize→Act→Verify→Learn
rows.statement: Step 124 verdict: establishes the fundamental autonomy boundary (SelfVerification ≠ SelfGovernance, Capability ≠ Authority) and the mature loop Observe->Verify->Find->Govern->Authorize->Act->Verify->Learn, with the agent participating in but never silently becoming the loop's authority.

aliases: Step 65 Multi-Agent Epistemic Independence and Error Propagation

sources.note: Step 65's formal treatment of multi-agent epistemic independence: the agent dependency graph, multi-dimensional dependency vector, circular-citation detection, the caught self-amplification failure and its correction (I_EpistemicIndependence), causal-vs-surface evidence diversity, contextual agent-capability profiles (AgentCapability≠AgentAuthority), the error-amplification coefficient, and the independent-source-count governance policy; extends epistemic-anchor-redundancy-model's (Step 47) common-mode-failure principle into a full agent/evidence dependency-graph formalism.

rows.anchor: Agreement != IndependentEvidence; agent dependency graph G_A; shared-source discounting (experiments 1-3)
rows.statement: States three agents agreeing (AI_A,AI_B,AI_C -> p) does not automatically justify Confidence(p) up, since agents may share training data, foundation model, retrieval sources, prompt, erroneous source, causal assumption, model family, or generated intermediate knowledge -- Agreement != IndependentEvidence. Worked example: three agents retrieving the same false E_bad all output p=True (3/3 agreement) but effective independent evidence is 1. Experiment 1: three agents with an identical retrieval source produce Support(p)=3 naively but IndependentEvidence(p)=1 correctly, given preserved source dependency -- PASS. Requires AI-artifact provenance (AgentId, ModelVersion, InputEvidence, RetrievalContext, Prompt/Configuration) enabling an agent dependency graph G_A=(V_A,E_A) with V_A={Agents,Models,Evidence,Artifacts} and edges A_i->A_j meaning A_j depends on A_i's output. Experiment 2: a cascading generation chain A1->C1->A2(C1)->C2->A3(C2)->C3->A4(C3)->C4 propagates an initial error through the whole chain, correctly tracked given preserved lineage -- PASS. Experiment 3: four agents sharing the same model M1 producing the same systematic error yields Agreement=High but IndependentSupport not-High -- PASS, giving AgentCount != EvidenceCount, 'one of the most important results of Step 65'.

lineage_claims.quote: This is CommonModeFailure.

rows.anchor: Multi-dimensional dependency vector Dep(Ai,Aj); partial independence and correlated-evidence Bayesian overstatement (experiments 4-5)
rows.statement: Defines Dep(A_i,A_j) = (D_model, D_data, D_source, D_prompt, D_pipeline, D_reasoning) -- 'independent agent' is not binary; two agents can be independent in one dimension (different models) yet dependent in another (same database). Experiment 4: different models but identical evidence yields SupportStrength increasing less than under fully independent evidence -- PASS. But genuine independence remains informative: two conditionally independent observations combine as P(H1|E1,E2)/P(H0|E1,E2) = prior-odds * LR1 * LR2, requiring conditional independence; if E1,E2 are correlated the joint likelihood P(E1,E2|H) is not P(E1|H)*P(E2|H), so naive multiplication overstates evidence. Experiment 5: correlated evidence (Corr(E1,E2)>0) correctly shows NaiveConfidence > CorrectConfidence -- PASS. Recommends preserving a structured Consensus=(Agents, Dependencies, EvidenceSources, Models, AgreementPattern) rather than a bare vote fraction, letting downstream contexts interpret agreement.

rows.anchor: Circular citation / epistemic circularity detected; feedback loop != justification cycle (requires temporal progress)
rows.statement: Experiment 6: A1->C1, A2(C1)->C2, A1(C2)->C3 creates many apparent supporting artifacts all originating from the same initial assertion -- EpistemicCircularity, detected by inspecting the provenance graph G_P for cycles (C1 leadsto C1) -- PASS. Distinguishes legitimate feedback (Prediction->Outcome->Learning->NewPrediction, valid because time advances) from a problematic static justification cycle (Claim->DerivedClaim->Support->OriginalClaim, where evidence ultimately depends on the claim itself) -- Cycle is not automatically an error; the discriminator is TemporalProgress.

rows.anchor: Self-reinforcing knowledge amplification: the step's one deliberate FAILURE, corrected via mandatory DerivedFrom tracking and I_EpistemicIndependence
rows.statement: Experiment 7: AI generates p, KnowledgeOS stores it; later AI retrieves p and generates p' citing it; another process then treats p' as independent support for p -- artificial evidence amplification -- FAILURE DETECTED, 'an important failure'. Architectural correction: generated knowledge must preserve DerivedFrom so p' is recognized as dependent on p and never automatically counted as independent evidence, yielding the new invariant I_EpistemicIndependence: derived artifacts cannot be counted as independent evidence of their own ancestry -- 'a very strong KnowledgeOS invariant'. Experiment 8: a false claim entering once and repeated by ten agents (11 apparent agreements) is correctly discounted to an effective independent-source count of ~1 once provenance (10<-1) is applied -- PASS.
invariants: I_EpistemicIndependence: a derived artifact can never count as independent evidence of its own ancestry

experiment.hypothesis: Untracked derivation chains allow a single false claim to fraudulently accumulate apparent independent confirmations as it is repeated/cited by other agents.
experiment.setup: A generated claim p stored, then re-derived (p') citing p, then p' mistakenly treated as independent support for p (experiment 7); separately, ten agents repeating one false claim (experiment 8).
experiment.assumptions: No DerivedFrom tracking was initially assumed in the failing case.
experiment.inputs: The self-citation chain and the ten-agent repetition scenario.
experiment.method: Trace whether the system's evidence count reflects true independent sources or merely repetition count.
experiment.result: Without DerivedFrom tracking, evidence count is falsely amplified (FAILURE DETECTED); with DerivedFrom/provenance tracking, the effective independent count correctly stays near 1 (PASS).
experiment.interpretation: AI-generated knowledge can recursively amplify itself unless derivation lineage is mandatorily tracked -- the step's central discovered hazard.
experiment.limitations: Manual scenario construction, not automated/exhaustive adversarial search.
experiment.conclusion: Experiment 7 FAILURE DETECTED (corrected); experiment 8 PASS after correction.

rows.anchor: Evidence-path diversity vs causal independence; SurfaceDiversity != CausalIndependence; common-source graph
rows.statement: Defines PathDiversity(p) (support from database, sensor, human observation, independent model, external experiment) as reducing but not guaranteeing against common-mode risk. Experiment 9: five agreeing agents using three independent data sources, two independent models, and separate retrieval pipelines have their dependency structure recorded -- PASS. Warns different-looking sources may still share a hidden common dependency (SurfaceDiversity != CausalIndependence); represents this as a common-source graph S0->S1, S0->S2 making S1,S2 non-independent despite being separate documents. Experiment 10: two apparently independent documents tracing to the same original report correctly yield IndependentEvidenceCount=1 (or appropriately discounted) -- PASS.

rows.anchor: AI-generated/simulated artifacts never promoted to ObservedFact; provenance-origin taxonomy; Observation->Inference->Prediction->Decision directionality (Prediction⇏Observation)
rows.statement: Experiment 11: an AI-generated explanation later promoted to ObservedFact is Rejected -- must instead be labeled AI GeneratedArtifact. Lists an evidence-origin taxonomy (Human, Instrument, ExternalSystem, AI, Simulation, Inference) with distinct epistemic semantics. Experiment 12: a simulation's Y=10 stored as Observed(Y=10) is Rejected -- it is SimulatedOutcome, evidentiary force depending on model validity; likewise SyntheticData != ObservedData. Builds the directional hierarchy Observation -> Inference -> Prediction -> Decision, which 'must not be reversed accidentally': Prediction ⇏ Observation. Experiment 13: a model's prediction of tomorrow's failure cannot be stored as FailureOccurred before tomorrow arrives -- PASS; only actual observation (ObservedFailure=True) permits evaluating the prediction, giving Prediction -> Outcome -> Evaluation.
invariants: Prediction ⇏ Observation; a forecast is never stored as an already-occurred fact

rows.anchor: Contextual/task-scoped agent quality; AgentCapability != AgentAuthority; scoped TrustProfile
rows.statement: For agent A_i, accumulates Predictions(A_i) and Outcomes(A_i) to estimate Accuracy, Calibration, BrierScore (or domain-specific metrics), but notes agent quality is contextual: Quality(A_i,Task) is more meaningful than Quality(A_i) (excellent at code review, poor at causal inference). Experiment 14: 95% accuracy in domain D1 automatically trusted in D2 is UnsupportedTransfer -- PASS. Defines Capability(A) = {Domain, Task, Model, Performance, Calibration, ValidityPeriod} as a governed artifact. States AgentCapability != AgentAuthority (mirroring Decision != Authorization): even a highly accurate agent lacks automatic authority for consequential actions. Experiment 15: a 99%-accurate agent attempting a restricted action is denied authorization by governance -- PASS. Proposes scoped trust TrustProfile(A,Domain,Task,Time) instead of a global TrustedAgent=True.

lineage_claims.quote: This mirrors: Decision ≠ Authorization.

rows.anchor: Hidden dependency exposure and common-ancestor discounting; formal Anc(A)/Common(A,B) dependency sets
rows.statement: Experiment 16: an apparently independent Agent_B is revealed by lineage inspection to depend on Agent_A's output via KnowledgeOS -- PASS if lineage exposes the dependency. Poses Independent(A,B|p)? as a graph property examined via dependency ancestors: defines Anc(A) as A's upstream artifact set, Common(A,B) = Anc(A) intersect Anc(B); large common dependency does not mathematically prove correlation but is evidence against assuming independence. Experiment 17: Common(A,B)={E0} correctly shows IndependentSupport is not automatically doubled -- PASS, enabling an EvidenceDependencyGraph to prevent artificial confidence inflation, 'substantially more rigorous than ordinary multi-agent consensus'.

rows.anchor: Multi-agent epistemic state M(p); consensus as a derived (not primary) property; untraceable agreement != independent confirmation
rows.statement: Defines M(p) = (Claims, Evidence, Agents, Models, Dependencies, Agreement, Conflict) as the multi-agent epistemic state of a proposition; Consensus(p) should be calculated from underlying artifacts and never itself become primary evidence. Experiment 18: a stored 'p=true, votes=17' with no evidence lineage correctly yields ConsensusEvidenceQuality=Unknown -- PASS, giving the principle: untraceable agreement is not equivalent to independent confirmation.
invariants: untraceable agreement is never equivalent to independent confirmation

rows.anchor: Error-amplification coefficient λ; positive-feedback false-claim entrenchment; independent-source-count governance policy (N_independent≥k)
rows.statement: Describes a positive-feedback risk: FalseClaim -> AI -> Knowledge -> AI -> MoreKnowledge if downstream agents blindly trust upstream AI outputs. Defines lambda = ExpectedDownstreamFalseSupport / InitialFalseSupport; lambda>1 means the system amplifies unsupported claims (exact metric requires a concrete stochastic model, but the architectural phenomenon is clear). Experiment 19: injecting one false claim and letting ten agents consume/reproduce it shows IndependentSupport does not increase proportionally to reproduction count -- PASS, requiring SourceLineage, DerivedFrom, and potentially EvidenceFreshness/IndependentSourceRequirement to stop amplification. For high-consequence claims, defines an independent-source-count policy N_independent >= k (e.g. k=2, a policy-determined value). Experiment 20: N_independent=1 (despite AgentAgreement=12/12) fails a k>=2 policy and the claim cannot be promoted -- PASS, 'mathematically separating AgentConsensus from EvidenceIndependence -- precisely what a governed AI knowledge architecture needs'.

rows.anchor: Four new invariants: I_AI-Provenance, I_EvidenceNonAmplification, I_NoCircularJustification, I_AgentScope
rows.statement: Adds four named invariants: I_AI-Provenance (every AI-generated artifact retains its model, input, and dependency lineage); I_EvidenceNonAmplification (derived copies of the same epistemic source cannot automatically increase independent evidence); I_NoCircularJustification (a claim cannot serve as independent justification for an ancestor claim); I_AgentScope (agent competence is task/domain/context specific).

rows.anchor: AIOutput≠Evidence≠Fact≠Truth epistemic firewall; nine-conjunct Correctness(KOS); explicit non-overclaiming methodological statement; verdict PASS WITH ONE CRITICAL CORRECTION
rows.statement: States the deeper epistemic firewall AIOutput != Evidence != Fact != Truth, with the required path AIOutput -> CandidateArtifact -> Evaluation -> KnowledgeStatus, 'should be fundamental to KnowledgeOS'. Extends the correctness equation to C_KOS = Safety ∧ Liveness ∧ Compositionality ∧ Concurrency ∧ EpistemicIntegrity ∧ DecisionIntegrity ∧ CausalIntegrity ∧ ModelValidity ∧ MultiAgent. Declares STEP 65 -- PASS WITH ONE CRITICAL CORRECTION: multi-agent reasoning is handled correctly only if provenance and dependency are first-class; the discovered failure mode is that AI-generated knowledge can recursively amplify itself, corrected via DerivedFrom + DependencyGraph + IndependentEvidenceAccounting. Makes an explicit methodological statement: 'I would not yet say we have mathematically proven that KnowledgeOS is correct... the architecture has survived a growing family of explicit mathematical counterexample tests', with failures converted into architectural invariants -- 'exactly how a serious architecture experiment should proceed'.

lineage_claims.quote: C_KOS = S ∧ L ∧ Comp ∧ Conc ∧ Epi ∧ Dec ∧ Causal ∧ Model ∧ MultiAgent.

rows.anchor: Transitive provenance and the multi-agent evidence-independence problem re-confirmed
rows.statement: Formalizes transitive provenance: Anc(B) superset-of Anc(A) and Anc(C) superset-of Anc(B) implies Anc(C) superset-of Anc(A). Experiment 7: tracing which observation ultimately influenced a decision (Observation->Evidence->Inference->Decision) is Traceable -- PASS. Re-derives the evidence-independence problem: E2=f(E1) means both cannot be counted as independent. Experiment 8: one source E1 summarized by five AI agents yielding an apparent count of 6 independent sources instead correctly triggers DependencyDetected/EffectiveEvidenceCount~=1 -- PASS. Restates EvidenceCount != IndependentEvidenceCount as I_EvidenceIndependence (correlated or derived evidence must not be counted as independent confirmation) -- 'a statistical invariant implemented through provenance'. Experiment 9: ten agents deriving the same claim from one document reporting Consensus=10/10 correctly triggers SharedSourceDependency -- PASS.
invariants: I_EvidenceIndependence: correlated or derived evidence must not be counted as independent confirmation

lineage_claims.quote: EvidenceCount ≠ IndependentEvidenceCount. This is an important KnowledgeOS invariant.

rows.anchor: Agent composition via typed artifacts and contracts, not implicit trust; survives heterogeneous models and model replacement
rows.statement: Models an agent pipeline A(Hypothesis)->B(evaluates)->C(statistics)->D(recommendation), stating agents do not need to trust one another -- they trust typed artifacts and contracts. Experiment 16: Agent A asserting H1 and Agent B asserting not-H1 yields Conflict rather than one agent overwriting the other -- PASS, giving the principle: agents communicate through governed artifacts, not implicit trust. Experiment 17: Agent A and B implemented with different LLMs, both producing valid typed artifacts, yields WorkflowCompatible -- PASS, since semantic compatibility comes from KnowledgeOS contracts, not shared internal cognition, letting the platform survive Model_A->Model_B->Model_C changes over time with stable knowledge semantics. Experiment 18: replacing the AI model such that an old claim loses its model provenance yields ProvenanceViolation -- PASS, requiring ModelVersion to remain part of provenance.

rows.anchor: Three-level belief hierarchy: agent belief B_A(p), shared knowledge K(p), organizationally accepted knowledge K_org(p); private belief must not auto-promote (Experiment 5); disagreement preserved not collapsed (Experiment 6)
rows.statement: Introduces agent Belief(A) as agent-scoped epistemic state; two agents may have Belief(A)≠Belief(B) without the organizational knowledge base needing two incompatible 'truths' -- beliefs are represented as agent-scoped claims until evaluated. Gives three distinct levels: agent belief B_A(p), shared knowledge K(p), organizationally accepted knowledge K_org(p) -- 'not identical'. Experiment 5: agent A internally estimates P(p)=0.8 and the system immediately promotes this to OrganizationalKnowledge(p)=Verified -- expected Rejected -- PASS. Experiment 6: Agent A P_A(p)=0.8 vs Agent B P_B(p)=0.3 -- expected BeliefDisagreement, and KnowledgeOS should preserve both analytical positions while determining whether a shared organizational conclusion exists -- PASS.

lineage_claims.quote: We already established: IndependentEvidence ≠ NumberOfAgents.

rows.anchor: Majority vote is not epistemic correctness: 9:1 agent agreement on a shared bad source does not establish truth (Experiment 7); governed CandidateKnowledge->AcceptedKnowledge promotion transition with explicit preconditions (Experiment 8)
rows.statement: States that a naive MajorityVote answer to 'when can beliefs become organizational knowledge' fails: majority agreement is not necessarily epistemic correctness (ten agents can derive the same conclusion from the same bad source). Experiment 7: nine agents use the same incorrect source; one agent has independently verified contradictory evidence -- expected 9:1 does not automatically establish truth -- PASS. Requires a governed transition Promote: Candidate -> Accepted with preconditions P_1 AND P_2 AND ... AND P_n depending on Evidence, Validation, Authority, Independence, Context, Policy -- explicitly contrasted with an unstructured 'status = approved' field. Experiment 8: candidate claim with valid provenance, sufficient evidence, required authority, and no unresolved contradiction -- expected PromotionAllowed -- PASS.

rows.anchor: ObservationQuality distinct from ObservationQuantity; correlated observations must not be counted as independent confirmation (Experiments 21-23)
rows.statement: Distinguishes ObservationQuality (accuracy, freshness, completeness, provenance, independence, resolution) from ObservationQuantity. Experiment 21: 100 telemetry signals all derive from the same underlying sensor, system claims EvidenceStrength=100x -- expected Rejected -- PASS, 'echoes our earlier independence analysis'. States correlated observations O_1,O_2,O_3 from one source should not be treated as three independent pieces of evidence, particularly important for AI systems that may repeatedly summarize the same source. Experiment 22: five agents independently repeat the same repository finding, all using the same repository snapshot -- expected EvidenceCount=1 in the relevant independence sense, not five independent confirmations -- PASS. Requires an observation-provenance graph (O_1<-Source_X, O_2<-Source_X) to identify CommonSource(O_1,O_2), preventing artificial confidence inflation. Experiment 23: ten agents produce identical conclusions from one document while one independently measured runtime signal contradicts them -- expected SourceIndependence must be considered -- PASS.

lineage_claims.quote: This echoes our earlier independence analysis.
